description: Matrix products with transpose options and selectable multiplication methods.
source:
program demo_matrix_products
   use kinds, only: rk
   use formatmul, only: matmul
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   character(2), parameter :: methods(*) = ['m1', 'm2', 'm3', 'm4']
   real(rk) :: a(2, 3), b(3, 2), expected(2, 2), c(2, 2), vector(3), product(2)
   integer :: i, j, k, method

   a = reshape([1.0_rk, 4.0_rk, 2.0_rk, 5.0_rk, 3.0_rk, 6.0_rk], shape(a))
   b = reshape([7.0_rk, 9.0_rk, 11.0_rk, 8.0_rk, 10.0_rk, 12.0_rk], shape(b))
   ! An independent scalar-loop reference, rather than this module's MATMUL.
   expected = 0.0_rk
   do j = 1, 2
      do i = 1, 2
         do k = 1, 3
            expected(i, j) = expected(i, j) + a(i, k)*b(k, j)
         end do
      end do
   end do
   vector = [1.0_rk, -2.0_rk, 3.0_rk]
   ! At this pinned version, pass BOTH transpose flags when specifying either.
   ! A single explicitly false flag incorrectly selects a transposed branch.
   do method = 1, size(methods)
      c = matmul(a, b, option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      c = matmul(a, b, transA=.false., transB=.false., option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      c = matmul(transpose(a), b, transA=.true., transB=.false., option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      c = matmul(a, transpose(b), transA=.false., transB=.true., option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      c = matmul(transpose(a), transpose(b), transA=.true., transB=.true., option=methods(method))
      call check(c)
      product = matmul(a, vector, option=methods(method))
      if (any(.not. ieee_is_finite(product))) error stop 'nonfinite vector product'
      if (maxval(abs(product - [6.0_rk, 12.0_rk])) > 1.e-10_rk) error stop 'matrix-vector product'
      print '(a)', methods(method)//': rectangular, transposed and matrix-vector products checked'
   end do
   print '(a)', 'A times B:'
   do i = 1, 2
      print '(2f12.3)', expected(i, :)
   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS formatmul'
contains
   subroutine check(matrix)
      real(rk), intent(in) :: matrix(:, :)
      if (any(.not. ieee_is_finite(matrix))) error stop 'nonfinite matrix product'
      if (maxval(abs(matrix - expected)) > 1.e-10_rk) error stop 'matrix product'
   end subroutine check
end program demo_matrix_products

gams_procedures.notes: Methods m1 through m4 are checked for rectangular matrix multiplication, all transpose combinations and a matrix-vector product. The demo is single-process and does not validate every implementation or coarray branch. At this pin a single explicitly false transpose flag is misrouted; the demo passes both flags whenever either is specified. Separate failing probes and the successful workaround are retained.

description: Fixed-width binary-string arithmetic, shifts and logical operations.
source:
program demo_binary_strings
   use bstrith, only: add, sub, xor, not, shift_l, shift_r
   implicit none
   character(8) :: bits, expected
   integer :: i, amount

   ! Exhaustively check every eight-bit value, including carry and wraparound.
   do i = 0, 255
      write(bits, '(b8.8)') i
      write(expected, '(b8.8)') modulo(i + 1, 256)
      if (add(bits, '00000001') /= expected) error stop 'addition'
      if (sub(expected, '00000001') /= bits) error stop 'subtraction round trip'
      if (xor(bits, not(bits)) /= '11111111') error stop 'complement and xor'
      do amount = 1, 7
         write(expected, '(b8.8)') iand(ishft(i, amount), 255)
         if (shift_l(bits, amount) /= expected) error stop 'left shift'
         write(expected, '(b8.8)') ishft(i, -amount)
         if (shift_r(bits, amount) /= expected) error stop 'right shift'
      end do
   end do
   print '(a)', '11111111 + 00000001 = '//add('11111111', '00000001')
   print '(a)', '00000000 - 00000001 = '//sub('00000000', '00000001')
   print '(a)', 'Left shift 00010101 by 2: '//shift_l('00010101', 2)
   print '(a)', 'All 256 eight-bit values passed arithmetic, logical and shift checks.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS bstrith'
end program demo_binary_strings

gams_procedures.notes: Fixed-width binary-string addition, subtraction, shifts and logical operations. The driver checks every eight-bit value, including carry and wraparound. This is not unlimited arbitrary-precision arithmetic. Dedicated N2 driver: 5120 exact comparisons against independent native integer references: shifts/complement/XOR over all 8-bit values, 8-bit increment/decrement, and all ordered pairs of 4-bit addition/subtraction operands. This N2 driver does not mark the separate A1 mapping verified.

description: Finite-difference models of Fourier and Cattaneo heat transport.
source:
program demo_fourier_diffusion
   use constants, only: real12, int12, pi
   use globe_data, only: ra
   use solver, only: SRSin, linbcg
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 31, steps = 50
   real(real12), parameter :: h = 1.0_real12/(n + 1), dt = 0.001_real12, r = dt/h**2
   real(real12) :: matrix(n, n), position(n), temperature(n), rhs(n), expected(n)
   real(real12) :: error, residual, discrete_factor, pde_error
   integer(int12) :: iterations
   integer :: i, step

   ! u_t = u_xx on [0,1], zero endpoint temperatures, u(x,0) = sin(pi*x).
   ! Use HeatFlow's sparse solver for backward-Euler steps of this independent
   ! one-dimensional discretization, rather than its full Cattaneo application.
   matrix = 0.0_real12
   do i = 1, n
      position(i) = i*h
      matrix(i, i) = 1.0_real12 + 2.0_real12*r
      if (i > 1) matrix(i, i - 1) = -r
      if (i < n) matrix(i, i + 1) = -r
   end do
   call SRSin(matrix, 0.0_real12, ra)
   temperature = sin(pi*position)
   do step = 1, steps
      rhs = temperature
      temperature = 0.0_real12
      iterations = 0_int12
      call linbcg(rhs, temperature, 1_int12, 1.e-11_real12, 100_int12, iterations, error)
      if (any(.not. ieee_is_finite(temperature))) error stop 'nonfinite temperature'
      residual = maxval(abs(matmul(matrix, temperature) - rhs))
      if (residual > 1.e-10_real12) error stop 'linear system residual'
   end do
   discrete_factor = (1.0_real12 + 4.0_real12*r*sin(pi*h/2.0_real12)**2)**(-steps)
   expected = discrete_factor*sin(pi*position)
   if (maxval(abs(temperature - expected)) > 1.e-9_real12) error stop 'discrete diffusion solution'
   expected = exp(-pi*pi*steps*dt)*sin(pi*position)
   pde_error = maxval(abs(temperature - expected))
   if (pde_error > 0.004_real12) error stop 'continuous solution accuracy'
   print '(a, f7.3)', 'Time: ', steps*dt

description: High-resolution WENO reconstruction and TVD integration for conservation equations.
source:
module advection_problem
   use hrweno_kinds, only: rk
   use hrweno_weno, only: weno
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 64
   real(rk), parameter :: dx = 1.0_rk/n
   type(weno) :: reconstruction
contains
   subroutine rhs(t, u, du)
      real(rk), intent(in) :: t, u(:)
      real(rk), intent(out) :: du(:)
      real(rk) :: extended(n+6), left(n+6), right(n+6), flux(0:n)
      ! Three periodic ghost cells at either end of the physical domain.
      extended(4:n+3) = u
      extended(1:3) = u(n-2:n)
      extended(n+4:n+6) = u(1:3)
      call reconstruction%reconstruct(extended, left, right)
      ! Unit positive advection speed: upwind flux is the right cell value.
      flux(0) = right(3)
      flux(1:n) = right(4:n+3)
      flux(n) = flux(0)
      du = -(flux(1:n)-flux(0:n-1))/dx
   end subroutine rhs
end module advection_problem

program periodic_advection
   use advection_problem
   use hrweno_tvdode, only: rktvd
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(rktvd) :: solver
   real(rk), parameter :: pi = acos(-1.0_rk), dt = 0.002_rk
   real(rk) :: x(n), u(n), exact(n), time, factor, error, mass
   integer :: i
   x = [( (i-0.5_rk)*dx, i=1,n )]
   ! Exact cell averages, rather than point samples.
   factor = sin(pi*dx)/(pi*dx)
   u = 1 + 0.2_rk*factor*sin(2*pi*x)
   reconstruction = weno(ncells=n+6, k=3, eps=1.e-6_rk)
   solver = rktvd(rhs, n, order=3)
   time = 0
   call solver%integrate(u, time, 0.25_rk, dt)
   exact = 1 + 0.2_rk*factor*sin(2*pi*(x-time))
   error = maxval(abs(u-exact))
   mass = sum(u)*dx
   if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(u))) error stop 'Nonfinite solution'
   if (abs(time-0.25_rk)>1.e-12_rk .or. error>1.e-4_rk) error stop 'Advection error'
   if (abs(mass-1.0_rk)>1.e-11_rk) error stop 'Mass conservation error'
   print '(a,f8.3)', 'Periodic advection time: ', time
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum cell-average error: ', error
   print '(a,f16.12)', 'Conserved mass: ', mass
   print *, 'PASS hrweno'
end program periodic_advection

description: Reduce the number of polyline points using geometric simplification algorithms.
source:
program simplify_curve
   ! This pin has upstream limitations in radial_distance and in repeated
   ! perpendicular_distance calls. This example makes one perpendicular call.
   ! Reproducers: docs/fpm-candidates/fortran-simplify in the playground repo.
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp => real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use simplify, only: perpendicular_distance
   use pyplot_module, only: pyplot
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n=251
   real(dp), parameter :: pi=acos(-1.0_dp), tolerance=0.005_dp
   real(dp) :: curve(n,2), fraction, interpolated, max_error
   real(dp), allocatable :: reduced(:,:)
   type(pyplot) :: plot
   integer :: i, j, status
   curve(:,1) = [(2*pi*(i-1)/(n-1),i=1,n)]
   curve(:,2) = sin(curve(:,1))
   ! One pass of perpendicular-distance simplification.
   reduced = perpendicular_distance(curve, tolerance)
   if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(reduced))) error stop 'Nonfinite coordinates'
   if (size(reduced,1)>=n .or. size(reduced,1)<2) error stop 'Unexpected point count'
   if (any(reduced(1,:)/=curve(1,:))) error stop 'First endpoint lost'
   if (any(reduced(size(reduced,1),:)/=curve(n,:))) error stop 'Last endpoint lost'
   max_error = 0
   j = 1
   do i=1,n
      do while (j<size(reduced,1)-1)
         if (curve(i,1)<=reduced(j+1,1)) exit
         j = j+1
      end do
      fraction = (curve(i,1)-reduced(j,1))/(reduced(j+1,1)-reduced(j,1))
      interpolated = (1-fraction)*reduced(j,2)+fraction*reduced(j+1,2)
      max_error = max(max_error,abs(curve(i,2)-interpolated))
   end do
   if (max_error>tolerance) error stop 'Independent interpolation check failed'
   print '(a,i0,a,i0)', 'Sine curve: ',n,' points reduced to ',size(reduced,1)
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum vertical interpolation error: ',max_error
   call plot%initialize(grid=.true.,legend=.true.,title='Polyline simplification', &
      xlabel='x',ylabel='sin(x)',use_oo_api=.true.)
   call plot%add_plot(curve(:,1),curve(:,2),label='Original',linestyle='b-')
   call plot%add_plot(reduced(:,1),reduced(:,2),label='Simplified',linestyle='r.')
   call plot%savefig('simplified.png',istat=status)
   if (status/=0) error stop 'Plot generation failed'
   print *, 'PASS fortran-simplify'
end program simplify_curve

gams_procedures.notes: Polyline simplification. The main checks one call of perpendicular-distance reduction against endpoints and an independent interpolation bound, and plots the original and reduced curves. Separate GNU 16 probes confirm incorrect radial-distance filtering and lost endpoints on consecutive perpendicular-distance calls at this pin; see the retained reproducers. The single-call example does not fix those upstream limitations.

   call z([resistance,0.0_dp,0.0_dp], omega, resistor, 'R', status, message)

      print *, message
      error stop 'Resistor calculation failed'
   end if

program dense_inference
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real32
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use athena, only: full_layer_type, array_type
   implicit none
   type(full_layer_type) :: layer
   type(array_type) :: input(1,1)
   real(real32) :: weights(2,3), bias(2), x(3,1), reference(2)
   ! Deterministic inference: no data files, training loop or random weights.
   weights = reshape([1.,-1.,2.,0.5,-0.5,3.], [2,3])
   bias = [0.25_real32,-0.75_real32]
   x(:,1) = [1.,2.,-1.]
   layer = full_layer_type(num_inputs=3, num_outputs=2, activation='tanh')
   layer%params(1)%val(:,1) = reshape(weights,[6])
   layer%params(2)%val(:,1) = bias
   call input(1,1)%allocate(source=x)
   call layer%forward(input)
   reference = tanh(matmul(weights,x(:,1))+bias)
   if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(layer%output(1,1)%val))) error stop 'Nonfinite output'
   if (maxval(abs(layer%output(1,1)%val(:,1)-reference))>2.e-6_real32) &
      error stop 'Dense layer does not match direct Fortran calculation'
   print '(a)', 'Fully connected layer: 3 inputs, 2 outputs, tanh activation'
   print '(a,2f12.7)', 'Athena inference: ', layer%output(1,1)%val(:,1)
   print '(a,2f12.7)', 'Direct reference: ', reference
   print *, 'PASS athena'
end program dense_inference

source:
program morton_neighbor
   use orbs
   implicit none
   type(operable_bitset) :: key, neighbor, one, mask_x, mask_y, expected
   character(4) :: text, expected_text
   integer :: code, x, y, next_x, next_code
   mask_x = operable_bitset('1010')
   mask_y = operable_bitset('0101')
   ! A 4-bit Morton key interleaves two bits of x with two bits of y.
   do code=0,15
      write(text,'(b4.4)') code
      key = operable_bitset(text)
      one = orbs_one(mold=key)
      neighbor = (((key.or.mask_y)+one).and.mask_x).or.(key.and.mask_y)
      ! Independent reference using ordinary integer bit operations.
      x = ibits(code,1,1) + 2*ibits(code,3,1)
      y = ibits(code,0,1) + 2*ibits(code,2,1)
      next_x = modulo(x+1,4)
      next_code = 2*ibits(next_x,0,1) + 8*ibits(next_x,1,1) &
         + ibits(y,0,1) + 4*ibits(y,1,1)
      write(expected_text,'(b4.4)') next_code
      expected = operable_bitset(expected_text)
      if (neighbor/=expected) error stop 'Morton neighbor mismatch'
      if (code==3) print '(a)', 'Morton key '//text//' -> x neighbor '//expected_text
   end do
   print '(a)', 'Verified all 16 cells, including periodic wraparound.'
   print *, 'PASS orbs'
end program morton_neighbor

gams_procedures.notes: Fixed-width bitset arithmetic and logical operations. The main computes an x neighbor for every cell of a two-dimensional 4-by-4 Morton grid, checking all sixteen results and wraparound against independent intrinsic integer operations.

description: Educational growable real arrays with spare capacity to reduce reallocations.
source:
program growable_matrix
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use rearrayfx, only: rearray_real64_r2
   implicit none
   integer :: i
   block
      type(rearray_real64_r2) :: matrix
      real(real64) :: expected(2,6)
      matrix%overprov = 2.0
      expected = reshape([(real(i,real64),i=1,12)], [2,6])
      call matrix%allocate([2,2])
      matrix%view = expected(:,1:2)
      ! This growth fits in the spare capacity; existing elements survive.
      call matrix%allocate([2,3])
      if (any(matrix%view(:,1:2)/=expected(:,1:2))) error stop 'First growth lost data'
      matrix%view(:,3) = expected(:,3)
      ! This growth needs a new backing allocation.
      call matrix%allocate([2,6])
      if (any(matrix%view(:,1:3)/=expected(:,1:3))) error stop 'Reallocation lost data'
      matrix%view(:,4:6) = expected(:,4:6)
      print '(a,2i4)', 'Final matrix shape: ', shape(matrix%view)
      print '(a,f8.1)', 'Sum of preserved and appended elements: ', sum(matrix%view)
      if (any(matrix%view/=expected)) error stop 'Matrix data mismatch'
      call matrix%allocate([2,1])
      if (any(matrix%view/=expected(:,1:1))) error stop 'Shrink lost data'
      matrix = expected(:,1:2)
      if (any(matrix%view/=expected(:,1:2))) error stop 'Array assignment failed'
   end block
   print *, 'PASS rearrayfx'
end program growable_matrix

gams_procedures.notes: Growable real rank-two arrays backed by spare capacity. The main checks data preservation across growth within spare capacity, reallocation, shrinking and plain-array assignment. This proof of concept is not a general-purpose container or a test of copying between container instances.

description: AMOS interfaces for complex-argument, noninteger-order Bessel and related functions.
source:
program complex_bessel_functions
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp=>real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use amos, only: f90_zbesj, f90_zbesi, f90_zbesk
   implicit none
   complex(dp) :: z, j(1), modified_i(1), modified_k(1), reference_j, reference_i, reference_k
   real(dp), parameter :: nu=0.3_dp, pi=acos(-1.0_dp)
   integer :: underflows, status
   z=cmplx(1.0_dp,0.5_dp,dp)
   call f90_zbesj(z,nu,1,1,j,underflows,status)
   if(status/=0 .or. underflows/=0) error stop 'J calculation failed'
   call f90_zbesi(z,nu,1,1,modified_i,underflows,status)
   if(status/=0 .or. underflows/=0) error stop 'I calculation failed'
   call f90_zbesk(z,0.5_dp,1,1,modified_k,underflows,status)
   if(status/=0 .or. underflows/=0) error stop 'K calculation failed'
   reference_j=power_series(z,nu,-1)
   reference_i=power_series(z,nu,1)
   reference_k=sqrt(pi/(2*z))*exp(-z)
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite([real(j(1)),aimag(j(1)),real(modified_i(1)),aimag(modified_i(1)), &
      real(modified_k(1)),aimag(modified_k(1))]))) error stop 'Nonfinite result'
   if(abs(j(1)-reference_j)>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'J disagrees with independent series'
   if(abs(modified_i(1)-reference_i)>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'I disagrees with independent series'
   if(abs(modified_k(1)-reference_k)>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'K half-order identity failed'
   print '(a)', 'Complex argument z = 1 + 0.5i; noninteger orders'
   print '(a,2f18.12)', 'J_0.3(z), real/imag: ',real(j(1)),aimag(j(1))
   print '(a,2f18.12)', 'I_0.3(z), real/imag: ',real(modified_i(1)),aimag(modified_i(1))
   print '(a,2f18.12)', 'K_0.5(z), real/imag: ',real(modified_k(1)),aimag(modified_k(1))
   print *, 'PASS amosf90'
contains
   function power_series(x,order,sign_factor) result(value)
      complex(dp),intent(in)::x
      real(dp),intent(in)::order
      integer,intent(in)::sign_factor
      complex(dp)::value,term,total
      integer::k
      term=cmplx(1.0_dp,0.0_dp,dp);total=term
      do k=1,60
         term=term*(sign_factor*x*x/4)/(k*(order+k))
         total=total+term
         if(abs(term)<epsilon(1.0_dp)*abs(total)) exit
      end do

program checked_lapack_operations
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp=>real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use linalg_fortran, only: linalg
   implicit none
   real(dp) :: a(3,3), inverse(3,3), vectors(3,3), eigenvalues(3), identity(3,3), determinant
   integer :: i
   a=reshape([2._dp,1._dp,0._dp,1._dp,2._dp,1._dp,0._dp,1._dp,2._dp],[3,3])
   identity=0
   do i=1,3
      identity(i,i)=1
   end do
   inverse=a
   if(.not.linalg%inv(inverse)) error stop 'Inverse failed'
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(inverse))) error stop 'Nonfinite inverse'
   if(maxval(abs(matmul(a,inverse)-identity))>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'Inverse residual'
   determinant=linalg%det(a)
   if(abs(determinant-4._dp)>1.e-11_dp) error stop 'Determinant mismatch'
   vectors=a
   call linalg%eigh(vectors,eigenvalues)
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(eigenvalues))) error stop 'Nonfinite eigenvalues'
   if(maxval(abs(eigenvalues-[2-sqrt(2._dp),2._dp,2+sqrt(2._dp)]))>1.e-11_dp) &
      error stop 'Eigenvalue mismatch'
   do i=1,3
      if(maxval(abs(matmul(a,vectors(:,i))-eigenvalues(i)*vectors(:,i)))>1.e-11_dp) &
         error stop 'Eigenpair residual'
   end do
   if(maxval(abs(matmul(transpose(vectors),vectors)-identity))>1.e-11_dp) &
      error stop 'Eigenvectors are not orthonormal'
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'Determinant: ',determinant
   print '(a,3f14.9)', 'Eigenvalues: ',eigenvalues
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Inverse residual: ',maxval(abs(matmul(a,inverse)-identity))
   print *, 'PASS linalg_fortran'
end program checked_lapack_operations

program editable_integer_vector
   use fortran_vector, only: vector_int,size
   implicit none
   type(vector_int)::values
   integer::i,last
   call values%init(2)
   do i=1,8
      call values%append(i)
   end do
   if(size(values)/=8) error stop 'Growth lost elements'
   do i=1,8
      if(values%get(i)/=i) error stop 'Growth changed an element'
   end do
   call values%append([3,1,9,9])
   call values%unique()
   if(size(values)/=9) error stop 'Duplicate removal failed'
   do i=1,9
      if(values%get(i)/=i) error stop 'Unique order was not preserved'
   end do
   call values%remove(4)
   call values%delete(2)
   last=values%pop()
   if(last/=9) error stop 'Wrong final element'
   if(size(values)/=6) error stop 'Wrong edited size'
   do i=1,6
      block
         integer,parameter::expected(6)=[1,3,5,6,7,8]
         if(values%get(i)/=expected(i)) error stop 'Wrong edited contents'
      end block
   end do
   call values%cut()
   print '(a)', 'After growth, unique, remove, delete and pop:'
   call values%write()
   call values%clear()
   print *, 'PASS fortran_vector'
end program editable_integer_vector

program scan_configuration
   use scanner, only: textscanner
   use stdlib_string_type, only: string_type, assignment(=)
   implicit none
   type(textscanner)::scan
   type(string_type)::input
   character(*),parameter::record='steps=12;dt=0.25'
   character(len(record))::recovered
   integer::i,code,steps,separator,status
   real::dt
   input=record
   call scan%new(input)
   ! Reconstruct the complete record through the scanner API.
   do i=1,len(record)
      code=scan%current()
      if(code<0) error stop 'Unexpected end of text'
      recovered(i:i)=achar(code)
      if(i<len(record)) then
         code=scan%next()
         if(code<0) error stop 'Unexpected end while advancing'
      end if
   end do
   if(recovered/=record) error stop 'Text reconstruction mismatch'
   if(scan%next()/=-1) error stop 'Scanner advanced beyond the end'
   call scan%first()
   if(scan%prev()/=-1) error stop 'Scanner moved before the beginning'
   call scan%jump_to(iachar('='))
   if(scan%current()/=iachar('=')) error stop 'First equals not found'
   if(scan%peek()/=iachar('1')) error stop 'Peek mismatch'
   if(scan%current()/=iachar('=')) error stop 'Peek moved the cursor'
   separator=index(recovered,';')
   read(recovered(7:separator-1),*,iostat=status) steps
   if(status/=0) error stop 'Integer conversion failed'
   call scan%jump_to(iachar(';'))
   call scan%jump_to(iachar('='))
   if(scan%peek()/=iachar('0')) error stop 'Second field not found'
   read(recovered(separator+4:),*,iostat=status) dt
   if(status/=0) error stop 'Real conversion failed'
   if(steps/=12 .or. abs(dt-0.25)>epsilon(dt)) error stop 'Parsed values mismatch'
   print '(a)', 'Scanned: '//recovered
   print '(a,i0,a,f6.3)', 'steps=',steps,'  dt=',dt
   print '(a)', 'End boundaries and non-moving peek verified.'
   print *, 'PASS scanner'
end program scan_configuration

gams_procedures.notes: Character-by-character text scanning. The main reconstructs a configuration record through current/next, verifies navigation and end boundaries, and checks that peek does not move the cursor. The recovered fields are converted with ordinary internal READ and compared with known values; this is a small parser example, not a full parsing language.

description: Construct, parse and serialize JSON values with explicit error handling.

program json_round_trip
   use rojff
   implicit none
   type(fallible_json_value_t) :: document, field, restored, invalid
   character(:),allocatable :: serialized
   document=parse_json_from_string('{"steps":12,"dt":0.25,"label":"heat"}')
   if(document%failed()) error stop 'JSON parsing failed'
   select type(object=>document%value_)
   type is(json_object_t)
      field=object%get('steps')
      if(field%failed()) error stop 'Missing steps'
      select type(value=>field%value_)
      type is(json_integer_t)
         if(value%number/=12) error stop 'Wrong integer value'
      type is(json_number_t)
         if(abs(value%number-12.d0)>1.d-12) error stop 'Wrong numeric value'
      class default
         error stop 'steps is not numeric'
      end select
      field=object%get('dt')
      if(field%failed()) error stop 'Missing dt'
      select type(value=>field%value_)
      type is(json_number_t)
         if(abs(value%number-0.25d0)>1.d-12) error stop 'Wrong dt'
      class default
         error stop 'dt is not a number'
      end select
      field=object%get('label')
      if(field%failed()) error stop 'Missing label'
      select type(value=>field%value_)
      type is(json_string_t)
         if(value%string/='heat') error stop 'Wrong label'
      class default
         error stop 'label is not a string'
      end select
      field=object%get('absent')
      if(.not.field%failed()) error stop 'Missing-key error was not reported'
   class default
      error stop 'Expected a JSON object'
   end select
   serialized=document%value_%to_compact_string()
   restored=parse_json_from_string(serialized)
   if(restored%failed()) error stop 'Round-trip parsing failed'
   if(restored%value_%to_compact_string()/=serialized) error stop 'Round trip changed data'
   invalid=parse_json_from_string('{"dt": }')
   if(.not.invalid%failed()) error stop 'Invalid JSON was accepted'
   print '(a)', 'Round-trip JSON: '//serialized
   print '(a)', 'Values, missing-key reporting and malformed-input reporting verified.'
   print *, 'PASS rojff'
end program json_round_trip

gams_procedures.notes: JSON parsing and serialization with explicit error values. The main checks numeric/string fields, missing-key reporting, compact serialization round trips and malformed-input rejection. It uses the original Erloff 2.2.0 API with a pinned compatible Strff 3.1.1 and ISO varying string 3.0.3; the Strff 4.0 dependency graph needs an unavailable GitHub mirror. No computational source is patched.

program typed_command_line
   use iso_fortran_env, only: dp=>real64
   use argparse, only: argparser
   implicit none
   type(argparser)::arguments
   character(2048)::executable
   integer::command_status,exit_status,length,status
   ! The playground starts a main without arguments. Relaunch this executable
   ! once with a fixed example command line to exercise the real parser API.
   if(command_argument_count()==0) then
      call get_command_argument(0,executable,length=length,status=status)
      if(status/=0 .or. length>len(executable)) error stop 'Cannot obtain executable path'
      call execute_command_line('"'//trim(executable)//'" -t 4 --scale 0.25 --name demo --verbose', &
         exitstat=exit_status,cmdstat=command_status)
      if(command_status/=0 .or. exit_status/=0) error stop 'Example command line failed'
   else
      arguments=argparser('Checked scientific command-line options')
      call arguments%set_program_name('example')
      call arguments%add_option_integer('-t','--threads','Thread count',1)
      call arguments%add_option_double('-s','--scale','Scale factor',1.0_dp)
      call arguments%add_option_string('-n','--name','Run label','unnamed')
      call arguments%add_option_integer('-i','--iterations','Iteration count',20)
      call arguments%add_option_logical('-v','--verbose','Enable verbose output')
      call arguments%parse()
      if(arguments%get_option_integer('--threads')/=4) error stop 'Integer option mismatch'
      if(abs(arguments%get_option_double('--scale')-0.25_dp)>1.e-12_dp) error stop 'Real option mismatch'
      if(trim(arguments%get_option_string('--name'))/='demo') error stop 'String option mismatch'
      if(arguments%get_option_integer('--iterations')/=20) error stop 'Default option mismatch'
      if(.not.arguments%has_option('--verbose')) error stop 'Logical option mismatch'
      print '(a)', 'Parsed: -t 4 --scale 0.25 --name demo --verbose'
      print '(a)', 'threads=4, scale=0.25, name=demo; default iterations=20'
      print *, 'PASS argparse-f'
   end if
end program typed_command_line

gams_procedures.notes: Typed process command-line parsing. The main launches itself once with fixed example arguments, then checks an integer, double, string, logical flag and untouched default. No supplied files or playground argument-setting changes are needed. Error exits, positional/named arguments, truncation and every syntax variant are not covered.

program unsigned_boundaries
   use iso_fortran_env, only: int64
   use unsigned_m
   use int_m, only: int
   implicit none
   type(uint32)::a,b,result
   type(uint16)::small
   integer(int64),parameter::modulus=4294967296_int64
   integer(int64)::expected
   a=2147483648_int64
   b=3
   result=a+b
   expected=2147483651_int64
   if(int(result)/=expected) error stop 'Addition across signed boundary failed'
   if(.not.(a>b)) error stop 'Unsigned comparison failed'
   print '(a,i0)', '2147483648 + 3 = ',int(result)
   a=modulus-1
   b=1
   result=a+b
   if(int(result)/=0_int64) error stop '32-bit addition did not wrap'
   result=b-a
   if(int(result)/=2_int64) error stop '32-bit subtraction did not wrap'
   a=-10
   if(int(a)/=modulus-10) error stop 'Negative assignment conversion failed'
   small=65535
   if(int(small)/=65535) error stop '16-bit upper boundary failed'
   small=small+1
   if(int(small)/=0) error stop '16-bit addition did not wrap'
   print '(a)', 'Verified 16/32-bit boundaries, wraparound and negative assignment.'
   print *, 'PASS uint-fortran'
end program unsigned_boundaries

module numerical_specification
   use veggies, only: result_t,assert_equals
   implicit none
contains
   pure double precision function simpson(values,h) result(integral)
      double precision,intent(in)::values(3),h
      integral=h*(values(1)+4*values(2)+values(3))/3
   end function simpson
   function constant_case() result(check)
      type(result_t)::check
      check=assert_equals(6.d0,simpson([3.d0,3.d0,3.d0],1.d0))
   end function constant_case
   function linear_case() result(check)
      type(result_t)::check
      check=assert_equals(2.d0,simpson([0.d0,1.d0,2.d0],1.d0))
   end function linear_case
   function quadratic_case() result(check)
      type(result_t)::check
      check=assert_equals(8.d0/3,simpson([0.d0,1.d0,4.d0],1.d0))
   end function quadratic_case
end module numerical_specification

program run_specification
   use numerical_specification
   use veggies, only: test_item_t,describe,it,run_tests
   implicit none
   type(test_item_t)::tests
   tests=describe('Simpson integration on [0,2]',[ &
      it('integrates a constant exactly',constant_case), &
      it('integrates a linear function exactly',linear_case), &
      it('integrates a quadratic exactly',quadratic_case)])
   if(.not.run_tests(tests)) error stop 'Numerical specification failed'
   print *, 'PASS veggies'
end program run_specification

module arithmetic_callbacks
   use parser_module, only: parser_t,token_t
   implicit none
contains
   function operand(self,token) result(answer)
      class(parser_t)::self
      type(token_t)::token,answer
      real::value
      integer::status
      read(token%string,*,iostat=status) value
      if(status/=0) error stop 'Invalid numeric operand'
      answer%object=value
   end function operand
   function unary(self,operation,argument) result(answer)
      class(parser_t)::self
      type(token_t)::operation,argument,answer
      select type(value=>argument%object)
      type is(real)
         select case(operation%string)
         case('-');answer%object=-value
         case('+');answer%object=value
         case('sqrt');answer%object=sqrt(value)
         case default;error stop 'Unsupported unary operation'
         end select
      class default
         error stop 'Wrong unary operand type'
      end select
   end function unary
   function binary(self,left,operation,right) result(answer)
      class(parser_t)::self
      type(token_t)::left,operation,right,answer
      select type(a=>left%object)
      type is(real)
         select type(b=>right%object)
         type is(real)
            select case(operation%string)
            case('+');answer%object=a+b
            case('-');answer%object=a-b
            case('*');answer%object=a*b
            case('/');answer%object=a/b
            case('^');answer%object=a**b
            case default;error stop 'Unsupported binary operation'
            end select
         class default
            error stop 'Wrong right operand type'
         end select
      class default
         error stop 'Wrong left operand type'
      end select
   end function binary
end module arithmetic_callbacks

program checked_expressions
   use arithmetic_callbacks
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(parser_t)::parser
   type(token_t)::result
   character(24),parameter::expressions(5)=[character(24):: &
      '2+3*4','(2+3)*4','2^3^2','sqrt(9)','-2+6']
   real,parameter::expected(5)=[14.,20.,512.,3.,4.]
   integer::i
   call parser%register_unary(['-   ','+   '])
   call parser%register_function(['sqrt'])
   call parser%register_operator(['^   '],is_right_assoc=.true.)
   call parser%register_operator(['+   ','-   ','*   ','/   '])
   call parser%ignore_tokens([' '])
   parser%on_operand=>operand
   parser%on_unary=>unary
   parser%on_binary=>binary
   do i=1,size(expressions)
      result=parser%parse(trim(expressions(i)))
      select type(value=>result%object)
      type is(real)
         if(.not.ieee_is_finite(value)) error stop 'Nonfinite expression value'
         if(abs(value-expected(i))>1.e-5) error stop 'Expression mismatch'
         print '(a,a,f10.3)',trim(expressions(i)),' = ',value
      class default
         error stop 'Wrong result type'
      end select
   end do
   print *, 'PASS shunting-yard-fortran'
end program checked_expressions

gams_procedures.notes: Token-based expression parsing with user-supplied callbacks. The main checks precedence, parentheses, right-associative exponentiation, square root and unary minus against five exact results. A checksum-guarded edit moves a host-independent library callback to module scope after the original layout crashed in the sandbox; parsing rules are unchanged. The author documents global registrations, fixed precedences and missing syntax validation; concurrent parsers and malformed expressions are not supported by this example.

module demo_token_rules
   implicit none
contains
   logical function field(token)
      character(*), intent(in) :: token
      field = scan(token, ' ,' // achar(9)) == 0
   end function
end module

program main
   use fortran_tokenizer, only: tokenizer_t, token_list, token_t, size
   use demo_token_rules, only: field
   implicit none
   type(tokenizer_t) :: tokenizer
   type(token_list) :: tokens
   type(token_t) :: token
   character(5), parameter :: expected(3) = ['alpha', 'beta ', 'gamma']
   integer :: i
   tokens = tokenizer%tokenize('alpha, beta' // achar(9) // ',gamma', validate=field)
   if (size(tokens) /= 3) error stop 'token count'
   do i = 1, 3
      token = tokens%get(i)
      if (token%string /= trim(expected(i))) error stop 'token contents'
      print '(i0,2a)', i, ': ', token%string
   end do
   call tokens%clear()
   if (size(tokens) /= 0) error stop 'clear'
   print *, 'PASS fortran-tokenizer'
end program

program main

   use integer32_set, only: int32_set, new_int32_set
   use integer64_set, only: int64_set, new_int64_set

      call small%push(int(i, c_int32_t))

   call small%pop(2_c_int32_t)
   call small%sort()

   if (large%data(1) /= 5000000000_c_int64_t) error stop '64-bit value'

   call large%destroy()
   print *, 'PASS integer_set'

description: Reference-counted smart pointers with automatic resource cleanup.
source:
! Adapted from the author's user_object_smart_pointer example.
module demo_resource
   use smart_pointer_m, only: sp_smart_pointer_t
   implicit none
   integer :: cleanup_count = 0
   type, extends(sp_smart_pointer_t) :: resource_t
      integer, pointer :: value => null()
   contains
      procedure :: free
   end type
contains
   impure elemental subroutine free(self)
      class(resource_t), intent(inout) :: self
      if (associated(self%value)) then
         deallocate(self%value)
         nullify(self%value)
         cleanup_count = cleanup_count + 1
      end if
   end subroutine
end module

program main
   use demo_resource
   implicit none
   call exercise()
   if (cleanup_count /= 1) error stop 'cleanup count'
   print *, 'Resource cleaned up exactly once'
   print *, 'PASS smart-pointers'
contains
   subroutine exercise()
      type(resource_t) :: first, second
      allocate(first%value, source=42)
      call first%start_counter()
      if (first%reference_count() /= 1) error stop 'initial count'
      second = first
      if (first%reference_count() /= 2) error stop 'shared count'
      if (.not. associated(first%value, second%value)) error stop 'shared resource'
      if (second%value /= 42) error stop 'resource value'
      print *, 'Shared value:', second%value, 'references:', first%reference_count()
      if (cleanup_count /= 0) error stop 'premature cleanup'
   end subroutine
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Reference-counted resource management. Adapted from the author example: a user type extends sp_smart_pointer_t and implements free. The checked main shares one integer resource, verifies reference counts and shared target, checks no premature cleanup and confirms exactly one cleanup after subroutine return. No source edits. This is not exhaustive compiler finalization conformance testing.

program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use nc4fortran, only: netcdf_file
   implicit none
   type(netcdf_file) :: file
   real(real64) :: original(2,3), restored(2,3)
   character(32) :: units
   integer :: unit
   original = reshape([1.0_real64, 2.0_real64, 3.0_real64, &
      4.0_real64, 5.0_real64, 6.0_real64], [2,3])
   call file%open('measurements.nc', action='w')
   call file%write('temperature', original, ['x','y'])
   call file%write_attribute('temperature', 'units', 'kelvin')
   call file%close()
   call file%open('measurements.nc', action='r')
   call file%read('temperature', restored)
   call file%read_attribute('temperature', 'units', units)
   call file%close()
   if (any(abs(restored-original) > 1.0e-12_real64)) error stop 'array round trip'
   if (trim(units) /= 'kelvin') error stop 'attribute round trip'
   print *, 'Restored array shape:', shape(restored)
   print *, 'Sum:', sum(restored), ' units: ', trim(units)
   open(newunit=unit, file='measurements.nc', status='old')
   close(unit, status='delete')
   print *, 'PASS nc4fortran'
end program

source:
program main
   use array_range, only: array2d_range_type, to_array2d_range
   implicit none
   type(array2d_range_type) :: bounds
   integer :: values(-1:1, 4:5), i, j, total, visited
   bounds = to_array2d_range([lbound(values), ubound(values)])
   if (any(bounds%to_array() /= [-1,4,1,5])) error stop 'bounds round trip'
   total = 0
   visited = 0
   do j = bounds%rank(2)%lower, bounds%rank(2)%upper
      do i = bounds%rank(1)%lower, bounds%rank(1)%upper
         values(i,j) = i+10*j
         total = total+values(i,j)
         visited = visited+1
      end do
   end do
   if (visited /= 6 .or. total /= 270) error stop 'array traversal'
   print *, 'Bounds:', bounds%to_array()
   print *, 'Visited:', visited, ' sum:', total
   print *, 'PASS array_range'
end program

program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use mpmodule
   use playground_kronrod, only: init, kronrod, nwds2
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 3
   type(mp_real) :: nodes(n+1), weights(n+1), gauss(n+1), tolerance, integral, expected
   real(real64) :: result
   integer :: power, i
   if (mpipl < 1000) error stop 'Kronrod requires MPFUN configured for at least 1000 digits'
   call init()
   tolerance = mpreal(10.0_real64, nwds2)**(-40)
   call kronrod(n, tolerance, nodes, weights, gauss)
   ! The routine returns only the nonnegative half of the symmetric 7-point rule.
   do power = 0, 10, 2
      integral = mpreal(0.0_real64, nwds2)
      do i = 1, n
         integral = integral+2*weights(i)*nodes(i)**power
      end do
      if (power == 0) integral = integral+weights(n+1)
      expected = mpreal(2.0_real64, nwds2)/(power+1)
      if (abs(integral-expected) > tolerance) error stop 'polynomial integral'
      result = dble(integral)
      print '(a,i0,a,f18.14)', 'Integral of x^', power, ' on [-1,1]: ', result
   end do
   print *, 'PASS kronrod'
end program

   use iso_c_binding, only: c_int64_t, c_sizeof, c_ptr, c_f_pointer, c_associated
   use fifo_queue, only: fifo, new_fifo_queue
   implicit none
   type(fifo) :: queue
   ! An 8-byte payload also keeps the following C pointer header aligned here.
   integer(c_int64_t), target :: input
   integer(c_int64_t), pointer :: output
   type(c_ptr) :: memory
   integer :: i
   interface
      subroutine c_free(pointer) bind(C, name='free')
         import c_ptr
         type(c_ptr), value :: pointer
      end subroutine
   end interface
   queue = new_fifo_queue(c_sizeof(input))
   do i = 1, 4
      input = 10*i
      call queue%push(input)
   end do
   if (queue%count() /= 4) error stop 'initial count'
   do i = 1, 4
      if (.not. queue%pop(memory)) error stop 'early empty queue'
      if (.not. c_associated(memory)) error stop 'null item'
      call c_f_pointer(memory, output)
      if (output /= 10*i) error stop 'FIFO order'
      print *, 'Popped:', output
      ! Items were allocated by C; release them with C free.
      call c_free(memory)
      nullify(output)
   end do
   if (.not. queue%is_empty()) error stop 'not empty'
   if (queue%count() /= 0) error stop 'final count'
   if (queue%pop(memory)) error stop 'extra item'
   call queue%destroy()
   print *, 'PASS for_fifo_queue'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: FIFO container using C allocations and byte copies. The main enqueues four 64-bit C-interoperable integers, verifies count and exact retrieval order, frees every popped allocation with C free, checks empty-pop behavior and destroys the queue. No source edits. The implementation uses GNU LOC and raw byte storage; the example makes no portability claim for arbitrary derived types, pointer-owning values, threading or every compiler.

description: Pure Fortran regular-expression matching, splitting and replacement.
source:
program main
   use regex, only: re_match, re_match_str, re_split, re_replace
   implicit none
   character(8), allocatable :: fields(:)
   character(:), allocatable :: number, replaced
   if (.not. re_match('^temp=\d+\.\d+$', 'temp=23.50')) error stop 'positive match'
   if (re_match('^temp=\d+\.\d+$', 'temp=warm')) error stop 'negative match'
   number = trim(re_match_str('\d+\.\d+', 'temp=23.50 kelvin'))
   if (number /= '23.50') error stop 'matched substring'
   call re_split('\s*,\s*', 'red, green,blue', fields)
   if (size(fields) /= 3) error stop 'split count'
   if (any(fields /= [character(8) :: 'red','green','blue'])) error stop 'split fields'
   replaced = trim(re_replace('temp', 'temperature', 'temp=23.50'))
   if (replaced /= 'temperature=23.50') error stop 'replacement'
   print '(a)', 'Matched number: '//number
   print '(a)', 'Fields: '//trim(fields(1))//', '//trim(fields(2))//', '//trim(fields(3))
   print '(a)', replaced
   print *, 'PASS jeyemhex-regex'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Pure Fortran regular expressions by Edward Higgins, distinct from perazz/fortran-regex already selected under fortran-regex. The main checks matching and nonmatching anchored decimal measurements, matched substring, comma/space splitting and replacement. No source edits or native regex library. Pattern whitespace is ignored unless escaped; the author documents missing capture references and other features, so PCRE compatibility and all patterns are not claimed.

description: Manipulate UTF-8 strings as arrays of Unicode code points.
source:
program main
   use string_utf_8, only: char_utf, chars_array, chars, substr, indexof, str_replace_all
   implicit none
   type(char_utf), allocatable :: text(:), replaced(:)

   ! UTF-8 code points, not bytes or combined grapheme clusters.
   text = chars_array('café été')
   if (size(text) /= 8) error stop 'code point count'
   if (chars(text) /= 'café été') error stop 'round trip'
   if (chars(substr(text, 6, 3)) /= 'été') error stop 'substring'
   if (indexof(text, chars_array('é')) /= 4) error stop 'search'
   replaced = str_replace_all(text, chars_array('é'), chars_array('e'))
   if (chars(replaced) /= 'cafe ete') error stop 'replacement'
   print '(a)', 'Original: '//chars(text)
   print '(a,i0)', 'Unicode code points: ', size(text)
   print '(a)', 'Substring: '//chars(substr(text, 6, 3))
   print '(a)', 'Replaced: '//chars(replaced)
   print '(a)', 'PASS string-utf-8'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: UTF-8 string handling using one array element per encoded Unicode code point. The main verifies a round trip, code point count, substring, search and replacement of accented text, and prints the results. No source edits. Combining marks remain separate code points; grapheme segmentation, normalization and malformed-input handling are not validated.

description: Measure wall-clock and CPU elapsed time, with optional parallel timers.
source:
program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use fortime, only: timer
   implicit none
   type(timer) :: wall, cpu
   integer :: i
   real(real64) :: total, expected

   call wall%timer_start()
   call cpu%ctimer_start()
   total = 0.0_real64
   do i = 1, 100000
      total = total + real(i, real64)
   end do
   call cpu%ctimer_stop(message='CPU seconds:')
   call wall%timer_stop(message='Wall seconds:')
   expected = 100000.0_real64 * 100001.0_real64 / 2
   if (total /= expected) error stop 'sum'
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(wall%elapsed_time)) error stop 'wall time'
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(cpu%cpu_time)) error stop 'CPU time'
   if (wall%elapsed_time < 0 .or. cpu%cpu_time < 0) error stop 'negative time'
   print '(a,f16.0)', 'Sum of integers 1 through 100000: ', total
   print '(a)', 'Timings illustrate the API; shared sandbox timings vary.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortime'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Serial system_clock and CPU timers. The checked main computes the exact sum of integers 1 through 100000, checks finite nonnegative elapsed times and prints the sum and timings. The root manifest VERSION placeholder is replaced with adapter version 0.0.0; the pinned source commit identifies the actual library. FACE is pinned to an already used revision. No Fortran source edits. MPI/OpenMP timers are not enabled or tested; sandbox timings vary and are not benchmark guarantees.

description: Extensible assertions for scalar and array values and numerical tolerances.
source:
program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use fassert, only: assert_equal, assert_approx_equal, expect_equal
   implicit none
   logical :: passed
   character(:), allocatable :: message

   call assert_equal(2 + 3, 5, 'integer addition')
   call assert_equal([1, 4, 9], [1, 4, 9], 'integer array')
   call assert_approx_equal(sqrt(2.0_real64)**2, 2.0_real64, 'square root round trip', &
      tolerance=1.0e-12_real64)
   ! Capture an intentional failure so the program can inspect it and continue.
   call expect_equal(2 + 3, 6, 'intentional mismatch', passed, output_message=message)
   if (passed) error stop 'mismatch not detected'
   if (index(message, 'intentional mismatch') == 0) error stop 'missing diagnostic'
   print '(a)', 'Scalar, array and approximate comparisons passed.'
   print '(a)', 'Captured expected failure:'
   print '(a)', message
   print '(a)', 'PASS fassert'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Assertions for integer scalars and arrays plus approximate real comparison with an explicit tolerance. The main captures an intentional failed comparison as a logical status and message, checks both, and continues successfully. No source edits; matches the existing Any dependency revision. Not a validation of every type, rank, tolerance convention, custom comparator or test-framework integration.

description: Return and inspect structured error statuses and messages.
source:
program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use errstat, only: error_stat_type, catch_error, set_success, error_occurred
   implicit none
   type(error_stat_type) :: status
   real(real64) :: value

   value = reciprocal(4.0_real64, status)
   if (error_occurred(status)) error stop 'unexpected error'
   if (value /= 0.25_real64) error stop 'reciprocal'
   print '(a,f6.2)', '1 / 4 = ', value
   value = reciprocal(0.0_real64, status)
   if (.not. error_occurred(status)) error stop 'zero not rejected'
   if (status%get_status() /= 1) error stop 'error code'
   if (status%get_message() /= 'Cannot divide by zero') error stop 'error message'
   print '(a,i0,2a)', 'Status ', status%get_status(), ': ', status%get_message()
   value = reciprocal(2.0_real64, status)
   if (error_occurred(status)) error stop 'error not cleared'
   if (value /= 0.5_real64) error stop 'recovery'
   print '(a)', 'A subsequent valid call clears the error.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS errstat'
contains
   function reciprocal(x, status) result(y)
      real(real64), intent(in) :: x
      type(error_stat_type), intent(out) :: status
      real(real64) :: y
      y = 0
      if (x == 0) then
         call catch_error(1, 'Cannot divide by zero', status)
         return
      end if
      y = 1 / x
      call set_success(status)
   end function reciprocal
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Error status and message handling. A custom reciprocal routine uses catch_error and set_success. The main checks a successful result, zero rejection with an exact code and message, and a subsequent successful call clearing the error. No source edits. The reciprocal is only a driver, not a mathematical procedure supplied by errstat. Optional omitted-status termination and user-defined task/message repositories are not exercised.

description: Generic singly linked list with reusable storage for small datasets.

edits.after: type(node) function node_init(data)

source:
program main
   use sll_module, only: sll, iterator, sll_finalizer, iterator_finalizer
   implicit none
   type(sll) :: list
   type(iterator) :: iter
   class(*), pointer :: item
   integer :: n, capacity

   call list%push_back(7)
   call list%push_back(2.5)
   if (list%size() /= 2) error stop 'list size'
   capacity = list%size(.true.)
   iter = iterator(list)
   n = 0
   do while (iter%next(item))
      n = n + 1
      select type (item)
      type is (integer)
         if (n /= 1 .or. item /= 7) error stop 'integer element'
         print '(a,i0)', 'Integer: ', item
      type is (real)
         if (n /= 2 .or. item /= 2.5) error stop 'real element'
         print '(a,f4.1)', 'Real: ', item
      class default
         error stop 'unexpected type'
      end select
   end do
   if (n /= 2) error stop 'iteration count'
   call iterator_finalizer(iter)
   call list%empty()
   if (.not. list%is_empty()) error stop 'empty'
   call list%push_back(9)
   if (list%size() /= 1) error stop 'reused size'
   if (list%size(.true.) /= capacity) error stop 'capacity changed'
   iter = iterator(list)
   if (.not. iter%next(item)) error stop 'missing reused element'
   select type (item)
   type is (integer)
      if (item /= 9) error stop 'reused value'
   class default
      error stop 'reused type'
   end select
   print '(a,i0)', 'Capacity retained after emptying and reusing: ', capacity
   call iterator_finalizer(iter)
   call sll_finalizer(list)
   print '(a)', 'PASS slinked-list'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Generic singly linked list for small datasets. The main checks integer and real payloads in insertion order, list size, iteration count, emptying, retained capacity and the value stored after reuse; iterator and list cleanup are explicit. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit removes PURE from node_init, whose result has a polymorphic allocatable component. Constructor allocation and copying are unchanged, and the call sites are impure. This patched root retains its own small archive instead of sharing an unmodified graph export. No display dependency is needed for the custom consumer. Large-data performance, all mutation operations and ownership of pointer-containing derived types are not validated.

program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: int64, real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use m_random, only: rng_t
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 10000
   type(rng_t) :: generator, replay
   integer(int64), parameter :: seed(2) = [123456789_int64, 987654321_int64]
   real(real64) :: uniform(n), normal(n), poisson(n), pair(2), sphere(3), repeated
   integer :: i, count

   call generator%set_seed(seed)
   call replay%set_seed(seed)
   do i = 1, n
      uniform(i) = generator%unif_01()
      repeated = replay%unif_01()
      if (uniform(i) /= repeated) error stop 'seed reproducibility'
   end do
   ! The implementation returns [0,1), despite the older README saying (0,1].
   if (any(uniform < 0) .or. any(uniform >= 1)) error stop 'uniform range'
   do i = 1, n
      normal(i) = generator%normal()
      count = generator%poisson(4.0_real64)
      if (count < 0) error stop 'negative Poisson count'
      poisson(i) = real(count, real64)
   end do
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(normal))) error stop 'nonfinite normal'
   if (abs(sum(uniform)/n - 0.5_real64) > 0.03_real64) error stop 'uniform mean'
   if (abs(sum(normal)/n) > 0.08_real64) error stop 'normal mean'
   if (abs(sum(normal**2)/n - 1) > 0.12_real64) error stop 'normal second moment'
   if (abs(sum(poisson)/n - 4) > 0.2_real64) error stop 'Poisson mean'
   pair = generator%circle(1.0_real64)
   sphere = generator%sphere(1.0_real64)
   if (abs(sum(pair**2)-1) > 1.0e-12_real64) error stop 'unit circle'
   if (abs(sum(sphere**2)-1) > 1.0e-12_real64) error stop 'unit sphere'
   print '(a,i0)', 'Reproducible uniform samples: ', n
   print '(a,f8.4)', 'Uniform mean (expected 0.5): ', sum(uniform)/n
   print '(a,f8.4)', 'Normal mean (expected 0): ', sum(normal)/n
   print '(a,f8.4)', 'Normal second moment (expected 1): ', sum(normal**2)/n
   print '(a,f8.4)', 'Poisson mean (expected 4): ', sum(poisson)/n
   print '(a)', 'These are small deterministic smoke checks, not a randomness certification.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS rng-fortran'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Xoroshiro128+ pseudo-random generator. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_random.f90 and uses -fwrapv for its intentional signed-integer wraparound. Two fresh generators replay 10000 seeded uniform draws exactly; the main checks the implementation range [0,1), broad uniform/normal/Poisson(4) moment tolerances, nonnegative counts and unit circle/sphere norms. These are deterministic smoke checks, not statistical quality or cryptographic validation. OpenMP, jump independence, large Poisson rates and all distributions are not covered. A separate hosted reproducer confirms that set_seed does not clear the cached second normal after an odd normal() call; use a fresh generator to restart normal sequences. The selected replay uses fresh objects.

program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: int32, int64, real64
   use fast_float_module, only: parse_double, parse_i64, parse_i32, parse_result, &
      parse_options, PRESET_FORTRAN, outcomes
   implicit none
   type(parse_result) :: result
   real(real64) :: value
   integer(int64) :: large
   integer(int32) :: hex

   value = parse_double('3.125e2', res=result)
   if (result%outcome%state /= outcomes%OK%state .or. value /= 312.5_real64) error stop 'decimal'
   print '(a,f8.3)', '3.125e2 = ', value
   value = parse_double('1.25D-2', parse_options(format=PRESET_FORTRAN), res=result)
   if (result%outcome%state /= outcomes%OK%state) error stop 'D exponent status'
   if (abs(value - 0.0125_real64) > 1.0e-16_real64) error stop 'D exponent value'
   print '(a,f8.4)', '1.25D-2 = ', value
   large = parse_i64('9223372036854775807', base=10, res=result)
   if (result%outcome%state /= outcomes%OK%state .or. large /= huge(large)) error stop 'integer limit'
   print '(a,i0)', 'Largest signed 64-bit integer: ', large
   hex = parse_i32('FF', base=16, res=result)
   if (result%outcome%state /= outcomes%OK%state .or. hex /= 255) error stop 'hexadecimal'
   value = parse_double('not-a-number', res=result)
   if (result%outcome%state /= outcomes%INVALID_INPUT%state) error stop 'invalid input'
   print '(a)', 'Invalid input was detected.'
   value = parse_double('1.0e999', res=result)
   if (result%outcome%state /= outcomes%OUT_OF_RANGE%state) error stop 'overflow status'
   print '(a)', 'Out-of-range exponent was detected.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortran-fast-float'
end program main

program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use m_config, only: CFG_t, CFG_add, CFG_get, CFG_get_size, CFG_read_file, CFG_clear
   implicit none
   type(CFG_t) :: config
   integer :: unit, steps, n
   real(real64) :: dt
   real(real64), allocatable :: values(:)
   logical :: enabled
   character(40) :: title

   call CFG_add(config, 'steps', 10, 'Number of time steps')
   call CFG_add(config, 'solver%dt', 0.1_real64, 'Time step')
   call CFG_add(config, 'enabled', .false., 'Enable calculation')
   call CFG_add(config, 'title', 'default', 'Run title')
   call CFG_add(config, 'samples', [0.0_real64], 'Sample values', dynamic_size=.true.)
   ! Create the entire small input file so this example is self-contained.
   open(newunit=unit, file='settings.cfg', status='replace', action='write')
   write(unit, '(a)') 'steps = 25', 'solver%dt = 0.025', 'enabled = .true.', &
      'title = playground', 'samples = 1.0 2.0 4.0'
   close(unit)
   call CFG_read_file(config, 'settings.cfg')
   call CFG_get(config, 'steps', steps)
   call CFG_get(config, 'solver%dt', dt)
   call CFG_get(config, 'enabled', enabled)
   call CFG_get(config, 'title', title)
   call CFG_get_size(config, 'samples', n)
   allocate(values(n))
   call CFG_get(config, 'samples', values)
   if (steps /= 25 .or. .not. enabled) error stop 'scalar settings'
   if (abs(dt-0.025_real64) > 1.0e-14_real64) error stop 'time step'
   if (trim(title) /= 'playground') error stop 'title'

program main
   use kdtree2_precision_module, only: kdkind
   use kdtree2_module, only: kdtree2, kdtree2_result, kdtree2_create, kdtree2_destroy, &
      kdtree2_n_nearest, kdtree2_r_nearest
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 30, neighbors = 4
   real(kdkind), target :: points(2,n), query(2)
   real(kdkind) :: direct(n), work(n), radius2
   type(kdtree2), pointer :: tree
   type(kdtree2_result) :: nearest(neighbors), within(n)
   integer :: i, j, index, expected(neighbors), found

   do i = 1, n
      points(:,i) = [real(mod(i*7,31),kdkind)/31, real(mod(i*11,37),kdkind)/37]
   end do
   query = [0.37_kdkind, 0.62_kdkind]
   do i = 1, n
      direct(i) = sum((points(:,i)-query)**2)
   end do
   work = direct
   do i = 1, neighbors
      expected(i) = minloc(work,dim=1)
      work(expected(i)) = huge(1.0_kdkind)
   end do
   tree => kdtree2_create(points, sort=.true., rearrange=.true.)
   call kdtree2_n_nearest(tree, query, neighbors, nearest)
   print '(a)', 'Nearest neighbors: index, squared distance'
   do i = 1, neighbors
      index = nearest(i)%idx
      if (index /= expected(i)) error stop 'nearest index'
      if (abs(nearest(i)%dis-direct(index)) > 1.0e-6_kdkind) error stop 'nearest distance'
      print '(i5,f12.7)', index, nearest(i)%dis
   end do
   radius2 = 0.08_kdkind
   call kdtree2_r_nearest(tree, query, radius2, found, n, within)
   if (found /= count(direct <= radius2)) error stop 'radius count'
   do i = 1, found
      index = within(i)%idx
      if (index < 1 .or. index > n) error stop 'radius index'
      if (direct(index) > radius2) error stop 'radius membership'
      if (abs(within(i)%dis-direct(index)) > 1.0e-6_kdkind) error stop 'radius distance'
      do j = 1, i-1
         if (within(j)%idx == index) error stop 'duplicate neighbor'
      end do
   end do
   print '(a,i0)', 'Neighbors within squared radius 0.08: ', found
   call kdtree2_destroy(tree)
   print '(a)', 'Checked against an independent direct search; upstream single precision.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS kdtree2'
end program main

description: Forward-mode derivatives, gradients and square Jacobians using dual numbers.
source:
program main
   use differentia, only: wp, derivative, gradient, jacobian
   implicit none
   real(wp) :: value, slope, expected, grad(2), x(2), values(2), jac(2,2)
   character(:), allocatable :: err
   call derivative(scalar, 2.0_wp, value, slope)
   expected = exp(2.0_wp)*(4*cos(2.0_wp)+8*sin(2.0_wp))
   if (abs(value-(4*exp(2.0_wp)*sin(2.0_wp)+1)) > 1.0e-11_wp) error stop 'function value'
   if (abs(slope-expected) > 1.0e-11_wp) error stop 'derivative'
   print '(a,f16.9)', 'Derivative at x=2: ', slope
   x = [2.0_wp,3.0_wp]
   call gradient(multivariate, x, value, grad, err)
   if (allocated(err)) error stop err
   if (abs(value-17) > 1.0e-12_wp .or. maxval(abs(grad-[13.0_wp,5.0_wp])) > 1.0e-12_wp) &
      error stop 'gradient'
   call jacobian(vector, x, values, jac, err=err)
   if (allocated(err)) error stop err
   if (maxval(abs(values-[10.0_wp,7.0_wp])) > 1.0e-12_wp) error stop 'vector values'
   if (maxval(abs(jac-reshape([3.0_wp,4.0_wp,2.0_wp,1.0_wp],[2,2]))) > 1.0e-12_wp) &
      error stop 'Jacobian'
   print '(a,2f9.3)', 'Gradient: ', grad
   print '(a)', 'Jacobian rows:'
   print '(2f9.3)', jac(1,:),jac(2,:)
   print '(a)', 'PASS differentia'
contains
   function scalar(x) result(y)
      use differentia
      type(dual), intent(in) :: x
      type(dual) :: y
      y = sin(x)*exp(x)*x**2.0_wp + 1.0_wp
   end function
   function multivariate(x) result(y)
      use differentia
      type(dual), target, intent(in) :: x(:)
      type(dual) :: y
      y = x(1)*x(1)*x(2)+x(1)+x(2)
   end function
   subroutine vector(x,y)
      use differentia
      type(dual), target, intent(in) :: x(:)
      type(dual), target, intent(out) :: y(:)
      y(1) = x(1)*x(2)+4.0_wp
      y(2) = x(1)*x(1)+x(2)
   end subroutine
end program main

program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: int32, real64
   use m_npy, only: save_npy
   implicit none
   real(real64) :: matrix(2,3), recovered(2,3)
   character(8) :: magic
   character(:), allocatable :: header
   integer(int32) :: header_length
   integer :: unit, i, bytes
   matrix = reshape([1.0_real64,2.0_real64,3.0_real64,4.0_real64,5.0_real64,6.0_real64],[2,3])
   call save_npy('matrix.npy',matrix)
   open(newunit=unit,file='matrix.npy',access='stream',form='unformatted',status='old',action='read')
   read(unit) magic, header_length
   if (magic /= achar(147)//'NUMPY'//achar(2)//achar(0)) error stop 'NPY magic/version'
   if (header_length < 1 .or. header_length > 4096) error stop 'NPY header length'
   allocate(character(header_length) :: header)
   read(unit) header
   if (index(header,'<f8') == 0 .or. index(header,'True') == 0) error stop 'dtype/order'
   read(unit) recovered
   close(unit)
   if (any(recovered /= matrix)) error stop 'matrix payload'
   inquire(file='matrix.npy',size=bytes)
   if (bytes /= 12+header_length+storage_size(matrix)/8*size(matrix)) error stop 'file size'
   print '(a)', 'Matrix written to matrix.npy:'
   do i = 1, 2
      print '(3f7.2)',matrix(i,:)
   end do
   print '(a)', 'NPY header: '//trim(header)
   print '(a,i0)', 'File size in bytes: ', bytes
   print '(a)', 'PASS npy-for-fortran'
end program main

program main
   use ftlDynArrayIntModule, only: ftlDynArrayInt
   use ftlHashMapStringIntModule, only: ftlHashMapStringInt
   implicit none
   type(ftlDynArrayInt) :: array
   type(ftlHashMapStringInt) :: counts
   integer :: i, removed
   call array%New()
   do i = 1, 8
      call array%PushBack(i*i)
   end do
   if (array%Size() /= 8) error stop 'array size'
   if (any(array%data /= [(i*i,i=1,8)])) error stop 'array values'
   print '(a,8i4)', 'Growing integer array: ', array%data
   removed = array%PopBack()
   if (removed /= 64 .or. array%Size() /= 7) error stop 'pop'
   call counts%New(10)
   call counts%Set('red',2)
   call counts%Set('blue',3)
   call counts%Set('red',5)
   if (counts%Size() /= 2) error stop 'map size'
   if (.not. counts%Has('red') .or. counts%Has('missing')) error stop 'map presence'
   if (counts%Get('red') /= 5 .or. counts%Get('blue') /= 3) error stop 'map values'
   print '(a,i0)', 'red: ', counts%Get('red')
   print '(a,i0)', 'blue: ', counts%Get('blue')
   call counts%Erase('blue')
   if (counts%Has('blue') .or. counts%Size() /= 1) error stop 'map erase'
   call counts%Delete()
   call array%Delete()
   print '(a)', 'PASS ftl'
end program main

program main
   use delsparse_mod, only: R8, delaunaysparses
   implicit none
   real(R8) :: points(2,9), queries(2,3), original(2,3), data(1,9), result(1,3), weights(3,3)
   real(R8) :: expected(3), tolerance
   integer :: simplices(3,3), status(3), i, j, k
   ! An irregular grid avoids square-grid diagonal ties; queries are strictly interior.
   points = reshape([0.0_R8,0.0_R8, 1.0_R8,0.0_R8, 0.0_R8,1.0_R8, &
      1.0_R8,1.0_R8, 0.21_R8,0.31_R8, 0.72_R8,0.24_R8, &
      0.32_R8,0.78_R8, 0.76_R8,0.69_R8, 0.51_R8,0.48_R8],[2,9])
   queries = reshape([0.3_R8,0.4_R8, 0.6_R8,0.5_R8, 0.7_R8,0.7_R8],[2,3])
   original = queries
   data(1,:) = 2*points(1,:)-3*points(2,:)+1
   expected = 2*queries(1,:)-3*queries(2,:)+1
   call delaunaysparses(2,9,points,3,queries,simplices,weights,status,interp_in=data,interp_out=result)
   tolerance = 1.0e-10_R8
   if (any(status /= 0)) error stop 'interpolation status'
   if (maxval(abs(result(1,:)-expected)) > tolerance) error stop 'linear reproduction'
   do i = 1, 3
      if (abs(sum(weights(:,i))-1) > tolerance) error stop 'barycentric sum'
      if (any(weights(:,i) < -tolerance)) error stop 'barycentric sign'
      do j = 1, 3
         k = simplices(j,i)
         if (k < 1 .or. k > 9) error stop 'vertex index'
      end do
      print '(a,2f7.3,a,f10.6)', 'At ',original(:,i),' interpolated value: ',result(1,i)
   end do
   print '(a,es12.3)', 'Maximum error for 2*x-3*y+1: ', maxval(abs(result(1,:)-expected))
   print '(a)', 'PASS delaunaysparse'
end program main

! Serial QNSTOP: a seeded search for the minimum of a bounded quadratic.
module playground_objective
   use qnstops_mod, only: r8
   implicit none
contains
   function objective(x, iflag) result(f)
      real(r8), intent(in) :: x(:)
      integer, intent(out) :: iflag
      real(r8) :: f
      f = sum((x - [0.25_r8, -0.5_r8])**2)
      iflag = 0
   end function objective
end module playground_objective

program main
   use qnstops_mod, only: qnstops, r8
   use playground_objective, only: objective
   implicit none
   integer :: status, iterations, evaluations, count
   integer, allocatable :: seed(:)
   real(r8) :: x(2), minimum
   call random_seed(size=count)
   allocate(seed(count))
   seed = 1729
   call random_seed(put=seed)
   x = [1.5_r8, 1.0_r8]
   iterations = 500
   evaluations = 0
   call qnstops(2, [-2.0_r8, -2.0_r8], [2.0_r8, 2.0_r8], objective, &
      x, 'G', minimum, status, n=32, max_iter=iterations, max_eval=evaluations, &
      tau=1.0_r8, gain=10.0_r8)
   print '(a,2f12.7)', 'Estimated minimizer: ', x

! A periodic one-dimensional Poisson problem with an exact sine solution.
program main
   use poisfft
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 32
   real(drp), parameter :: pi_value = acos(-1.0_drp)
   real(drp) :: rhs(n), solution(n), exact(n), x, error
   integer :: i
   type(PoisFFT_Solver1D_DP) :: solver
   do i = 1, n
      x = real(i-1, drp) / real(n, drp)
      exact(i) = sin(2.0_drp*pi_value*x)
   end do
   rhs = -(2.0_drp*pi_value)**2 * exact
   solver = PoisFFT_Solver1D_DP([n], [1.0_drp], [PoisFFT_Periodic, PoisFFT_Periodic], &
      approximation=PoisFFT_Spectral, planning=PoisFFT_Estimate)
   call Execute(solver, solution, rhs)
   call Finalize(solver)
   error = maxval(abs(solution-exact))
   print '(a,i0)', 'Periodic Poisson grid points: ', n
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum error against sin(2*pi*x): ', error
   if (error > 1.0e-10_drp) error stop 'Poisson solution is inaccurate'
   print '(a)', 'PASS poisfft'
end program main

! Transactions in a small sandbox-local LMDB database. Nothing is persisted.
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding
   use lmdb
   implicit none
   type(c_ptr) :: env, txn
   type(mdb_val_type) :: key, value, found
   character(5), target :: key_text = 'color'
   character(5), target :: first = 'green', second = 'amber'
   character(:), allocatable :: text
   integer :: db, rc, unit
   key%mv_size = len(key_text, kind=c_size_t)
   key%mv_data = c_loc(key_text)
   call check(mdb_env_create(env))
   call check(mdb_env_set_mapsize(env, 1048576_c_size_t))
   call check(mdb_env_set_maxdbs(env, 1))
   call check(mdb_env_open(env, 'playground.mdb', MDB_NOSUBDIR, int(o'0600')))
   call check(mdb_txn_begin(env, c_null_ptr, 0, txn))
   call check(mdb_dbi_open(txn, 'colors', MDB_CREATE, db))
   value%mv_size = len(first, kind=c_size_t)
   value%mv_data = c_loc(first)
   call check(mdb_put(txn, db, key, value, 0))
   call check(mdb_txn_commit(txn))
   call read_value('green')
   call check(mdb_txn_begin(env, c_null_ptr, 0, txn))
   value%mv_data = c_loc(second)
   call check(mdb_put(txn, db, key, value, 0))
   call check(mdb_txn_commit(txn))
   call read_value('amber')
   ! An aborted update must not replace the committed value.
   call check(mdb_txn_begin(env, c_null_ptr, 0, txn))
   value%mv_data = c_loc(first)
   call check(mdb_put(txn, db, key, value, 0))
   call mdb_txn_abort(txn)
   call read_value('amber')
   call check(mdb_txn_begin(env, c_null_ptr, 0, txn))
   call check(mdb_del(txn, db, key, c_null_ptr))
   call check(mdb_txn_commit(txn))
   call check(mdb_txn_begin(env, c_null_ptr, MDB_RDONLY, txn))
   rc = mdb_get(txn, db, key, found)
   if (rc /= MDB_NOTFOUND) error stop 'Deleted key still exists'
   call mdb_txn_abort(txn)
   call mdb_dbi_close(env, db)
   call mdb_env_close(env)
   open(newunit=unit, file='playground.mdb', status='old')
   close(unit, status='delete')
   open(newunit=unit, file='playground.mdb-lock', status='old')
   close(unit, status='delete')
   print '(a)', 'Delete and transaction rollback verified.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortran-lmdb'
contains
   subroutine check(status)
      integer, intent(in) :: status
      if (status == MDB_SUCCESS) return
      print '(a)', mdb_strerror(status)
      error stop 'LMDB operation failed'
   end subroutine check
   subroutine read_value(expected)
      character(*), intent(in) :: expected
      call check(mdb_txn_begin(env, c_null_ptr, MDB_RDONLY, txn))
      call check(mdb_get(txn, db, key, found))
      call c_f_str_ptr(found%mv_data, text, found%mv_size)
      if (text /= expected) error stop 'Incorrect database value'
      print '(a)', 'color = ' // text
      call mdb_txn_abort(txn)
   end subroutine read_value
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: LMDB key-value database bindings with Debian LMDB 0.9.31. A checksum-guarded compatibility edit selects the existing signed-kind fallback rather than GNU unsigned extension kinds, which are unavailable without enabling nondefault unsigned support. The checked consumer creates a small sandbox-local database, inserts and updates a value, verifies committed reads and rollback after an aborted update, deletes the key and checks MDB_NOTFOUND, then closes and removes both database files. No persistent storage is provided. Large mappings, concurrent writers/readers, all cursor interfaces and other platforms are not validated.

! Adapted from the author's in-memory string example; no script file is needed.
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding, only: c_associated
   use lua
   implicit none
   type(c_ptr) :: state
   integer :: status, kind
   integer(lua_integer) :: answer
   state = lual_newstate()
   if (.not. c_associated(state)) error stop 'Cannot create Lua state'
   call lual_openlibs(state)
   status = lual_loadstring(state, 'function square_plus_one(x) return x*x+1 end')
   if (status /= LUA_OK) error stop 'Lua source did not load'
   status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0)
   if (status /= LUA_OK) error stop 'Lua definition failed'
   kind = lua_getglobal(state, 'square_plus_one')
   if (kind /= LUA_TFUNCTION) error stop 'Expected a Lua function'
   call lua_pushinteger(state, 6_lua_integer)
   status = lua_pcall(state, 1, 1, 0)
   if (status /= LUA_OK) error stop 'Lua call failed'
   answer = lua_tointeger(state, -1)
   call lua_close(state)
   print '(a,i0)', 'Lua square_plus_one(6) = ', answer
   if (answer /= 37_lua_integer) error stop 'Incorrect Lua result'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortran-lua54'
end program main

! Sandbox-local file metadata and removal using the author's POSIX bindings.
program main
   use unix
   implicit none
   character(*), parameter :: filename = 'playground-posix.txt'
   type(c_stat_t) :: info
   integer :: unit, status
   logical :: exists
   open(newunit=unit, file=filename, access='stream', form='unformatted', status='replace')
   write(unit) 'Fortran POSIX'
   close(unit)
   status = c_stat(filename // c_null_char, info)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'stat failed'
   if (info%st_size /= 13) error stop 'Incorrect file size'
   print '(a,i0,a)', 'Created file: ', info%st_size, ' bytes'
   status = c_unlink(filename // c_null_char)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'unlink failed'
   inquire(file=filename, exist=exists)
   if (exists) error stop 'File was not removed'
   print '(a)', 'Removed the temporary file.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortran-unix'
end program main

! Adapted from the author's serial driver and CONVEX test function.
program main
   use vtmop_lib
   use vtmop_func_mod, only: convex
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: dimensions = 3, objectives = 2
   real(r8), allocatable :: x(:,:), f(:,:)
   real(r8) :: actual(objectives), center(dimensions)
   integer, allocatable :: seed(:)
   integer :: count, status, i, j, k
   call random_seed(size=count)
   allocate(seed(count))
   seed = 1729
   call random_seed(put=seed)
   call vtmop_solve(dimensions, objectives, [0.0_r8,0.0_r8,0.0_r8], &
      [1.0_r8,1.0_r8,1.0_r8], convex, x, f, status, bb_budget=100, &
      maxiters=20, search_budget=6, initial_sbudget=10, lopt_budget=200, &
      local_opt=gps, fit_surrogates=lshep_fit, eval_surrogates=lshep_eval, pflag=0)
   if (status < 0 .or. status >= 10) error stop 'VTMOP failed'
   if (.not. allocated(x) .or. .not. allocated(f)) error stop 'No solutions'
   if (size(f,2) < 2) error stop 'Expected multiple trade-off points'
   if (any(x < 0.0_r8) .or. any(x > 1.0_r8)) error stop 'Infeasible point'
   do i = 1, size(f,2)
      do k = 1, objectives
         center = 0.1_r8
         center(k) = 0.6_r8
         actual(k) = sum((x(:,i)-center)**2)
      end do
      if (maxval(abs(actual-f(:,i))) > 1.0e-10_r8) error stop 'Incorrect objective values'
      do j = 1, size(f,2)
         if (all(f(:,j) <= f(:,i)) .and. any(f(:,j) < f(:,i)-1.0e-10_r8)) &
            error stop 'Dominated point in reported set'
      end do
   end do
   if (maxval(f(1,:))-minval(f(1,:)) < 1.0e-3_r8) error stop 'No trade-off spread'
   print '(a,i0)', 'Nondominated solutions found: ', size(f,2)
   print '(a)', 'First trade-off objective pairs:'
   do i = 1, min(5,size(f,2))
      print '(2f12.6)', f(:,i)
   end do
   print '(a)', 'Verified bounds, objective formulas and nondominance within the returned set.'
   print '(a)', 'PASS vtmop'
end program main

An FPM wrapper selects the unchanged solver, surrogate and test-function sources with bundled SLATEC support and links system LP64 BLAS/LAPACK rather than recompiling those bundled libraries. OpenMP linking is enabled, but the checked run uses the serial driver and one execution thread; heap trampolines support internal callbacks in the sandbox. Adapted from the author serial driver and CONVEX function, the seeded 3-variable/2-objective example uses a small evaluation budget, checks feasible design bounds, recomputes both quadratic objectives independently and verifies that no returned point dominates another. It requires multiple distinct trade-off points. This checks the finite returned set, not convergence to the exact global Pareto front or comparative performance. Parallel evaluation, checkpoint recovery, every surrogate and other problem classes are not validated.

! Treat the constant decay rate as a second state to differentiate with respect to it.
module decay_problem
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   implicit none
contains
   subroutine rhs(n, t, y, f)
      integer, intent(in) :: n
      real(real64), intent(in) :: t, y(n)
      real(real64), intent(out) :: f(n)
      f = [-y(2)*y(1), 0.0_real64]
   end subroutine rhs
   subroutine jacobian(n, t, y, jac)
      integer, intent(in) :: n
      real(real64), intent(in) :: t, y(n)
      real(real64), intent(out) :: jac(n,n)
      jac = 0.0_real64
      jac(1,1) = -y(2)
      jac(1,2) = -y(1)
   end subroutine jacobian
end module decay_problem

program main
   use decay_problem
   use erk_tlm_f90_integrator, only: integrate_tlm
   implicit none
   real(real64) :: y(2), tangent(2,1), atol(2), rtol(2), atol_tlm(2,1), rtol_tlm(2,1)
   real(real64) :: exact
   integer :: status, controls(20)
   y = [1.0_real64, 2.0_real64]
   tangent(:,1) = [0.0_real64, 1.0_real64]
   atol = 1.0e-11_real64
   rtol = 1.0e-9_real64
   atol_tlm = 1.0e-11_real64
   rtol_tlm = 1.0e-9_real64
   controls = 0
   controls(5) = 1 ! Use the supplied analytical Jacobian.
   controls(12) = 1 ! Include tangent variables in adaptive error control.
   call integrate_tlm(0.0_real64, 1.0_real64, 2, 1, y, tangent, atol_tlm, &
      rtol_tlm, atol, rtol, rhs, jacobian, icntrl_u=controls, ierr_u=status)
   exact = exp(-2.0_real64)
   print '(a,f14.10)', 'y(1), exact exp(-2): ', y(1)
   print '(a,f14.10)', 'dy(1)/dk, exact -exp(-2): ', tangent(1,1)
   if (status < 0) error stop 'FATODE integration failed'
   if (abs(y(1)-exact) > 1.0e-7_real64) error stop 'Incorrect solution'

end program main

! Solve A^T X + X A = scale*C for a stable, nondiagonal A.
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use slicot, only: sb03md
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n=2, ldwork=256
   real(real64) :: a(n,n), original(n,n), u(n,n), c(n,n), rhs(n,n), known(n,n)
   real(real64) :: scale, sep, ferr, wr(n), wi(n), work(ldwork), residual
   integer :: iwork(n*n), info
   original = reshape([-1.0_real64,0.0_real64,1.0_real64,-2.0_real64], [n,n])
   known = reshape([2.0_real64,0.5_real64,0.5_real64,1.0_real64], [n,n])
   rhs = matmul(transpose(original),known) + matmul(known,original)
   a = original
   c = rhs
   call sb03md('C','B','N','N',n,a,n,u,n,c,n,scale,sep,ferr,wr,wi,iwork,work,ldwork,info)
   if (info /= 0 .or. scale <= 0.0_real64) error stop 'Lyapunov solver failed'
   residual = maxval(abs(matmul(transpose(original),c)+matmul(c,original)-scale*rhs))
   print '(a)', 'Solution X / scale:'
   print '(2f12.7)', c(1,:)/scale
   print '(2f12.7)', c(2,:)/scale
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum Lyapunov residual: ', residual
   if (residual > 1.0e-10_real64) error stop 'Large residual'
   if (maxval(abs(c/scale-known)) > 1.0e-10_real64) error stop 'Incorrect solution'
   print '(a)', 'PASS slicot'
end program main
