! ARPACK reverse communication: three smallest eigenpairs of a tridiagonal matrix.
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n=20, nev=3, ncv=10, lwork=ncv*(ncv+8)
   integer :: ido, info, iparam(11), ipntr(11), i, j
   real(real64) :: resid(n), v(n,ncv), workd(3*n), workl(lwork), eigenvalues(nev), z(n,nev)
   real(real64) :: tol, exact, product(n), error
   logical :: selected(ncv)
   interface
      subroutine dsaupd(ido,bmat,n,which,nev,tol,resid,ncv,v,ldv,iparam,ipntr,workd,workl,lworkl,info)
         import real64
         character :: bmat
         character(2) :: which
         integer :: ido,n,nev,ncv,ldv,lworkl,info,iparam(11),ipntr(11)
         real(real64) :: tol,resid(*),v(ldv,*),workd(*),workl(*)
      end subroutine dsaupd
      subroutine dseupd(rvec,howmny,selected,d,z,ldz,sigma,bmat,n,which,nev,tol, &
         resid,ncv,v,ldv,iparam,ipntr,workd,workl,lworkl,info)
         import real64
         logical :: rvec,selected(*)
         character :: howmny,bmat
         character(2) :: which
         integer :: ldz,n,nev,ncv,ldv,lworkl,info,iparam(11),ipntr(11)
         real(real64) :: d(*),z(ldz,*),sigma,tol,resid(*),v(ldv,*),workd(*),workl(*)
      end subroutine dseupd
   end interface
   ido = 0
   info = 1 ! Supply a reproducible, nonzero initial residual.
   do i=1,n
      resid(i) = sin(real(i,real64))
   end do
   iparam = 0
   iparam(1) = 1
   iparam(3) = 1000
   iparam(7) = 1
   tol = 1.0e-11_real64
   do
      call dsaupd(ido,'I',n,'SM',nev,tol,resid,ncv,v,n,iparam,ipntr,workd,workl,lwork,info)
      if (ido == -1 .or. ido == 1) then
         call multiply(workd(ipntr(1):ipntr(1)+n-1), product)
         workd(ipntr(2):ipntr(2)+n-1) = product
      else if (ido == 2) then
         workd(ipntr(2):ipntr(2)+n-1) = workd(ipntr(1):ipntr(1)+n-1)
      else
         exit
      end if
   end do
   if (info /= 0 .or. iparam(5) /= nev) error stop 'Eigenvalue iteration failed'
   call dseupd(.true.,'A',selected,eigenvalues,z,n,0.0_real64,'I',n,'SM',nev, &
      tol,resid,ncv,v,n,iparam,ipntr,workd,workl,lwork,info)
   if (info /= 0) error stop 'Eigenvector extraction failed'
   print '(a)', 'Computed eigenvalue       Exact eigenvalue         Residual'
   do j=1,nev
      exact = 2.0_real64-2.0_real64*cos(real(j,real64)*acos(-1.0_real64)/real(n+1,real64))
      call multiply(z(:,j),product)
      error = sqrt(sum((product-eigenvalues(j)*z(:,j))**2))
      print '(3es24.14)', eigenvalues(j), exact, error
      if (abs(eigenvalues(j)-exact) > 1.0e-9_real64 .or. error > 1.0e-9_real64) &
         error stop 'Incorrect eigenpair'
   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS arpack-ng'
contains
   subroutine multiply(x,y)
      real(real64), intent(in) :: x(n)
      real(real64), intent(out) :: y(n)
      y = 2.0_real64*x
      y(2:n) = y(2:n)-x(1:n-1)
      y(1:n-1) = y(1:n-1)-x(2:n)
   end subroutine multiply
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Serial classic Fortran ARPACK-NG interfaces, built from unchanged SRC .f files, the documented UTIL support set, and upstream debug/statistics initializers. The wrapper uses native LP64 BLAS/LAPACK and excludes PARPACK/MPI and generated C bindings. The upstream second_NONE timing stub disables ARPACK internal elapsed-time statistics; playground build/run timings still work. Adapted from the author symmetric reverse-communication example, the main computes three smallest eigenpairs of a 20-by-20 symmetric tridiagonal operator, checks convergence status/count, analytical eigenvalues and eigenvector residual norms. A deterministic nonzero initial residual avoids dependence on random initialization. Nonsymmetric/complex modes, shift-invert, generalized problems and parallel execution are not validated. Dedicated D4 driver checks the three smallest and three largest eigenpairs of the 20-by-20 Dirichlet tridiagonal (2 diagonal,-1 off-diagonal), with explicit starting residual, convergence/extraction status, analytical eigenvalues and sign-invariant sine eigenvector comparisons, equation residuals and orthonormality. Generalized, nonsymmetric, shift-invert and arbitrary spectra are not verified. Refined from broad D4 to D4a1 for the reviewed real symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem interfaces.

source:
! Recoverable diagnostics: validate values and retain a useful application trace.
program main
   use ErrorCriteriaModule
   use ErrorInstanceModule
   use ResultModule
   implicit none
   type(ErrorCriteria) :: handler
   type(ErrorInstance) :: problem
   type(Result0D) :: checked
   call handler%init(errors=[ErrorInstance(code=200, message='Demonstration warning; continuing.', &
      isCritical=.false.)], bashColors=.false.)
   problem = handler%limit(7,0,10)
   if (problem%isError()) error stop 'Valid input was rejected'
   checked = Result(data=7, errors=[problem])
   if (checked%hasError()) error stop 'Unexpected result error'
   print '(a,i0)', 'Accepted value: ', checked%getDataAsInteger()
   problem = handler%limit(12,0,10)
   if (.not. problem%isError() .or. problem%code /= 105) error stop 'Missing range error'
   call problem%addToTrace('read_input')
   call problem%addToTrace('validate_configuration')
   if (size(problem%trace) /= 2) error stop 'Missing application trace'
   print '(a,i0,2a)', 'Rejected value 12 with code ', problem%code, ': ', trim(problem%message)
   print '(a)', 'Trace: ' // trim(problem%trace(1)) // ' -> ' // trim(problem%trace(2))
   call handler%trigger(200)
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortran-error-handler'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Structured error handling and validation. The upstream FPM library sources are unchanged; unlimited free-form line length accommodates existing long source lines. Adapted from the author example, the main checks a valid bounded integer in a Result object, rejects an out-of-range integer with expected code 105, checks two retained application trace entries, and triggers a custom noncritical warning while execution continues. The example uses fixed values rather than interactive input. All Result ranks/types, critical-error termination, all validation criteria and every trace-propagation path are not validated.

! Real 2D Laplace potentials: compare the FMM with an independent log-distance sum.
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: ns=512, nt=16
   real(real64) :: sources(2,ns), charge(ns), targets(2,nt), potential(nt), direct(nt)
   real(real64) :: distance, relative_error
   integer :: i, j, status
   interface
      subroutine rfmm2d_t_c_p(eps,ns,sources,charge,nt,targ,pottarg,ier)
         import real64
         integer :: ns, nt, ier
         real(real64) :: eps, sources(2,ns), charge(ns), targ(2,nt), pottarg(nt)
      end subroutine rfmm2d_t_c_p
   end interface
   do i=1,ns
      sources(:,i) = [real(mod(i-1,32),real64)/31.0_real64, &
         real((i-1)/32,real64)/15.0_real64]
      charge(i) = (1.0_real64+0.3_real64*sin(real(i,real64)))/real(ns,real64)
   end do
   do i=1,nt
      targets(:,i) = [1.25_real64+0.03_real64*i, 0.05_real64*i]
   end do
   call rfmm2d_t_c_p(1.0e-10_real64,ns,sources,charge,nt,targets,potential,status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'FMM2D failed'
   direct = 0.0_real64
   do i=1,nt
      do j=1,ns
         distance = sqrt(sum((targets(:,i)-sources(:,j))**2))
         direct(i) = direct(i)+charge(j)*log(distance)
      end do
   end do
   relative_error = maxval(abs(potential-direct))/maxval(abs(direct))
   print '(a,i0,a,i0)', 'Sources: ', ns, '; targets: ', nt
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Relative maximum error against direct summation: ', relative_error
   print '(a,es16.8)', 'First target potential: ', potential(1)
   if (relative_error > 1.0e-8_real64) error stop 'Incorrect 2D potentials'
   print '(a)', 'PASS fmm2d'
end program main

OpenMP and portable -O2 are enabled; the visitor sandbox uses one execution thread and retains bounds checks. Checksum-guarded compatibility edits skip zero-point multipole/local evaluations and zero-source neighbor calls before passing one-past-end array elements. The inverse reorder helper declares its arrays with the actual n extent rather than the legacy dummy extent 1. Source and target branches receive matching guards; formulas are unchanged. The checked real Laplace driver evaluates 512 deterministic sources at 16 separate targets and compares with an independent charge-weighted log-distance sum. A separate source-and-target probe also checks all source potentials by direct summation with self-interactions excluded, exercising the source-side guards. The code is classified as a structured kernel-matrix application and Green-function evaluation related to PDEs, not as a complete boundary-value solver. Helmholtz, biharmonic/Stokes, dipoles, gradients/Hessians, every complex/vector interface and parallel speedups are not validated. The small accuracy check is not a performance benchmark.

! A cubic is reproduced by the spline, including its first two derivatives.
program main
   use types, only: dp
   use mesh, only: linspace, meshexp
   use splines, only: spline3ders
   use sorting, only: sort
   implicit none
   real(dp) :: x(9), y(9), query(17), value(17), derivative(17), second(17), stretched(9)
   real(dp) :: errors(3), ratio
   integer :: values(6)
   x = linspace(0.0_dp,1.0_dp,size(x))
   y = x**3-2.0_dp*x+1.0_dp
   query = linspace(0.0_dp,1.0_dp,size(query))
   call spline3ders(x,y,query,value,derivative,second)
   errors = [maxval(abs(value-(query**3-2.0_dp*query+1.0_dp))), &
      maxval(abs(derivative-(3.0_dp*query**2-2.0_dp))), maxval(abs(second-6.0_dp*query))]
   print '(a,3es12.4)', 'Maximum errors: value, first derivative, second derivative: ', errors
   if (any(errors > 1.0e-10_dp)) error stop 'Cubic reproduction failed'
   stretched = meshexp(0.0_dp,1.0_dp,4.0_dp,8)
   if (abs(stretched(1)) > 1.0e-12_dp .or. abs(stretched(9)-1.0_dp) > 1.0e-12_dp) &
      error stop 'Incorrect mesh endpoints'
   if (any(stretched(2:) <= stretched(:8))) error stop 'Mesh is not increasing'
   ratio = (stretched(9)-stretched(8))/(stretched(2)-stretched(1))
   if (abs(ratio-4.0_dp) > 1.0e-12_dp) error stop 'Incorrect mesh spacing ratio'
   print '(a,f8.4)', 'Last/first mesh spacing: ', ratio
   values = [9,-2,5,5,0,3]
   call sort(values)
   if (any(values /= [-2,0,3,5,5,9])) error stop 'Incorrect sort'
   print '(a,6i4)', 'Sorted integers: ', values
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortran-utils'
end program main

! Adapted from Formal's extended-gauss-divergence example.
! Copyright (c) 2026, The Regents of the University of California.
! See docs/fpm-candidates/formal/licenses/LICENSE.txt for the upstream terms.
module playground_fields
   implicit none
contains
   pure function scalar(x) result(f)
      real, intent(in) :: x(:)
      real, allocatable :: f(:)
      f = x**2/2
   end function
   pure function vector(x) result(v)
      real, intent(in) :: x(:)
      real, allocatable :: v(:)
      v = x
   end function
end module

program main
   use formal_m, only: scalar_1D_t, vector_1D_t, scalar_1D_initializer_i, vector_1D_initializer_i
   use playground_fields, only: scalar, vector
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   procedure(scalar_1D_initializer_i), pointer :: fs => scalar
   procedure(vector_1D_initializer_i), pointer :: vs => vector
   real :: volume_gradient, volume_divergence, surface, residual

   associate(f => scalar_1D_t(fs, 4, 64, 0.0, 1.0), v => vector_1D_t(vs, 4, 64, 0.0, 1.0))
      associate(dV => f%dV(), dA => v%dA())
         volume_gradient = .SSS. (v .dot. .grad. f) * dV
         volume_divergence = .SSS. (f * .div. v) * dV
         surface = .SS. (f .x. (v .dot. dA))
      end associate
   end associate
   residual = volume_gradient + volume_divergence - surface
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'Integral v grad(f), expected 1/3: ', volume_gradient
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'Integral f div(v), expected 1/6:  ', volume_divergence
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'Boundary flux, expected 1/2:     ', surface
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Divergence-theorem residual: ', residual
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite([volume_gradient, volume_divergence, surface]))) error stop 'nonfinite result'
   if (abs(volume_gradient-1.0/3) > 2e-5 .or. abs(volume_divergence-1.0/6) > 2e-5) error stop 'volume integral'
   if (abs(surface-0.5) > 2e-5 .or. abs(residual) > 2e-5) error stop 'divergence theorem'
   print *, 'PASS formal'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Mimetic vector-calculus library with pinned Julienne and Assert dependencies. A single-image coarray build is used. The checked consumer adapts the author's extended Gauss-divergence example to f=x**2/2 and v=x on a 64-cell unit interval. It checks the two volume integrals against 1/3 and 1/6, the boundary flux against 1/2, finiteness and the conservation residual using single-precision tolerances. The command-line parsing and shell display calls of the upstream example are omitted. Library numerical sources are unchanged. Other 2D/3D operators, time integration and convergence orders are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained; this is not labeled plain BSD-3-Clause.

! Hydrogen check based on dftatom's MIT-licensed tests/hydrogen example.
program main
   use dftatom, only: dp, mesh_exp, mesh_exp_deriv, solve_radial_eigenproblem
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: points=3000, z=1
   real(dp), parameter :: rmin=1e-8_dp, rmax=80.0_dp, ratio=1e6_dp
   real(dp) :: r(points+1), rp(points+1), potential(points+1), p(points+1), q(points+1)
   real(dp) :: energy, exact, error
   integer :: n, l, status

   r = mesh_exp(rmin, rmax, ratio, points)
   rp = mesh_exp_deriv(rmin, rmax, ratio, points)
   potential = -z/r
   print '(a)', 'Hydrogen energies in Hartree: n l computed exact absolute error'
   do n=1, 3
      do l=0, n-1
         exact = -0.5_dp/n**2
         call solve_radial_eigenproblem(n, l, -0.4_dp, 1e-10_dp, 100, r, rp, potential, z, &
            137.035999037_dp, 0, .true., -1.0_dp, 0.0_dp, status, energy, p, q)
         if (status /= 0) error stop 'radial eigensolver did not converge'
         if (.not. ieee_is_finite(energy)) error stop 'nonfinite energy'
         error = abs(energy-exact)
         print '(2i3,2f16.10,es12.3)', n, l, energy, exact, error
         if (error > 1e-7_dp) error stop 'hydrogen energy mismatch'
      end do
   end do
   print *, 'PASS dftatom'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Unmodified Fortran library sources selected from the upstream native makefile and wrapped for FPM. The checked example adapts the upstream hydrogen test to Z=1 and computes all six (n,l) states through n=3 on an exponential radial mesh. It requires solver convergence, finite energies and agreement with the analytical nonrelativistic energies -1/(2*n**2) within 1e-7 Hartree. Relativistic Dirac, Poisson and self-consistent density-functional calculations are present in the library but not exercised by this example. C/Python bindings and optional extra integration/interpolation/LAPACK sources are outside the selected native source set.

description: POSIX system interfaces for files, directories, permissions and process information.
source:
program main
   use M_system, only: system_mkdir, system_isdir, system_isreg, system_remove, system_rmdir, &
      R_USR, W_USR, X_USR
   implicit none
   integer :: status, unit, value
   logical :: exists

   status = system_mkdir('playground-demo', iany([R_USR, W_USR, X_USR]))
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'mkdir failed'
   if (.not. system_isdir('playground-demo')) error stop 'directory not found'
   open(newunit=unit, file='playground-demo/value.txt', status='new', action='write', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'file creation failed'
   write(unit, *) 42
   close(unit)
   if (.not. system_isreg('playground-demo/value.txt')) error stop 'regular file not found'
   open(newunit=unit, file='playground-demo/value.txt', status='old', action='read', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'file open failed'
   read(unit, *, iostat=status) value
   close(unit)
   if (status /= 0 .or. value /= 42) error stop 'file contents mismatch'
   print '(a,i0)', 'Created a directory and regular file; read back ', value
   status = system_remove('playground-demo/value.txt')
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'remove failed'
   inquire(file='playground-demo/value.txt', exist=exists)
   if (exists) error stop 'file still exists'
   status = system_rmdir('playground-demo')
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'rmdir failed'
   if (system_isdir('playground-demo')) error stop 'directory still exists'
   print *, 'Cleanup verified'
   print *, 'PASS m-system'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Unmodified mixed C/Fortran POSIX system library in the Linux/glibc sandbox. The checked example creates a local directory with owner-only permissions, writes and reads back the integer 42, checks directory and regular-file types, removes both and confirms cleanup. Other system calls, processes, networking, permissions changes and Windows portability are not validated or promised. Upstream development dependencies and applications are not part of the consumer demonstration.

description: Fortran bindings for embedding Tcl 8.6 scripting and accessing Tcl/Tk APIs.

edits.after: #include <tcl8.6/tcl.h>

source:
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding, only: c_ptr, c_associated
   use tcl, only: tcl_create_interp, tcl_delete_interp, tcl_eval_ex, tcl_get_string_result, TCL_OK
   implicit none
   type(c_ptr) :: interp
   character(len=:), allocatable :: result
   integer :: status, value

   interp = tcl_create_interp()
   if (.not. c_associated(interp)) error stop 'interpreter creation failed'
   status = tcl_eval_ex(interp, 'set total 0; foreach x {1 2 3 4 5} {incr total [expr {$x*$x}]}; set total')
   if (status /= TCL_OK) error stop 'Tcl script failed'
   result = tcl_get_string_result(interp)
   read(result, *, iostat=status) value
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'Tcl returned a noninteger result'
   if (value /= sum([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]**2)) error stop 'Tcl calculation mismatch'
   print '(a,a)', 'Tcl sum of squares of 1 through 5: ', result
   call tcl_delete_interp(interp)
   print *, 'PASS fortran-tcl86'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Fortran/C bindings linked to pinned Debian Tcl/Tk 8.6 development libraries. A checksum-guarded include edit selects Debian's tcl8.6/tcl.h path for the C macro wrappers; interfaces and calculation code are unchanged. Adapted from the upstream evaluation example, the consumer creates a Tcl interpreter, evaluates an in-memory sum-of-squares script, checks evaluation status and the integer result against Fortran, then destroys the interpreter. Tk graphical windows, extension modules, Tcl stubs and all bindings are not validated; the browser example requires no graphical display or network.

program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use lib_algebra, only: quadratic
   use lib_array, only: linspace, integral, interp1d, ipos, xval
   implicit none
   real(real64) :: x(101), y(101), roots(2), area, midpoint

   call linspace(0.0_real64, 1.0_real64, x)
   y = 2*x+1
   area = integral(x, y)
   midpoint = interp1d(x, y, 0.375_real64)
   call quadratic(1.0_real64, -5.0_real64, 6.0_real64, roots(1), roots(2))
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite([area, midpoint, roots]))) error stop 'nonfinite result'
   if (abs(area-2.0_real64) > 1e-12_real64) error stop 'integration mismatch'
   if (abs(midpoint-1.75_real64) > 1e-12_real64) error stop 'interpolation mismatch'
   if (maxval(abs(roots-[2.0_real64,3.0_real64])) > 1e-12_real64) error stop 'quadratic mismatch'
   ! The requested interval is clipped to the available tabulated domain.
   if (abs(integral(x,y,-1.0_real64,2.0_real64)-2.0_real64) > 1e-12_real64) &
      error stop 'clipped integration mismatch'
   if (ipos(1.0_real64,0.0_real64,0.75_real64,4) /= 2) error stop 'descending histogram bin'
   if (ipos(1.0_real64,0.0_real64,1.1_real64,4) /= 0) error stop 'above descending range'
   if (ipos(1.0_real64,0.0_real64,-0.1_real64,4) /= 5) error stop 'below descending range'
   if (abs(xval(0.0_real64,1.0_real64,2,3)-0.5_real64) > 1e-15_real64) &
      error stop 'bin center precision'
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'Integral of 2*x+1 on [0,1]: ', area
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'Interpolated value at 0.375: ', midpoint
   print '(a,2f10.5)', 'Roots of x**2-5*x+6: ', roots
   print *, 'Clipped integration limits and histogram bins checked'
   print *, 'PASS fortranlib'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Selected base_types, lib_algebra and lib_array modules, using the pinned revision immediately before the upstream FPM test suite introduced source symlinks. Nine checksum-guarded edits bring lib_array exactly to upstream commit 844611933cba06d71490033e68b355f6f0ff704f, retaining its integration-limit, descending histogram-bin and precision fixes. The other selected modules are unchanged. The ordinary archive policy remains unchanged. A synthetic FPM wrapper uses the already generated Fortran sources, not the Python templates. The checked consumer integrates the affine function 2*x+1 on [0,1], checks linear interpolation at an interior off-grid point, and solves x**2-5*x+6 against the exact roots 2 and 3. Additional checks cover integration limits outside the tabulated range, descending histogram bins and bin-center precision; the expanded example fails with the older unpatched array module and passes with the upstream fixes. GAMS F1 denotes the quadratic solver, not a general iterative root finder. Random sampling, statistics, geometry, HDF5/FITS bindings and other modules are not selected; the example does not validate every routine in the included modules.

description: Neural-network inference using the GNU-compatible 0.12.0 source revision.
source:
! Based on Fiats 0.12.0's write-read-infer example, with known network weights.
! Copyright (c), The Regents of the University of California.
! See docs/fpm-candidates/fiats/licenses/LICENSE.txt for the upstream terms.
program main
   use inference_engine_m, only: inference_engine_t, tensor_t, rkind
   use julienne_string_m, only: string_t
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(inference_engine_t) :: network
   type(tensor_t) :: inputs, outputs
   real(rkind), allocatable :: values(:)
   real(rkind) :: expected(2), weights(2,2,2), biases(2,2)
   integer :: i

   weights(:,:,1) = reshape([2.0_rkind, 0.0_rkind, 0.0_rkind, 3.0_rkind], [2,2])
   weights(:,:,2) = reshape([1.0_rkind, 0.0_rkind, 0.0_rkind, 1.0_rkind], [2,2])
   biases(:,1) = [1.0_rkind, -1.0_rkind]
   biases(:,2) = 0.0_rkind
   network = inference_engine_t( &
      metadata=[string_t('Known weights'), string_t('Playground'), string_t('2026-10-29'), &
                string_t('relu'), string_t('false')], weights=weights, biases=biases, nodes=[2,2,2])
   if (network%num_inputs() /= 2 .or. network%num_outputs() /= 2) error stop 'network dimensions'
   do i=-1, 2
      inputs = tensor_t([real(i,rkind), real(i,rkind)])
      outputs = network%infer(inputs)
      values = outputs%values()
      expected = max(0.0_rkind, [2.0_rkind*i+1.0_rkind, 3.0_rkind*i-1.0_rkind])
      if (size(values) /= 2) error stop 'output dimensions'
      if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(values))) error stop 'nonfinite inference'
      if (maxval(abs(values-expected)) > 1e-5_rkind) error stop 'inference mismatch'
      print '(a,i3,a,2f10.5)', 'Input pair: ', i, '  predicted outputs: ', values
   end do
   print *, 'PASS fiats'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Pinned Fiats tag 0.12.0 (upstream manifest version 0.11.1), named inference-engine at that revision, with an explicitly pinned compatible Julienne 1.3.1 dependency and Assert 1.7.0. Tag 0.14.0 was tried first but its consumer build cannot find Julienne modules because they are declared only as a development dependency. Single-image coarrays and long free-form lines are enabled. Based on the author's write-read-infer example, the checked consumer constructs a two-input ReLU network with known diagonal weights and biases, evaluates negative, zero and positive input pairs, and compares every output with direct formulas. K is a broad function-approximation classification; training algorithms, gradients, model-file round trips and parallel speedups are not verified. The historical version is explicit in the menu description. The original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained.

description: Expressive numerical comparisons, unit-test diagnoses and diagnostic messages.
source:
! Uses Julienne's documented comparison idioms.
program main
   use julienne_m, only: test_diagnosis_t, operator(.approximates.), operator(.within.), &
      operator(.equalsExpected.), operator(//)
   implicit none
   type(test_diagnosis_t) :: numerical, exact, intentional_failure
   character(len=:), allocatable :: message

   numerical = (22.0/7.0 .approximates. acos(-1.0) .within. 0.002)
   exact = (sum([1,2,3]) .equalsExpected. 6)
   if (.not. numerical%test_passed()) error stop 'numerical comparison failed'
   if (.not. exact%test_passed()) error stop 'integer comparison failed'
   print *, 'Approximate and exact comparisons passed'

   ! Inspect a deliberately failing diagnosis without terminating the program.
   intentional_failure = (1 .equalsExpected. 2) // ' (deliberate demonstration)'
   if (intentional_failure%test_passed()) error stop 'failed comparison reported success'
   message = intentional_failure%diagnostics_string()
   if (len_trim(message) == 0) error stop 'missing failure diagnostic'
   if (index(message, 'deliberate demonstration') == 0) error stop 'missing appended diagnostic'
   print '(a)', 'Expected failure diagnostic: '//message
   print *, 'PASS julienne'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Standalone demonstration of the modern Julienne testing framework, with its pinned Assert dependency and single-image coarrays. The numerical source is unchanged. The checked consumer verifies an approximate real comparison and an exact integer sum, then deliberately creates a failed test_diagnosis_t, checks its failure flag and nonempty appended diagnostic and prints it while completing successfully. This demonstrates diagnosis construction and inspection rather than macro assertion termination. The full test harness, automatic test discovery, macro enforcement and multi-image behavior are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab/Sourcery Institute license terms and dependency notices are retained.

description: POSIX pipes for reading and writing subprocess streams.
source:
program main
   use M_process, only: streampointer, process_open_read, process_readline, process_close
   implicit none
   type(streampointer) :: stream
   character(len=256) :: line
   integer :: status, read_status, value, i

   call process_open_read("printf '7\n11\n'", stream, status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'pipe open failed'
   do i=1, 2
      call process_readline(line, stream, status)
      if (status /= 0) error stop 'pipe read failed'
      read(line, *, iostat=read_status) value
      if (read_status /= 0) error stop 'invalid pipe output'
      if (value /= 4*i+3) error stop 'unexpected pipe value'
      print '(a,i0)', 'Read from subprocess: ', value
   end do
   call process_readline(line, stream, status)
   if (status == 0) error stop 'expected end of pipe'
   call process_close(stream, status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'subprocess did not exit successfully'
   print *, 'End of output and subprocess status checked'
   print *, 'PASS m-process'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Unmodified Fortran/C POSIX pipe interfaces in the restricted Linux sandbox. Following the upstream process_open_read example, the consumer opens a local printf command, reads and checks the integers 7 and 11, verifies end of output and requires a successful process_close status. Commands run under the ordinary sandbox restrictions; this does not add network or host-system access. Interactive terminals, graphical subprocesses, arbitrary process behavior, write pipes and Windows portability are not verified.

source:
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: nj=96, ms=32
   real(real64), parameter :: pi=acos(-1.0_real64), eps=1e-10_real64
   real(real64) :: x(nj), error
   complex(real64) :: c(nj), fk(-ms/2:(ms-1)/2), reference(-ms/2:(ms-1)/2)
   integer :: j, k, sign, status
   interface
      subroutine nufft1d1f90(nj,xj,cj,iflag,eps,ms,fk,ier)
         import real64
         integer :: nj, iflag, ms, ier
         real(real64) :: xj(nj), eps
         complex(real64) :: cj(nj), fk(-ms/2:(ms-1)/2)
      end subroutine
   end interface
   do j=1, nj
      x(j) = pi*sin(0.71_real64*j)
      c(j) = cmplx(cos(0.13_real64*j), sin(0.17_real64*j), real64)
   end do
   do sign=-1, 1, 2
      call nufft1d1f90(nj, x, c, sign, eps, ms, fk, status)
      if (status /= 0) error stop 'NUFFT returned an error'
      do k=-ms/2, (ms-1)/2
         reference(k) = sum(c*exp(cmplx(0.0_real64, sign*k*x, real64)))/nj
      end do
      if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(real(fk))) .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(fk)))) &
         error stop 'nonfinite transform'
      error = maxval(abs(fk-reference))/max(1.0_real64,maxval(abs(reference)))
      print '(a,i2,a,es12.4)', 'Type 1, sign ', sign, ': scaled maximum error ', error
      if (error > 1e-8_real64) error stop 'transform differs from direct Fourier sum'
   end do
   print *, 'PASS nufft1d'
end program

gams.label: Trigonometric transforms including fast Fourier transforms

gams_procedures.notes: Original one-dimensional nonuniform Fourier code using the dynamically allocated Fortran 90 interface and bundled Netlib FFT implementation. Forty-nine checksum-guarded edits change legacy extent-one FFT dummy-array declarations to assumed size; every changed array is checked against its containing procedure argument list. No local arrays, transform formulas or global bounds-checking settings are changed. Legacy workspace argument type punning is accepted with the package-specific -fallow-argument-mismatch option. The example evaluates a type-1 transform of 96 deterministic nonuniform points into 32 modes for both exponent signs and compares every complex coefficient with an independent direct sum, including the documented 1/nj normalization. Status and finite values are checked. Types 2/3, the static Fortran 77 interface and every bundled FFT routine are not verified.

description: Nonuniform Fourier transforms in 2 dimensions.

program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: nj=96, ms=16, mt=18
   real(real64), parameter :: pi=acos(-1.0_real64), eps=1e-10_real64
   real(real64) :: x(nj), y(nj), error
   complex(real64) :: c(nj), fk(-ms/2:(ms-1)/2,-mt/2:(mt-1)/2)
   complex(real64) :: reference(-ms/2:(ms-1)/2,-mt/2:(mt-1)/2)
   integer :: j, k, l, sign, status
   interface
      subroutine nufft2d1f90(nj,xj,yj,cj,iflag,eps,ms,mt,fk,ier)
         import real64
         integer :: nj, iflag, ms, mt, ier
         real(real64) :: xj(nj), yj(nj), eps
         complex(real64) :: cj(nj), fk(-ms/2:(ms-1)/2,-mt/2:(mt-1)/2)
      end subroutine
   end interface
   do j=1, nj
      x(j) = pi*sin(0.71_real64*j)
      y(j) = pi*cos(0.43_real64*j)
      c(j) = cmplx(cos(0.13_real64*j), sin(0.17_real64*j), real64)
   end do
   do sign=-1, 1, 2
      call nufft2d1f90(nj, x, y, c, sign, eps, ms, mt, fk, status)
      if (status /= 0) error stop 'NUFFT returned an error'
      do l=-mt/2, (mt-1)/2
         do k=-ms/2, (ms-1)/2
            reference(k,l) = sum(c*exp(cmplx(0.0_real64, sign*(k*x+l*y), real64)))/nj
         end do
      end do
      if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(real(fk))) .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(fk)))) &
         error stop 'nonfinite transform'
      error = maxval(abs(fk-reference))/max(1.0_real64,maxval(abs(reference)))
      print '(a,i2,a,es12.4)', 'Type 1, sign ', sign, ': scaled maximum error ', error
      if (error > 1e-8_real64) error stop 'transform differs from direct Fourier sum'
   end do
   print *, 'PASS nufft2d'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Original two-dimensional nonuniform Fourier code using the dynamically allocated Fortran 90 interface and bundled Netlib FFT implementation. Forty-nine checksum-guarded edits change legacy extent-one FFT dummy-array declarations to assumed size after checking that each is a procedure argument; no formulas or local arrays change and bounds checking remains enabled. Legacy workspace argument type punning uses the package-specific -fallow-argument-mismatch option. The example transforms 96 deterministic scattered points onto a 16-by-18 mode grid for both exponent signs, checking status, finite values and all coefficients against an independent direct sum with the documented 1/nj normalization. Types 2/3, the static Fortran 77 interface, every FFT routine and multidimensional performance are not verified.

program main
   use aotus_module, only: flu_State, open_config_file, close_config, aot_get_val, &
      aoterr_Fatal, aoterr_NonExistent
   use aot_table_module, only: aot_table_open, aot_table_close, aot_table_length
   use flu_kinds_module, only: double_k
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(flu_State) :: config
   integer :: unit, status, steps, nx, ny, mesh, fallback
   real(double_k) :: scale

   open(newunit=unit, file='playground-config.lua', status='new', action='write', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'cannot create configuration'
   write(unit,'(a)') 'steps = 3*4', 'scale = 1.5', 'mesh = {nx=4, ny=6}'
   close(unit)
   call open_config_file(L=config, filename='playground-config.lua', ErrCode=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'configuration load failed'
   call aot_get_val(L=config, key='steps', val=steps, ErrCode=status)
   if (btest(status,aoterr_Fatal) .or. steps /= 12) error stop 'steps mismatch'
   call aot_get_val(L=config, key='scale', val=scale, ErrCode=status)
   if (btest(status,aoterr_Fatal)) error stop 'scale retrieval failed'
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(scale)) error stop 'nonfinite scale'
   if (abs(scale-1.5_double_k) > 1e-12_double_k) error stop 'scale mismatch'
   call aot_table_open(L=config, thandle=mesh, key='mesh')
   if (mesh == 0) error stop 'mesh table missing'
   if (aot_table_length(L=config,thandle=mesh) /= 2) error stop 'mesh table length'
   call aot_get_val(L=config, thandle=mesh, key='nx', val=nx, ErrCode=status)
   if (btest(status,aoterr_Fatal) .or. nx /= 4) error stop 'nx mismatch'
   call aot_get_val(L=config, thandle=mesh, key='ny', val=ny, ErrCode=status)
   if (btest(status,aoterr_Fatal) .or. ny /= 6) error stop 'ny mismatch'
   call aot_table_close(L=config, thandle=mesh)
   call aot_get_val(L=config, key='missing', val=fallback, ErrCode=status, default=99)
   if (btest(status,aoterr_Fatal) .or. .not. btest(status,aoterr_NonExistent)) error stop 'default status'
   if (fallback /= 99) error stop 'default value mismatch'
   call close_config(L=config)
   print '(a,i0,a,f5.2)', 'Steps: ', steps, '  scale: ', scale
   print '(a,i0,a,i0)', 'Mesh: ', nx, ' by ', ny
   print '(a,i0)', 'Missing setting uses default: ', fallback
   open(newunit=unit, file='playground-config.lua', status='old', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'cannot reopen configuration for cleanup'
   close(unit,status='delete')
   print *, 'PASS aotus'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Mixed C/Fortran source set selected from the upstream Waf library lists, wrapped for FPM with the bundled Lua 5.4.8 core and libraries, the C dump wrapper and GNU-supported extended/quad precision module variants. Lua command-line interpreter/compiler executables and upstream tests are excluded. Sources are unchanged; the operator-only wrapper now permits explicitly listed locked C files, retaining old adapter identities and the ordinary downloader/archive limits. The consumer creates a small Lua configuration, checks a computed integer, a double-precision scalar, two named nested-table entries and a missing-key default with error bits, closes the state and deletes its file. Broader scripting, dump/reload callbacks, every numeric kind and sandbox-restricted system operations are not verified.

module playground_operator
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   implicit none
contains
   ! A is an m-by-n diagonal matrix with diagonal entries 1,...,n.
   subroutine product(trans,m,n,x,y,dparm,iparm)
      character, intent(in) :: trans
      integer :: m, n, iparm(*)
      real(real64) :: x(*), y(*), dparm(*)
      integer :: j
      if (trans == 'n' .or. trans == 'N') then
         y(1:m) = 0.0_real64
      else
         y(1:n) = 0.0_real64
      end if
      do j=1, min(m,n)
         y(j) = j*x(j)
      end do
   end subroutine
end module

program main
   use playground_operator, only: real64, product
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: m=18, n=12, wanted=3, kmax=12, lwork=10000, liwork=1000
   real(real64) :: u(m,kmax+1), v(n,kmax), sigma(kmax), bounds(kmax), work(lwork)
   real(real64) :: options(3), dparm(1), av(m), atu(n), tolerance, residual
   integer :: iwork(liwork), ioptions(2), iparm(1), info, j, k
   interface
      subroutine dlansvd(jobu,jobv,m,n,k,kmax,aprod,u,ldu,sigma,bnd,v,ldv,tolin, &
                         work,lwork,iwork,liwork,doption,ioption,info,dparm,iparm)
         import real64
         character :: jobu, jobv
         integer :: m,n,k,kmax,ldu,ldv,lwork,liwork,info,iwork(liwork),ioption(*),iparm(*)
         real(real64) :: u(ldu,*),v(ldv,*),sigma(*),bnd(*),tolin,work(lwork),doption(*),dparm(*)
         external :: aprod
      end subroutine
   end interface
   u = 0.0_real64
   u(1:n,1) = 1.0_real64
   v = 0.0_real64
   options = [-1.0_real64,-1.0_real64,12.0_real64]
   ioptions = [1,1]
   work = 0.0_real64
   iwork = 0
   dparm = 0.0_real64
   iparm = 0
   tolerance = 1e-12_real64
   ! PROPACK updates k to the number of converged singular values.
   k = wanted
   call dlansvd('Y','Y',m,n,k,kmax,product,u,m,sigma,bounds,v,n,tolerance, &
                work,lwork,iwork,liwork,options,ioptions,info,dparm,iparm)
   if (info /= 0) error stop 'PROPACK did not converge'
   if (k /= wanted) error stop 'unexpected number of singular values'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(sigma(1:k)))) error stop 'nonfinite singular values'
   do j=1, k
      if (abs(sigma(j)-(n-j+1)) > 1e-8_real64) error stop 'singular value mismatch'
      call product('n',m,n,v(:,j),av,dparm,iparm)
      call product('t',m,n,u(:,j),atu,dparm,iparm)
      residual = max(sqrt(sum((av-sigma(j)*u(:,j))**2)),sqrt(sum((atu-sigma(j)*v(:,j))**2)))
      print '(a,f12.8,a,es12.3)', 'Singular value: ', sigma(j), '  residual: ', residual
      if (.not. ieee_is_finite(residual)) error stop 'nonfinite residual'
      if (residual > 1e-8_real64) error stop 'singular vector residual'
      if (abs(sum(u(:,j)**2)-1) > 1e-8_real64 .or. abs(sum(v(:,j)**2)-1) > 1e-8_real64) &
         error stop 'singular vector normalization'
   end do
   print *, 'PASS propack'
end program

gams_procedures.notes: Historical SciPy PROPACK 2.1 sources, whose repository is archived and explicitly points to rmlarsen/propack for the maintained implementation. The current author archive and tags v2.2/v2.1 exceed the unchanged source download limit, largely due to saved example outputs. The menu explicitly identifies this historical source choice. Only the native double-precision serial routines are wrapped, using the portable RISC modified Gram-Schmidt implementation and compatible system LP64 BLAS/LAPACK. Numerical sources are unchanged. A callback supplies multiplication by a rectangular diagonal matrix with known singular values. The consumer passes a writable convergence-count argument, requests the leading three singular triplets, and checks 12, 11 and 10, both A*v-sigma*u and transpose(A)*u-sigma*v residuals, finite values and unit vector norms. The restarted algorithm, other precisions, arbitrary sparse matrices and parallel performance are not verified.

module qhashtbl_m
    use iso_c_binding
    use qhashtbl_interface_m
    use qlibc_util_m
    use qhashtbl_util_m
    implicit none


    type, public :: qhashtbl_t
        private
        type(c_ptr) :: q_cp = c_null_ptr
        integer(c_size_t) :: size_data

        logical :: was_init = .false.
        ! It seems, that gfortran has a bug, which prevents qobj to be initialized to c_null_ptr here.
        ! variable wasInit is used as a workaround.
    contains
        final :: qhashtbl_free
        procedure :: new => qhashtbl_new          !< Constructor of the container. Should be called before the use.
        procedure :: put => qhashtbl_put          !< Put key-value pair to the container.
        procedure :: putstr => qhashtbl_putstr    !< Put string to the container.
        procedure :: get => qhashtbl_get          !< Get data.
        procedure :: getstr => qhashtbl_getstr    !< Get character data.
        procedure :: haskey => qhashtbl_haskey    !< Return if the key is in the container.
        procedure :: remove => qhashtbl_remove    !< Remove key from the container.
        procedure :: size => qhashtbl_size        !< Get current size (number of pairs) in the container.
        procedure :: getnext => qhashtbl_getnext  !< Get next object.
        procedure :: clear => qhashtbl_clear      !< Remove all values from the container.
    end type

    ! Type describes a one object of the qhashtbl
    type, public :: qhashtbl_obj_t
        type(c_ptr) :: qobj = c_null_ptr
        logical :: wasInit = .false.
        ! It seems, that gfortran has a bug, which prevents qobj to be initialized to c_null_ptr here.
        ! Variable wasInit is used as a workaround.
    contains
        final :: qhashtbl_objfree
        procedure :: getdata => qhashtbl_getdata                !< Get data from the object.
        procedure :: getname => qhashtbl_getname                !< Get name from the object.
        procedure :: init => qhashtbl_objinit                   !< Initialize the object.
    end type

    interface assignment(=)
        module procedure qhashtbl_copy
        module procedure qhashtbl_obj_copy
    end interface

    private
    public :: assignment(=)

contains

    !> @brief qhashtbl constructor
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_new(self, range, size_data)
        class(qhashtbl_t) :: self
        integer, optional, intent(in) :: range      !< initial size of index range. Value of 0 will use default value.
        integer, optional, intent(in) :: size_data  !< size of each element in bytes.

        integer(c_int) :: opt = 0
        integer(c_size_t) :: ran

        if (present(range)) then
            ran = range
        else
            ran = 0
        end if
        self%q_cp = qhashtbl_c(ran, opt)
        if (present(size_data)) then
            self%size_data = int(size_data, kind=c_size_t)
        else
            self%size_data = 0
        end if

        self%was_init = .true.
    end subroutine

    !> @brief  Destructor of the qhashtbl.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_free(self)
        type(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: self

        if (.not. self%was_init) then
            self%q_cp = c_null_ptr
            self%was_init = .true.
        end if

        if (c_associated(self%q_cp)) then
            call qhashtbl_free_c(self%q_cp)
            self%q_cp = c_null_ptr
        end if
    end subroutine

    !> @brief  Put a value into this table.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_put(self, name, val_data, size_data, success)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in) :: name       !< key name.
#ifndef USE_COMPILER_DIRECTIVE
        type(*), target, intent(in) :: val_data   !< data to put
#else
#include "nocheck_val_data.fi"
#endif
        integer, optional, intent(in)  :: size_data !< size of data object.
        logical, optional, intent(out) :: success  !< true if successful.

        integer(c_size_t) :: sd
        logical(c_bool) :: suc_c

        if (present(size_data)) then
            sd = int(size_data, kind=c_size_t)
        else
            sd = self%size_data
        end if

        suc_c = qhashtbl_put_c(self%q_cp, f_c_string(name), c_loc(val_data), sd)
        if (present(success)) success = suc_c
    end subroutine

    !> @brief  Put a string into this table.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_putstr(self, name, str_data, success)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in)     :: name      !< key name.
        character(len=*), target, intent(in) :: str_data  !< string to put.
        logical, optional, intent(out)   :: success   !< true if successful.

        logical(c_bool) :: suc_c

        suc_c = qhashtbl_put_c(self%q_cp, f_c_string(name), c_loc(str_data), len(str_data, kind=c_size_t))
        if (present(success)) success = suc_c
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Get data from the table.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_get(self, name, val_data, found)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(in) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in)  :: name  !< key name.
#ifndef USE_COMPILER_DIRECTIVE
        type(*), target :: val_data   !< returned data.
#else
#include "nocheck_val_data.fi"
#endif
        logical, intent(out) :: found          !< true if key was found.

        integer(c_size_t), target :: size_data
        type(c_ptr) :: size_data_p
        type(c_ptr) :: val_data_p
        logical(c_bool) :: newmem = .false.

        size_data_p = c_loc(size_data)
        val_data_p = qhashtbl_get_c(self%q_cp, f_c_string(name), size_data_p, newmem)
        if (c_associated(val_data_p)) then
            call qlibc_copy_data_c(val_data_p, c_loc(val_data), size_data, newmem)
            found = .true.
        else
            found = .false.
        end if
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Get character data.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_getstr(self, name, str_data, found)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(in) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in)  :: name  !< key name.
        character(len=:), allocatable, target, intent(inout) :: str_data  !< returned string.
        logical, intent(out) :: found          !< true if key was found, else false.

        integer(c_size_t), target :: size_data
        type(c_ptr) :: size_data_p
        type(c_ptr) :: val_data_p
        logical(c_bool) :: newmem = .false.

        size_data_p = c_loc(size_data)
        val_data_p = qhashtbl_get_c(self%q_cp, f_c_string(name), size_data_p, newmem)
        if (c_associated(val_data_p)) then
            if (allocated(str_data)) then
                if (len(str_data) /= size_data) then
                    deallocate(str_data)
                    allocate(character(len=size_data) :: str_data)
                end if
            else
                allocate(character(len=size_data) :: str_data)
            end if
            call qlibc_copy_data_c(val_data_p, c_loc(str_data), size_data, newmem)
            found = .true.
        else
            found = .false.
        end if
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Return if the key is in the container.
    !!
    logical function qhashtbl_haskey(self, name)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(in) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in)  :: name  !< key name.

        type(c_ptr) :: size_data_p
        type(c_ptr) :: val_data_p
        logical(c_bool) :: newmem = .false.

        size_data_p = c_null_ptr
        val_data_p = qhashtbl_get_c(self%q_cp, f_c_string(name), size_data_p, newmem)
        if (c_associated(val_data_p)) then
            qhashtbl_haskey = .true.
        else
            qhashtbl_haskey = .false.
        end if
    end function

    !> @brief Remove an object from this table.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_remove(self, name, success)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in)  :: name     !< key name.
        logical, optional, intent(out) :: success !< true if successful, else false.

        logical(c_bool) :: suc

        suc = qhashtbl_remove_c(self%q_cp, f_c_string(name))
        if (present(success)) success = suc
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Get next element.
    !!
    logical function qhashtbl_getnext(self, obj)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(in) :: self
        type(qhashtbl_obj_t), intent(inout) :: obj  !< qhashtbl object.
        logical(c_bool) :: newmem = .false.

        qhashtbl_getnext = qhashtbl_getnext_c(self%q_cp, obj%qobj, newmem)
    end function

    !> @brief Returns the number of keys in this hashtable.
    !!
    integer function qhashtbl_size(self)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(in) :: self

        qhashtbl_size = qhashtbl_size_c(self%q_cp)
    end function

    !> @brief Clears this hashtable so that it contains no keys.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_clear(self)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: self

        call qhashtbl_clear_c(self%q_cp)
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Copy procedure.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_copy(to, from)
        type(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: to
        type(qhashtbl_t), intent(in)    :: from

        if (.not. to%was_init) then
            to%q_cp = c_null_ptr
            to%was_init = .true.
        end if
        call qhashtbl_copy_c(to%q_cp, from%q_cp)
        to%size_data = from%size_data
    end subroutine



    !**********************************************
    !*** Procedures for work with qhashtbl_obj_t
    !**********************************************

    !> @brief Initialize the object. Should be called before the use of the object.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_objinit(obj)
        class(qhashtbl_obj_t), intent(inout) :: obj

        if (.not. obj%wasInit) then
            obj%wasInit = .true.
            obj%qobj = c_null_ptr
        end if

        if ( .not. c_associated(obj%qobj)) then
            obj%qobj = qhashtbl_getobj_c()
        else
            call qhashtbl_objinit_c(obj%qobj)
        end if
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Destructor.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_objfree(obj)
        type(qhashtbl_obj_t), intent(inout) :: obj

        if (.not. obj%wasInit) then
            obj%qobj = c_null_ptr
            obj%wasInit = .true.
        end if
        if (c_associated(obj%qobj)) then
            call qlibc_free_c(obj%qobj)
            obj%qobj = c_null_ptr
        end if
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Copy procedure. Should not be called.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_obj_copy(to, from)
        type(qhashtbl_obj_t), intent(inout) :: to
        type(qhashtbl_obj_t), intent(in)    :: from

        print *, "Error. qhashtbl_obj_t object can not be copied."
        print *, "Sub: qhashtbl_obj_copy"
        stop "Program terminated!"
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Get data from the object.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_getdata(obj, val_data)
        class(qhashtbl_obj_t) :: obj
#ifndef USE_COMPILER_DIRECTIVE
        type(*), target :: val_data   !< returned data.
#else
#include "nocheck_val_data.fi"
#endif

        call qhashtbl_getdata_c(obj%qobj, c_loc(val_data))
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Get name from the object.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_getname(obj, name)
        class(qhashtbl_obj_t) :: obj
        character(len=:), allocatable, target, intent(inout) :: name  !< returned name

        integer(c_size_t) :: namesize

        namesize = qhashtbl_getnamesize_c(obj%qobj)
        if (allocated(name)) then
            if (len(name) /= namesize) then
                deallocate(name)
                allocate(character(len=namesize) :: name)
            end if
        else
            allocate(character(len=namesize) :: name)
        end if

        call qhashtbl_getname_c(obj%qobj, c_loc(name))
    end subroutine

end module

#undef USE_COMPILER_DIRECTIVE
#endif

#ifndef USE_COMPILER_DIRECTIVE
        type(*), target :: val_data   !< returned data.
#else
#include "nocheck_val_data.fi"
#endif
        logical, intent(out) :: found          !< true if key was found.

        integer(c_size_t), target :: size_data
        type(c_ptr) :: size_data_p
        type(c_ptr) :: val_data_p
        logical(c_bool) :: newmem = .false.

        size_data_p = c_loc(size_data)
        val_data_p = qhashtbl_get_c(self%q_cp, qlibc_f_c_string(name), size_data_p, newmem)
        if (c_associated(val_data_p)) then
            call qlibc_copy_data_c(val_data_p, c_loc(val_data), size_data, newmem)
            found = .true.
        else
            found = .false.
        end if
    end subroutine

    !> @brief Get character data.
    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_getstr(self, name, str_data, found)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(in) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in)  :: name  !< key name.
        character(len=:), allocatable, target, intent(inout) :: str_data  !< returned string.
        logical, intent(out) :: found          !< true if key was found, else false.

        integer(c_size_t), target :: size_data
        type(c_ptr) :: size_data_p
        type(c_ptr) :: val_data_p
        logical(c_bool) :: newmem = .false.

        size_data_p = c_loc(size_data)
        val_data_p = qhashtbl_get_c(self%q_cp, qlibc_f_c_string(name), size_data_p, newmem)
        if (c_associated(val_data_p)) then
            if (allocated(str_data)) then
                if (len(str_data) /= size_data) then
                    deallocate(str_data)
                    allocate(character(len=size_data) :: str_data)
                end if
            else
                allocate(character(len=size_data) :: str_data)
            end if
            call qlibc_copy_data_c(val_data_p, c_loc(str_data), size_data, newmem)
            found = .true.
        else
            found = .false.
        end if
    end subroutine

    !!

        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(in) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in)  :: name  !< key name.

        type(c_ptr) :: size_data_p
        type(c_ptr) :: val_data_p
        logical(c_bool) :: newmem = .false.

        size_data_p = c_null_ptr
        val_data_p = qhashtbl_get_c(self%q_cp, qlibc_f_c_string(name), size_data_p, newmem)
        if (c_associated(val_data_p)) then
            qhashtbl_haskey = .true.
        else
            qhashtbl_haskey = .false.
        end if
    end function

    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_remove(self, name, success)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: self
        character(len=*), intent(in)  :: name     !< key name.
        logical, optional, intent(out) :: success !< true if successful, else false.

        logical(c_bool) :: suc

        suc = qhashtbl_remove_c(self%q_cp, qlibc_f_c_string(name))
        if (present(success)) success = suc
    end subroutine

        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(in) :: self
        type(qhashtbl_obj_t), intent(inout) :: obj  !< qhashtbl object.
        logical(c_bool) :: newmem = .false.

        qhashtbl_getnext = qhashtbl_getnext_c(self%q_cp, obj%qobj, newmem)
    end function

    integer function qhashtbl_size(self)

    subroutine qhashtbl_clear(self)
        class(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: self

    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_copy(to, from)
        type(qhashtbl_t), intent(inout) :: to
        type(qhashtbl_t), intent(in)    :: from

        if (.not. to%was_init) then
            to%q_cp = c_null_ptr
            to%was_init = .true.
        end if
        call qhashtbl_copy_c(to%q_cp, from%q_cp)

    !!
    subroutine qhashtbl_objinit(obj)
        class(qhashtbl_obj_t), intent(inout) :: obj

        if (.not. obj%wasInit) then
            obj%wasInit = .true.
            obj%qobj = c_null_ptr
        end if

        if ( .not. c_associated(obj%qobj)) then
            obj%qobj = qhashtbl_getobj_c()

            obj%wasInit = .true.
        end if

            obj%qobj = c_null_ptr

#ifndef USE_COMPILER_DIRECTIVE
        type(*), target :: val_data   !< returned data.

        class(qhashtbl_obj_t) :: obj
        character(len=:), allocatable, target, intent(inout) :: name  !< returned name

! Integer vectors and string-keyed maps, following the upstream tutorials.
program main
   use qvector_m, only: qvector_t, QVECTOR_RESIZE_LINEAR
   use qhashtbl_m, only: qhashtbl_t
   implicit none
   integer :: i, value, values(5)
   logical :: found
   ! Block scope invokes finalizers for both C-backed containers.
   block
      type(qvector_t) :: vector
      type(qhashtbl_t) :: table
      call vector%new(2, storage_size(i)/8, QVECTOR_RESIZE_LINEAR)
      do i = 1, 5
         call vector%addlast(i, found)
         if (.not. found) error stop 'vector append failed'
      end do
      if (vector%size() /= 5) error stop 'vector growth failed'
      call vector%getat(3, value, found)
      if (.not. found .or. value /= 3) error stop 'vector indexing failed'
      call vector%setat(5, 50, found)
      if (.not. found) error stop 'vector replacement failed'
      call vector%toarray(values)
      if (any(values /= [1, 2, 3, 4, 50])) error stop 'vector contents failed'
      print '(a,5i4)', 'Vector: ', values
      call vector%popfirst(value, found)
      if (.not. found .or. value /= 1) error stop 'vector pop failed'
      if (vector%size() /= 4) error stop 'vector pop size failed'
      call table%new(range=10, size_data=storage_size(value)/8)
      call table%put('red', 10, success=found)
      if (.not. found) error stop 'map insertion failed'
      call table%put('blue', 20, success=found)
      if (.not. found) error stop 'map insertion failed'
      call table%put('red', 30, success=found)
      if (.not. found) error stop 'map replacement failed'
      call table%get('red', value, found)
      if (.not. found .or. value /= 30) error stop 'map lookup failed'
      print '(a,i0)', 'Map red: ', value
      call table%get('missing', value, found)
      if (found) error stop 'missing key reported present'
      call vector%clear()
      call table%clear()
      if (vector%size() /= 0 .or. table%size() /= 0) error stop 'clear failed'
   end block
   print '(a)', 'PASS qcontainers'
end program main

The unrelated qencode.c utility is excluded: its query parser refers to qstrtrim and qlisttbl routines absent from the archive. ! All files are temporary and stay inside the program's working directory.
program main
   use os, only: mkdir, rmdir, rename, unlink, os_name, os_id, OS_LINUX
   use os_path, only: join, exists, isdir, isfile, getsize, basename, dirname, normpath
   implicit none
   integer :: status, unit
   character(:), allocatable :: folder, filename, renamed
   if (os_id /= OS_LINUX .or. os_name /= 'Linux') error stop 'Linux configuration failed'
   folder = join('os-demo', 'nested')
   filename = join(folder, 'sample.txt')
   renamed = join(folder, 'renamed.txt')
   call mkdir('os-demo', stat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'mkdir failed'
   call mkdir(folder, stat=status)
   if (status /= 0 .or. .not. isdir(folder)) error stop 'nested directory failed'
   open(newunit=unit, file=filename, access='stream', form='unformatted', status='new', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'open failed'
   write(unit) 'Hello Fortran!'
   close(unit)
   if (.not. exists(filename) .or. .not. isfile(filename)) error stop 'file metadata failed'
   if (getsize(filename) /= 14) error stop 'file size failed'
   if (basename(filename) /= 'sample.txt') error stop 'basename failed'
   if (dirname(filename) /= folder) error stop 'dirname failed'
   if (normpath('os-demo/./nested/../nested') /= folder) error stop 'path normalization failed'
   print '(a,a)', 'Operating system: ', os_name
   print '(a,a,a,i0)', 'Created ', filename, ', bytes: ', getsize(filename)
   call rename(filename, renamed, stat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'rename failed'
   if (exists(filename) .or. .not. exists(renamed)) error stop 'rename metadata failed'
   call unlink(renamed, stat=status)
   if (status /= 0 .or. exists(renamed)) error stop 'unlink failed'
   call rmdir(folder, stat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'nested rmdir failed'
   call rmdir('os-demo', stat=status)
   if (status /= 0 .or. exists('os-demo')) error stop 'cleanup failed'
   print '(a)', 'PASS stdlib-os'
end program main

! Use a file-output device; this example needs no display or font files.
program main
   use M_draw, only: voutput, vinit, prefsize, ortho2, color, clear, move2, draw2, vexit, D_BLACK, D_BLUE
   implicit none
   integer :: i, unit, status, bytes, width, height, maximum, red, green, blue, blue_pixels
   real :: x, y
   character(len=2048) :: line
   call voutput('drawing.ppm')
   call prefsize(400, 300)
   call vinit('ppm')
   call ortho2(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0)
   call color(D_BLACK)
   call clear()
   call color(D_BLUE)
   call move2(0.0, 0.0)
   do i = 1, 20
      x = real(i)/20.0
      y = x*x
      call draw2(x, y)
   end do
   call vexit()
   inquire(file='drawing.ppm', size=bytes, iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0 .or. bytes < 100) error stop 'PPM file missing or empty'
   open(newunit=unit, file='drawing.ppm', status='old', action='read', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'PPM read failed'
   read(unit, '(a)') line
   if (trim(line) /= 'P3') error stop 'PPM format mismatch'
   call next_header_line()
   read(line, *) width, height
   if (width /= 400 .or. height /= 300) error stop 'PPM dimensions mismatch'
   call next_header_line()
   read(line, *) maximum
   if (maximum /= 255) error stop 'PPM color range mismatch'
   blue_pixels = 0
   do i = 1, width*height
      read(unit, *, iostat=status) red, green, blue
      if (status /= 0) error stop 'PPM pixel read failed'
      if (min(red,green,blue) < 0 .or. max(red,green,blue) > maximum) error stop 'PPM pixel range failed'
      if (blue > red .and. blue > green) blue_pixels = blue_pixels + 1
   end do
   close(unit)
   if (blue_pixels < 20) error stop 'Curve pixels missing'
   print '(a,i0,a,i0)', 'Generated drawing.ppm, bytes: ', bytes, ', blue pixels: ', blue_pixels
   print '(a)', 'Twenty-segment curve: y = x*x, 0 <= x <= 1'
   print '(a)', 'PASS m_draw'
contains
   subroutine next_header_line()
      do
         read(unit, '(a)', iostat=status) line
         if (status /= 0) error stop 'PPM header read failed'
         if (len_trim(line) == 0) cycle
         if (line(1:1) /= '#') exit
      end do
   end subroutine next_header_line
end program main

The X11 link dependency is retained but the checked main uses the PPM file driver, requiring no display server or Hershey font files. A 20-segment blue parabola is rendered with the PPM driver; the consumer checks P3 magic, image dimensions, color range, every pixel range and the presence of blue curve pixels. The ordinary image collector converts the generated PPM to a bounded PNG browser preview. The SVG driver aborted during font initialization when no Hershey fonts were supplied; no upstream driver code is patched, and the example uses PPM. Interactive drivers, all drawing primitives, software text/font setup and SVG output are not validated.

! Evaluate a Lua function with integer and real results, without external files.
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding, only: c_ptr, c_associated
   use lua
   implicit none
   type(c_ptr) :: state
   integer :: status, i
   integer(kind=lua_integer) :: square
   real(kind=lua_number) :: root
   state = lual_newstate()
   if (.not. c_associated(state)) error stop 'Lua allocation failed'
   call lual_openlibs(state)
   status = lual_loadstring(state, 'function calculate(x) return x*x, math.sqrt(x) end')
   if (status /= LUA_OK) error stop 'Lua parsing failed'
   status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0)
   if (status /= LUA_OK) error stop 'Lua definition failed'
   do i = 1, 4
      status = lua_getglobal(state, 'calculate')
      if (lua_isfunction(state, -1) /= 1) error stop 'Lua function missing'
      call lua_pushinteger(state, int(i, kind=lua_integer))
      status = lua_pcall(state, 1, 2, 0)
      if (status /= LUA_OK) error stop 'Lua call failed'
      square = lua_tointeger(state, -2)
      root = lua_tonumber(state, -1)
      if (square /= i*i) error stop 'integer result mismatch'
      if (abs(root - sqrt(real(i, lua_number))) > 1.0e-12_lua_number) error stop 'real result mismatch'
      print '(i2,a,i3,a,f12.8)', i, ': square = ', square, ', square root = ', root
      call lua_pop(state, 2)
      if (lua_gettop(state) /= 0) error stop 'Lua stack was not cleared'
   end do
   call lua_close(state)
   print '(a)', 'PASS fortran-lua53'
end program main

! A self-contained NetCDF classic write/read round trip.
program main
   use netcdf
   implicit none
   integer :: ncid, xdim, ydim, variable, dims(2), i, j, length, unit, status
   real :: values(3,2), loaded(3,2)
   character(len=20) :: units
   do j = 1, 2
      do i = 1, 3
         values(i,j) = real(i + 10*j)
      end do
   end do
   call check(nf90_create('dataset.nc', nf90_clobber, ncid))
   call check(nf90_def_dim(ncid, 'x', 3, xdim))
   call check(nf90_def_dim(ncid, 'y', 2, ydim))
   call check(nf90_def_var(ncid, 'temperature', nf90_float, [xdim,ydim], variable))
   call check(nf90_put_att(ncid, variable, 'units', 'degree_Celsius'))
   call check(nf90_enddef(ncid))
   call check(nf90_put_var(ncid, variable, values))
   call check(nf90_close(ncid))
   call check(nf90_open('dataset.nc', nf90_nowrite, ncid))
   call check(nf90_inq_varid(ncid, 'temperature', variable))
   call check(nf90_inquire_variable(ncid, variable, dimids=dims))
   call check(nf90_inquire_dimension(ncid, dims(1), len=length))
   if (length /= 3) error stop 'x dimension mismatch'
   call check(nf90_inquire_dimension(ncid, dims(2), len=length))
   if (length /= 2) error stop 'y dimension mismatch'
   call check(nf90_get_att(ncid, variable, 'units', units))
   if (trim(units) /= 'degree_Celsius') error stop 'attribute mismatch'
   call check(nf90_get_var(ncid, variable, loaded))
   if (any(abs(loaded-values) > 1.0e-6)) error stop 'array mismatch'
   call check(nf90_close(ncid))
   print '(a,a)', 'Units: ', trim(units)
   do j = 1, 2
      print '(3f8.1)', loaded(:,j)
   end do
   open(newunit=unit, file='dataset.nc', status='old', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'cleanup open failed'
   close(unit, status='delete')
   print '(a)', 'PASS netcdf-fortran'
contains
   subroutine check(code)
      integer, intent(in) :: code
      if (code /= nf90_noerr) then
         print '(a)', trim(nf90_strerror(code))
         error stop 'NetCDF operation failed'
      end if
   end subroutine check
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Selected serial classic-format Fortran sources follow the upstream CMake classic-library source set and use the unchanged public netCDF-C API. The operator-owned FPM wrapper retains original include files and sets HAVE_F2008, HAVE_TS29113_SUPPORT and NO_NETCDF_2 for the GNU 16 Linux environment; no library sources are edited. The native libnetcdf-dev package is locked to 1:4.9.3-1. The consumer writes a 3-by-2 real array and units attribute to a classic dataset, reopens it, checks dimension lengths, attribute and every value, then removes the file. NetCDF-4-specific Fortran interfaces, the old V2 API, parallel I/O and all data types are outside this selected build and verification scope. Source exports require the native netCDF C development library.

    !*****************************************************************************80
    !
    !! QC25C returns integration rules for Cauchy Principal Value integrals.
    !
    !  Discussion:
    !
    !    This routine estimates 
    !      I = integral of F(X) * W(X) over (a,b) 
    !    with error estimate, where 
    !      w(x) = 1/(x-c)
    !
    !  Author:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner
    !
    !  Reference:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner,
    !    QUADPACK, a Subroutine Package for Automatic Integration,
    !    Springer Verlag, 1983
    !
    !  Parameters:
    !
    !    Input, external real(8) :: F, the name of the function routine, of the form
    !      function f ( x )
    !      real(8) :: f
    !      real(8) :: x
    !    which evaluates the integrand function.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: A, B, the limits of integration.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: C, the parameter in the weight function.
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: RESULT, the estimated value of the integral.
    !    RESULT is computed by using a generalized Clenshaw-Curtis method if
    !    C lies within ten percent of the integration interval.  In the 
    !    other case the 15-point Kronrod rule obtained by optimal addition
    !    of abscissae to the 7-point Gauss rule, is applied.
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: ABSERR, an estimate of || I - RESULT ||.
    !
    !           krul   - integer
    !                    key which is decreased by 1 if the 15-point
    !                    Gauss-Kronrod scheme has been used
    !
    !    Output, integer NEVAL, the number of times the integral was evaluated.
    !
    !  Local parameters:
    !
    !           fval   - value of the function f at the points
    !                    cos(k*pi/24),  k = 0, ..., 24
    !           cheb12 - Chebyshev series expansion coefficients, for the
    !                    function f, of degree 12
    !           cheb24 - Chebyshev series expansion coefficients, for the
    !                    function f, of degree 24
    !           res12  - approximation to the integral corresponding to the
    !                    use of cheb12
    !           res24  - approximation to the integral corresponding to the
    !                    use of cheb24
    !           qwgtc  - external function subprogram defining the weight
    !                    function
    !           hlgth  - half-length of the interval
    !           centr  - mid point of the interval
    !
    implicit none

    real(8) :: a
    real(8) :: abserr
    real(8) :: ak22
    real(8) :: amom0
    real(8) :: amom1
    real(8) :: amom2
    real(8) :: b
    real(8) :: c
    real(8) :: cc
    real(8) :: centr
    real(8) :: cheb12(13)
    real(8) :: cheb24(25)
    real(8), external :: f
    real(8) :: fval(25)
    real(8) :: hlgth
    integer i
    integer isym
    integer k 
    integer kp
    integer krul
    integer neval
    real(8) :: p2
    real(8) :: p3
    real(8) :: p4
    real(8), external :: qwgtc
    real(8) :: resabs
    real(8) :: resasc
    real(8) :: result
    real(8) :: res12
    real(8) :: res24
    real(8) :: u
    real(8), parameter, dimension ( 11 ) :: x = (/ &
         9.914448613738104e-01, 9.659258262890683e-01, &
         9.238795325112868e-01, 8.660254037844386e-01, &
         7.933533402912352e-01, 7.071067811865475e-01, &
         6.087614290087206e-01, 5.000000000000000e-01, &
         3.826834323650898e-01, 2.588190451025208e-01, &
         1.305261922200516e-01 /)
    !
    !  Check the position of C.
    !
    cc = ( 2.0e+00 * c - b - a ) / ( b - a )
    !
    !  Apply the 15-point Gauss-Kronrod scheme.
    !
    if ( abs ( cc ) >= 1.1e+00 ) then
       krul = krul - 1
       call qk15w ( f, qwgtc, c, p2, p3, p4, kp, a, b, result, abserr, &
            resabs, resasc )
       neval = 15
       if ( resasc == abserr ) then
          krul = krul+1
       end if
       return
    end if
    !
    !  Use the generalized Clenshaw-Curtis method.
    !
    hlgth = 5.0e-01 * ( b - a )
    centr = 5.0e-01 * ( b + a )
    neval = 25
    fval(1) = 5.0e-01 * f(hlgth+centr)
    fval(13) = f(centr)
    fval(25) = 5.0e-01 * f(centr-hlgth)

    do i = 2, 12
       u = hlgth * x(i-1)
       isym = 26 - i
       fval(i) = f(u+centr)
       fval(isym) = f(centr-u)
    end do
    !
    !  Compute the Chebyshev series expansion.
    !
    call qcheb ( x, fval, cheb12, cheb24 )
    !
    !  The modified Chebyshev moments are computed by forward
    !  recursion, using AMOM0 and AMOM1 as starting values.
    !
    amom0 = log ( abs ( ( 1.0e+00 - cc ) / ( 1.0e+00 + cc ) ) )
    amom1 = 2.0e+00 + cc * amom0
    res12 = cheb12(1) * amom0 + cheb12(2) * amom1
    res24 = cheb24(1) * amom0 + cheb24(2) * amom1

    do k = 3, 13
       amom2 = 2.0e+00 * cc * amom1 - amom0
       ak22 = ( k - 2 ) * ( k - 2 )
       if ( ( k / 2 ) * 2 == k ) then
          amom2 = amom2 - 4.0e+00 / ( ak22 - 1.0e+00 )
       end if
       res12 = res12 + cheb12(k) * amom2
       res24 = res24 + cheb24(k) * amom2
       amom0 = amom1
       amom1 = amom2
    end do

    do k = 14, 25
       amom2 = 2.0e+00 * cc * amom1 - amom0
       ak22 = ( k - 2 ) * ( k - 2 )
       if ( ( k / 2 ) * 2 == k ) then
          amom2 = amom2 - 4.0e+00 / ( ak22 - 1.0e+00 )
       end if
       res24 = res24 + cheb24(k) * amom2
       amom0 = amom1
       amom1 = amom2
    end do

    result = res24
    abserr = abs ( res24 - res12 )

    return
  end subroutine qc25c

    !*****************************************************************************80
    !
    !! QC25O returns integration rules for integrands with a COS or SIN factor.
    !
    !  Discussion:
    !
    !    This routine estimates the integral
    !      I = integral of f(x) * w(x) over (a,b)
    !    where
    !      w(x) = cos(omega*x)
    !    or 
    !      w(x) = sin(omega*x),
    !    and estimates
    !      J = integral ( A <= X <= B ) |F(X)| dx.
    !

    !    Gauss-Kronrod rule is used.  In all other cases a generalized
    !    Clenshaw-Curtis method is used, that is, a truncated Chebyshev 
    !    expansion of the function F is computed on (a,b), so that the 
    !    integrand can be written as a sum of terms of the form W(X)*T(K,X), 
    !    where T(K,X) is the Chebyshev polynomial of degree K.  The Chebyshev
    !    moments are computed with use of a linear recurrence relation.
    !
    !  Author:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner
    !
    !  Reference:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner,
    !    QUADPACK, a Subroutine Package for Automatic Integration,
    !    Springer Verlag, 1983
    !
    !  Parameters:
    !
    !    Input, external real(8) :: F, the name of the function routine, of the form
    !      function f ( x )
    !      real(8) :: f
    !      real(8) :: x
    !    which evaluates the integrand function.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: A, B, the limits of integration.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: OMEGA, the parameter in the weight function.
    !
    !    Input, integer INTEGR, indicates which weight function is to be used
    !    = 1, w(x) = cos(omega*x)
    !    = 2, w(x) = sin(omega*x)
    !
    !    ?, integer NRMOM, the length of interval (a,b) is equal to the length
    !    of the original integration interval divided by
    !    2**nrmom (we suppose that the routine is used in an
    !    adaptive integration process, otherwise set
    !    nrmom = 0).  nrmom must be zero at the first call.
    !
    !           maxp1  - integer
    !                    gives an upper bound on the number of Chebyshev
    !                    moments which can be stored, i.e. for the intervals
    !                    of lengths abs(bb-aa)*2**(-l), l = 0,1,2, ...,
    !                    maxp1-2.
    !
    !           ksave  - integer
    !                    key which is one when the moments for the
    !                    current interval have been computed
    !

    !

    !                    error, which should equal or exceed abs(i-result)

    !                    been computed. if nrmom < momcom or ksave = 1,

    !                    have already been computed and stored, otherwise

    !           chebmo - real

    !                    Chebyshev series expansion of degree 24

    !           ress24 - the analogue of resc24 for the sine
    !

    integer maxp1

    real(8) :: a
    real(8) :: abserr
    real(8) :: ac
    real(8) :: an
    real(8) :: an2
    real(8) :: as
    real(8) :: asap
    real(8) :: ass
    real(8) :: b

    real(8) :: cons
    real(8) :: cospar

    real(8) :: d1(28)
    real(8) :: d2(28)
    real(8) :: d3(28)
    real(8) :: estc
    real(8) :: ests
    real(8), external :: f
    real(8) :: fval(25)
    real(8) :: hlgth

    integer integr
    integer isym
    integer j
    integer k
    integer ksave
    integer m
    integer momcom
    integer neval
    integer, parameter :: nmac = 28
    integer noeq1
    integer noequ

    real(8) :: parint
    real(8) :: par2
    real(8) :: par22
    real(8) :: p2
    real(8) :: p3
    real(8) :: p4

    real(8) :: resasc
    real(8) :: resc12
    real(8) :: resc24
    real(8) :: ress12
    real(8) :: ress24
    real(8) :: result
    real(8) :: sinpar
    real(8) :: v(28)
    real(8), dimension ( 11 ) :: x = (/ &
         9.914448613738104e-01,     9.659258262890683e-01, &
         9.238795325112868e-01,     8.660254037844386e-01, &
         7.933533402912352e-01,     7.071067811865475e-01, &

         3.826834323650898e-01,     2.588190451025208e-01, &
