    dhlgth = abs(hlgth)
    !
    !  Compute the 15-point Kronrod approximation to the integral,
    !  and estimate the error.
    !
    fc = f(centr)*w(centr,p1,p2,p3,p4,kp)
    resg = wg(4)*fc
    resk = wgk(8)*fc
    resabs = abs(resk)

    do j = 1, 3
       jtw = j*2
       absc = hlgth*xgk(jtw)
       absc1 = centr-absc
       absc2 = centr+absc
       fval1 = f(absc1)*w(absc1,p1,p2,p3,p4,kp)
       fval2 = f(absc2)*w(absc2,p1,p2,p3,p4,kp)
       fv1(jtw) = fval1
       fv2(jtw) = fval2
       fsum = fval1+fval2
       resg = resg+wg(j)*fsum
       resk = resk+wgk(jtw)*fsum
       resabs = resabs+wgk(jtw)*(abs(fval1)+abs(fval2))
    end do

    do j = 1, 4
       jtwm1 = j*2-1
       absc = hlgth*xgk(jtwm1)
       absc1 = centr-absc
       absc2 = centr+absc
       fval1 = f(absc1)*w(absc1,p1,p2,p3,p4,kp)
       fval2 = f(absc2)*w(absc2,p1,p2,p3,p4,kp)
       fv1(jtwm1) = fval1
       fv2(jtwm1) = fval2
       fsum = fval1+fval2
       resk = resk+wgk(jtwm1)*fsum
       resabs = resabs+wgk(jtwm1)*(abs(fval1)+abs(fval2))
    end do

    reskh = resk*5.0e-01
    resasc = wgk(8)*abs(fc-reskh)

    do j = 1, 7
       resasc = resasc+wgk(j)*(abs(fv1(j)-reskh)+abs(fv2(j)-reskh))
    end do

    result = resk*hlgth
    resabs = resabs*dhlgth
    resasc = resasc*dhlgth
    abserr = abs((resk-resg)*hlgth)

    if ( resasc /= 0.0e+00.and.abserr /= 0.0e+00) then
       abserr = resasc*min ( 1.0e+00,(2.0e+02*abserr/resasc)**1.5e+00)
    end if

    if ( resabs > tiny ( resabs ) /(5.0e+01* epsilon ( resabs ) ) ) then
       abserr = max ( ( epsilon ( resabs ) * 5.0e+01)*resabs,abserr)
    end if

    return
  end subroutine qk15w
  subroutine qk21 ( f, a, b, result, abserr, resabs, resasc )

    !*****************************************************************************80
    !
    !! QK21 carries out a 21 point Gauss-Kronrod quadrature rule.
    !
    !  Discussion:
    !
    !    This routine approximates
    !      I = integral ( A <= X <= B ) F(X) dx
    !    with an error estimate, and
    !      J = integral ( A <= X <= B ) | F(X) | dx
    !
    !  Author:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner
    !
    !  Reference:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner,
    !    QUADPACK, a Subroutine Package for Automatic Integration,
    !    Springer Verlag, 1983
    !
    !  Parameters:
    !
    !    Input, external real(8) :: F, the name of the function routine, of the form
    !      function f ( x )
    !      real(8) :: f
    !      real(8) :: x
    !    which evaluates the integrand function.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: A, B, the limits of integration.
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: RESULT, the estimated value of the integral.
    !    RESULT is computed by applying the 21-point Kronrod rule (resk) 
    !    obtained by optimal addition of abscissae to the 10-point Gauss 
    !    rule (resg).
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: ABSERR, an estimate of | I - RESULT |.
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: RESABS, approximation to the integral of the absolute
    !    value of F.
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: RESASC, approximation to the integral | F-I/(B-A) | 
    !    over [A,B].
    !
    implicit none

    real(8) :: a
    real(8) :: absc
    real(8) :: abserr
    real(8) :: b
    real(8) :: centr
    real(8) :: dhlgth
    real(8), external :: f
    real(8) :: fc
    real(8) :: fsum
    real(8) :: fval1
    real(8) :: fval2
    real(8) :: fv1(10)
    real(8) :: fv2(10)
    real(8) :: hlgth
    integer j
    integer jtw
    integer jtwm1
    real(8) :: resabs
    real(8) :: resasc
    real(8) :: resg
    real(8) :: resk
    real(8) :: reskh
    real(8) :: result
    real(8) :: wg(5)
    real(8) :: wgk(11)
    real(8) :: xgk(11)
    !
    !           the abscissae and weights are given for the interval (-1,1).
    !           because of symmetry only the positive abscissae and their
    !           corresponding weights are given.
    !
    !           xgk    - abscissae of the 21-point Kronrod rule
    !                    xgk(2), xgk(4), ...  abscissae of the 10-point
    !                    Gauss rule
    !                    xgk(1), xgk(3), ...  abscissae which are optimally
    !                    added to the 10-point Gauss rule
    !
    !           wgk    - weights of the 21-point Kronrod rule
    !
    !           wg     - weights of the 10-point Gauss rule
    !
    data xgk(1),xgk(2),xgk(3),xgk(4),xgk(5),xgk(6),xgk(7),xgk(8), &
         xgk(9),xgk(10),xgk(11)/ &
         9.956571630258081d-01,     9.739065285171717d-01, &
         9.301574913557082d-01,     8.650633666889845d-01, &
         7.808177265864169d-01,     6.794095682990244d-01, &
         5.627571346686047d-01,     4.333953941292472d-01, &
         2.943928627014602d-01,     1.488743389816312d-01, &
         0.000000000000000d+00/
    !
    data wgk(1),wgk(2),wgk(3),wgk(4),wgk(5),wgk(6),wgk(7),wgk(8), &
         wgk(9),wgk(10),wgk(11)/ &
         1.169463886737187d-02,     3.255816230796473d-02, &
         5.475589657435200d-02,     7.503967481091995d-02, &
         9.312545458369761d-02,     1.093871588022976d-01, &
         1.234919762620659d-01,     1.347092173114733d-01, &
         1.427759385770601d-01,     1.477391049013385d-01, &
         1.494455540029169d-01/
    !
    data wg(1),wg(2),wg(3),wg(4),wg(5)/ &
         6.667134430868814d-02,     1.494513491505806d-01, &
         2.190863625159820d-01,     2.692667193099964d-01, &
         2.955242247147529d-01/
    !
    !
    !           list of major variables
    !
    !           centr  - mid point of the interval
    !           hlgth  - half-length of the interval
    !           absc   - abscissa
    !           fval*  - function value
    !           resg   - result of the 10-point Gauss formula
    !           resk   - result of the 21-point Kronrod formula
    !           reskh  - approximation to the mean value of f over (a,b),
    !                    i.e. to i/(b-a)
    !
    centr = 5.0e-01*(a+b)
    hlgth = 5.0e-01*(b-a)
    dhlgth = abs(hlgth)
    !
    !  Compute the 21-point Kronrod approximation to the
    !  integral, and estimate the absolute error.
    !
    resg = 0.0e+00
    fc = f(centr)
    resk = wgk(11)*fc
    resabs = abs(resk)

    do j = 1, 5
       jtw = 2*j
       absc = hlgth*xgk(jtw)
       fval1 = f(centr-absc)
       fval2 = f(centr+absc)
       fv1(jtw) = fval1
       fv2(jtw) = fval2
       fsum = fval1+fval2
       resg = resg+wg(j)*fsum
       resk = resk+wgk(jtw)*fsum
       resabs = resabs+wgk(jtw)*(abs(fval1)+abs(fval2))
    end do

    do j = 1, 5
       jtwm1 = 2*j-1
       absc = hlgth*xgk(jtwm1)
       fval1 = f(centr-absc)
       fval2 = f(centr+absc)
       fv1(jtwm1) = fval1
       fv2(jtwm1) = fval2
       fsum = fval1+fval2
       resk = resk+wgk(jtwm1)*fsum
       resabs = resabs+wgk(jtwm1)*(abs(fval1)+abs(fval2))
    end do

    reskh = resk*5.0e-01
    resasc = wgk(11)*abs(fc-reskh)

    do j = 1, 10
       resasc = resasc+wgk(j)*(abs(fv1(j)-reskh)+abs(fv2(j)-reskh))
    end do

    result = resk*hlgth
    resabs = resabs*dhlgth
    resasc = resasc*dhlgth
    abserr = abs((resk-resg)*hlgth)

    if ( resasc /= 0.0e+00.and.abserr /= 0.0e+00) then
       abserr = resasc*min ( 1.0e+00,(2.0e+02*abserr/resasc)**1.5e+00)
    end if

    if ( resabs > tiny ( resabs ) /(5.0e+01* epsilon ( resabs ) )) then
       abserr = max (( epsilon ( resabs ) *5.0e+01)*resabs,abserr)
    end if

    return
  end subroutine qk21

    data xgk(1),xgk(2),xgk(3),xgk(4),xgk(5),xgk(6),xgk(7),xgk(8), &

    real(8) :: b
    real(8) :: centr
    real(8) :: dhlgth
    real(8), external :: f
    real(8) :: fc
    real(8) :: fsum
    real(8) :: fval1
    real(8) :: fval2
    real(8) :: fv1(30)
    real(8) :: fv2(30)
    real(8) :: hlgth
    integer j
    integer jtw
    integer jtwm1
    real(8) :: resabs
    real(8) :: resasc
    real(8) :: resg
    real(8) :: resk
    real(8) :: reskh
    real(8) :: result
    real(8) :: wg(15)
    real(8) :: wgk(31)
    real(8) :: xgk(31)
    !
    !           the abscissae and weights are given for the
    !           interval (-1,1). because of symmetry only the positive
    !           abscissae and their corresponding weights are given.
    !
    !           xgk   - abscissae of the 61-point Kronrod rule
    !                   xgk(2), xgk(4)  ... abscissae of the 30-point
    !                   Gauss rule
    !                   xgk(1), xgk(3)  ... optimally added abscissae
    !                   to the 30-point Gauss rule
    !
    !           wgk   - weights of the 61-point Kronrod rule
    !
    !           wg    - weigths of the 30-point Gauss rule
    !
    data xgk(1),xgk(2),xgk(3),xgk(4),xgk(5),xgk(6),xgk(7),xgk(8), &
         xgk(9),xgk(10)/ &
         9.994844100504906d-01,     9.968934840746495d-01, &
         9.916309968704046d-01,     9.836681232797472d-01, &
         9.731163225011263d-01,     9.600218649683075d-01, &
         9.443744447485600d-01,     9.262000474292743d-01, &
         9.055733076999078d-01,     8.825605357920527d-01/
    data xgk(11),xgk(12),xgk(13),xgk(14),xgk(15),xgk(16),xgk(17), &
         xgk(18),xgk(19),xgk(20)/ &
         8.572052335460611d-01,     8.295657623827684d-01, &
         7.997278358218391d-01,     7.677774321048262d-01, &
         7.337900624532268d-01,     6.978504947933158d-01, &
         6.600610641266270d-01,     6.205261829892429d-01, &
         5.793452358263617d-01,     5.366241481420199d-01/
    data xgk(21),xgk(22),xgk(23),xgk(24),xgk(25),xgk(26),xgk(27), &
         xgk(28),xgk(29),xgk(30),xgk(31)/ &
         4.924804678617786d-01,     4.470337695380892d-01, &
         4.004012548303944d-01,     3.527047255308781d-01, &
         3.040732022736251d-01,     2.546369261678898d-01, &
         2.045251166823099d-01,     1.538699136085835d-01, &
         1.028069379667370d-01,     5.147184255531770d-02, &
         0.0e+00                   /
    data wgk(1),wgk(2),wgk(3),wgk(4),wgk(5),wgk(6),wgk(7),wgk(8), &
         wgk(9),wgk(10)/ &
         1.389013698677008d-03,     3.890461127099884d-03, &
         6.630703915931292d-03,     9.273279659517763d-03, &
         1.182301525349634d-02,     1.436972950704580d-02, &
         1.692088918905327d-02,     1.941414119394238d-02, &
         2.182803582160919d-02,     2.419116207808060d-02/
    data wgk(11),wgk(12),wgk(13),wgk(14),wgk(15),wgk(16),wgk(17), &
         wgk(18),wgk(19),wgk(20)/ &
         2.650995488233310d-02,     2.875404876504129d-02, &
         3.090725756238776d-02,     3.298144705748373d-02, &
         3.497933802806002d-02,     3.688236465182123d-02, &
         3.867894562472759d-02,     4.037453895153596d-02, &
         4.196981021516425d-02,     4.345253970135607d-02/
    data wgk(21),wgk(22),wgk(23),wgk(24),wgk(25),wgk(26),wgk(27), &
         wgk(28),wgk(29),wgk(30),wgk(31)/ &
         4.481480013316266d-02,     4.605923827100699d-02, &
         4.718554656929915d-02,     4.818586175708713d-02, &
         4.905543455502978d-02,     4.979568342707421d-02, &
         5.040592140278235d-02,     5.088179589874961d-02, &
         5.122154784925877d-02,     5.142612853745903d-02, &
         5.149472942945157d-02/
    data wg(1),wg(2),wg(3),wg(4),wg(5),wg(6),wg(7),wg(8)/ &
         7.968192496166606d-03,     1.846646831109096d-02, &
         2.878470788332337d-02,     3.879919256962705d-02, &
         4.840267283059405d-02,     5.749315621761907d-02, &
         6.597422988218050d-02,     7.375597473770521d-02/
    data wg(9),wg(10),wg(11),wg(12),wg(13),wg(14),wg(15)/ &
         8.075589522942022d-02,     8.689978720108298d-02, &
         9.212252223778613d-02,     9.636873717464426d-02, &
         9.959342058679527d-02,     1.017623897484055d-01, &
         1.028526528935588d-01/

    centr = 5.0e-01*(b+a)
    hlgth = 5.0e-01*(b-a)
    dhlgth = abs(hlgth)
    !
    !  Compute the 61-point Kronrod approximation to the integral,
    !  and estimate the absolute error.
    !
    resg = 0.0e+00
    fc = f(centr)
    resk = wgk(31)*fc
    resabs = abs(resk)

    do j = 1, 15
       jtw = j*2
       absc = hlgth*xgk(jtw)
       fval1 = f(centr-absc)
       fval2 = f(centr+absc)
       fv1(jtw) = fval1
       fv2(jtw) = fval2
       fsum = fval1+fval2
       resg = resg+wg(j)*fsum
       resk = resk+wgk(jtw)*fsum
       resabs = resabs+wgk(jtw)*(abs(fval1)+abs(fval2))
    end do

    do j = 1, 15
       jtwm1 = j*2-1
       absc = hlgth*xgk(jtwm1)
       fval1 = f(centr-absc)
       fval2 = f(centr+absc)
       fv1(jtwm1) = fval1
       fv2(jtwm1) = fval2
       fsum = fval1+fval2
       resk = resk+wgk(jtwm1)*fsum
       resabs = resabs+wgk(jtwm1)*(abs(fval1)+abs(fval2))
    end do

    reskh = resk * 5.0e-01
    resasc = wgk(31)*abs(fc-reskh)

    do j = 1, 30
       resasc = resasc+wgk(j)*(abs(fv1(j)-reskh)+abs(fv2(j)-reskh))
    end do

    result = resk*hlgth
    resabs = resabs*dhlgth
    resasc = resasc*dhlgth
    abserr = abs((resk-resg)*hlgth)

    if ( resasc /= 0.0e+00 .and. abserr /= 0.0e+00) then
       abserr = resasc*min ( 1.0e+00,(2.0e+02*abserr/resasc)**1.5e+00)
    end if

    if ( resabs > tiny ( resabs ) / (5.0e+01* epsilon ( resabs ) )) then
       abserr = max ( ( epsilon ( resabs ) *5.0e+01)*resabs, abserr )
    end if

    return
  end subroutine qk61
  subroutine qmomo ( alfa, beta, ri, rj, rg, rh, integr )

    !*****************************************************************************80
    !
    !! QMOMO computes modified Chebyshev moments.
    !
    !  Discussion:
    !
    !    This routine computes modified Chebyshev moments.
    !    The K-th modified Chebyshev moment is defined as the
    !    integral over (-1,1) of W(X)*T(K,X), where T(K,X) is the
    !    Chebyshev polynomial of degree K.
    !
    !  Author:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner
    !
    !  Reference:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner,
    !    QUADPACK, a Subroutine Package for Automatic Integration,
    !    Springer Verlag, 1983
    !
    !  Parameters:
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: ALFA, a parameter in the weight function w(x), ALFA > -1.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: BETA, a parameter in the weight function w(x), BETA > -1.
    !
    !           ri     - real
    !                    vector of dimension 25
    !                    ri(k) is the integral over (-1,1) of
    !                    (1+x)**alfa*t(k-1,x), k = 1, ..., 25.
    !
    !           rj     - real
    !                    vector of dimension 25
    !                    rj(k) is the integral over (-1,1) of
    !                    (1-x)**beta*t(k-1,x), k = 1, ..., 25.
    !
    !           rg     - real
    !                    vector of dimension 25
    !                    rg(k) is the integral over (-1,1) of
    !                    (1+x)**alfa*log((1+x)/2)*t(k-1,x), k = 1, ...,25.
    !
    !           rh     - real
    !                    vector of dimension 25
    !                    rh(k) is the integral over (-1,1) of
    !                    (1-x)**beta*log((1-x)/2)*t(k-1,x), k = 1, ..., 25.
    !
    !           integr - integer
    !                    input parameter indicating the modified moments
    !                    to be computed
    !                    integr = 1 compute ri, rj
    !                           = 2 compute ri, rj, rg
    !                           = 3 compute ri, rj, rh
    !                           = 4 compute ri, rj, rg, rh
    !
    implicit none

    real(8) :: alfa
    real(8) :: alfp1
    real(8) :: alfp2
    real(8) :: an
    real(8) :: anm1
    real(8) :: beta
    real(8) :: betp1
    real(8) :: betp2
    integer i
    integer im1
    integer integr
    real(8) :: ralf
    real(8) :: rbet
    real(8) :: rg(25)
    real(8) :: rh(25)
    real(8) :: ri(25)
    real(8) :: rj(25)
    !
    alfp1 = alfa+1.0e+00
    betp1 = beta+1.0e+00
    alfp2 = alfa+2.0e+00
    betp2 = beta+2.0e+00
    ralf = 2.0e+00**alfp1
    rbet = 2.0e+00**betp1
    !
    !  Compute RI, RJ using a forward recurrence relation.
    !
    ri(1) = ralf/alfp1
    rj(1) = rbet/betp1
    ri(2) = ri(1)*alfa/alfp2
    rj(2) = rj(1)*beta/betp2
    an = 2.0e+00
    anm1 = 1.0e+00

    do i = 3, 25
       ri(i) = -(ralf+an*(an-alfp2)*ri(i-1))/(anm1*(an+alfp1))
       rj(i) = -(rbet+an*(an-betp2)*rj(i-1))/(anm1*(an+betp1))
       anm1 = an
       an = an+1.0e+00
    end do

    if ( integr == 1 ) go to 70
    if ( integr == 3 ) go to 40
    !
    !  Compute RG using a forward recurrence relation.
    !
    rg(1) = -ri(1)/alfp1
    rg(2) = -(ralf+ralf)/(alfp2*alfp2)-rg(1)
    an = 2.0e+00
    anm1 = 1.0e+00
    im1 = 2

    do i = 3, 25
       rg(i) = -(an*(an-alfp2)*rg(im1)-an*ri(im1)+anm1*ri(i))/ &
            (anm1*(an+alfp1))
       anm1 = an
       an = an+1.0e+00
       im1 = i
    end do

    if ( integr == 2 ) go to 70
    !
    !  Compute RH using a forward recurrence relation.
    !
40  continue

    rh(1) = -rj(1) / betp1
    rh(2) = -(rbet+rbet)/(betp2*betp2)-rh(1)
    an = 2.0e+00
    anm1 = 1.0e+00
    im1 = 2

    do i = 3, 25
       rh(i) = -(an*(an-betp2)*rh(im1)-an*rj(im1)+ &
            anm1*rj(i))/(anm1*(an+betp1))
       anm1 = an
       an = an+1.0e+00
       im1 = i
    end do

    do i = 2, 25, 2
       rh(i) = -rh(i)
    end do

70  continue

    do i = 2, 25, 2
       rj(i) = -rj(i)
    end do

    !  90 continue

    return
  end subroutine qmomo
  subroutine qsort ( limit, last, maxerr, ermax, elist, iord, nrmax )

    !*****************************************************************************80
    !
    !! QSORT maintains the order of a list of local error estimates.
    !
    !  Discussion:
    !
    !    This routine maintains the descending ordering in the list of the 
    !    local error estimates resulting from the interval subdivision process. 
    !    At each call two error estimates are inserted using the sequential 
    !    search top-down for the largest error estimate and bottom-up for the
    !    smallest error estimate.
    !
    !  Author:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner
    !
    !  Reference:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner,
    !    QUADPACK, a Subroutine Package for Automatic Integration,
    !    Springer Verlag, 1983
    !
    !  Parameters:
    !
    !    Input, integer LIMIT, the maximum number of error estimates the list can
    !    contain.
    !
    !    Input, integer LAST, the current number of error estimates.
    !
    !    Input/output, integer MAXERR, the index in the list of the NRMAX-th 
    !    largest error.
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: ERMAX, the NRMAX-th largest error = ELIST(MAXERR).
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: ELIST(LIMIT), contains the error estimates.
    !
    !    Input/output, integer IORD(LAST).  The first K elements contain 
    !    pointers to the error estimates such that ELIST(IORD(1)) through
    !    ELIST(IORD(K)) form a decreasing sequence, with
    !      K = LAST 
    !    if 
    !      LAST <= (LIMIT/2+2), 
    !    and otherwise
    !      K = LIMIT+1-LAST.
    !
    !    Input/output, integer NRMAX.
    !
    implicit none

    integer last

    real(8) :: elist(last)
    real(8) :: ermax
    real(8) :: errmax
    real(8) :: errmin
    integer i
    integer ibeg
    integer iord(last)
    integer isucc
    integer j
    integer jbnd
    integer jupbn
    integer k
    integer limit
    integer maxerr
    integer nrmax
    !
    !  Check whether the list contains more than two error estimates.
    !
    if ( last <= 2 ) then
       iord(1) = 1
       iord(2) = 2
       go to 90
    end if
    !
    !  This part of the routine is only executed if, due to a
    !  difficult integrand, subdivision increased the error
    !  estimate. in the normal case the insert procedure should
    !  start after the nrmax-th largest error estimate.
    !
    errmax = elist(maxerr)

    do i = 1, nrmax-1

       isucc = iord(nrmax-1)

       if ( errmax <= elist(isucc) ) then
          exit
       end if

       iord(nrmax) = isucc
       nrmax = nrmax-1

    end do
    !
    !  Compute the number of elements in the list to be maintained
    !  in descending order.  This number depends on the number of
    !  subdivisions still allowed.
    !
    jupbn = last

    if ( (limit/2+2) < last ) then
       jupbn = limit+3-last
    end if

    errmin = elist(last)
    !
    !  Insert errmax by traversing the list top-down, starting
    !  comparison from the element elist(iord(nrmax+1)).
    !
    jbnd = jupbn-1
    ibeg = nrmax+1

    do i = ibeg, jbnd
       isucc = iord(i)
       if ( elist(isucc) <= errmax ) then
          go to 60
       end if
       iord(i-1) = isucc
    end do

    iord(jbnd) = maxerr
    iord(jupbn) = last
    go to 90
    !
    !  Insert errmin by traversing the list bottom-up.
    !
60  continue

    iord(i-1) = maxerr
    k = jbnd

    do j = i, jbnd
       isucc = iord(k)
       if ( errmin < elist(isucc) ) then
          go to 80
       end if
       iord(k+1) = isucc
       k = k-1
    end do

    iord(i) = last
    go to 90

80  continue

    iord(k+1) = last
    !
    !  Set maxerr and ermax.
    !
90  continue

    maxerr = iord(nrmax)
    ermax = elist(maxerr)

    return
  end subroutine qsort
  function qwgtc ( x, c, p2, p3, p4, kp )

    !*****************************************************************************80
    !
    !! QWGTC defines the weight function used by QC25C.
    !
    !  Discussion:
    !
    !    The weight function has the form 1 / ( X - C ).
    !
    !  Author:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner
    !
    !  Reference:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner,
    !    QUADPACK, a Subroutine Package for Automatic Integration,
    !    Springer Verlag, 1983
    !
    !  Parameters:
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: X, the point at which the weight function is evaluated.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: C, the location of the singularity.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: P2, P3, P4, parameters that are not used.
    !
    !    Input, integer KP, a parameter that is not used.
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: QWGTC, the value of the weight function at X.
    !
    implicit none

    real(8) :: c
    integer kp
    real(8) :: p2
    real(8) :: p3
    real(8) :: p4
    real(8) :: qwgtc
    real(8) :: x

    qwgtc = 1.0E+00 / ( x - c )

    return
  end function qwgtc
  function qwgto ( x, omega, p2, p3, p4, integr )

    !*****************************************************************************80
    !
    !! QWGTO defines the weight functions used by QC25O.
    !
    !  Author:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner
    !
    !  Reference:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner,
    !    QUADPACK, a Subroutine Package for Automatic Integration,
    !    Springer Verlag, 1983
    !
    !  Parameters:
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: X, the point at which the weight function is evaluated.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: OMEGA, the factor multiplying X.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: P2, P3, P4, parameters that are not used.
    !
    !    Input, integer INTEGR, specifies which weight function is used:
    !    1. W(X) = cos ( OMEGA * X )
    !    2, W(X) = sin ( OMEGA * X )
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: QWGTO, the value of the weight function at X.
    !
    implicit none

    integer integr
    real(8) :: omega
    real(8) :: p2
    real(8) :: p3
    real(8) :: p4
    real(8) :: qwgto
    real(8) :: x

    if ( integr == 1 ) then
       qwgto = cos ( omega * x )
    else if ( integr == 2 ) then
       qwgto = sin ( omega * x )
    end if

    return
  end function qwgto
  function qwgts ( x, a, b, alfa, beta, integr )

    !*****************************************************************************80
    !
    !! QWGTS defines the weight functions used by QC25S.
    !
    !  Author:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner
    !
    !  Reference:
    !
    !    Robert Piessens, Elise de Doncker-Kapenger, 
    !    Christian Ueberhuber, David Kahaner,
    !    QUADPACK, a Subroutine Package for Automatic Integration,
    !    Springer Verlag, 1983
    !
    !  Parameters:
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: X, the point at which the weight function is evaluated.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: A, B, the endpoints of the integration interval.
    !
    !    Input, real(8) :: ALFA, BETA, exponents that occur in the weight function.
    !
    !    Input, integer INTEGR, specifies which weight function is used:
    !    1. W(X) = (X-A)**ALFA * (B-X)**BETA
    !    2, W(X) = (X-A)**ALFA * (B-X)**BETA * log (X-A)
    !    3, W(X) = (X-A)**ALFA * (B-X)**BETA * log (B-X)
    !    4, W(X) = (X-A)**ALFA * (B-X)**BETA * log (X-A) * log(B-X)
    !
    !    Output, real(8) :: QWGTS, the value of the weight function at X.
    !
    implicit none

    real(8) :: a
    real(8) :: alfa
    real(8) :: b
    real(8) :: beta
    integer integr
    real(8) :: qwgts
    real(8) :: x

    if ( integr == 1 ) then
       qwgts = ( x - a )**alfa * ( b - x )**beta
    else if ( integr == 2 ) then
       qwgts = ( x - a )**alfa * ( b - x )**beta * log ( x - a )
    else if ( integr == 3 ) then
       qwgts = ( x - a )**alfa * ( b - x )**beta * log ( b - x )
    else if ( integr == 4 ) then
       qwgts = ( x - a )**alfa * ( b - x )**beta * log ( x - a ) * log ( b - x )
    end if

    return
  end function qwgts

subroutine qng ( f, a, b, epsabs, epsrel, result, abserr, neval, ier )
  !*****************************************************************************80
  !! QNG estimates an integral, using non-adaptive integration.
  !  Discussion:
  !
  !    The routine calculates an approximation RESULT to a definite integral   
  !      I = integral of F over (A,B),
  !    hopefully satisfying
  !      || I - RESULT || <= max ( EPSABS, EPSREL * ||I|| ).
  !
  !    The routine is a simple non-adaptive automatic integrator, based on
  !    a sequence of rules with increasing degree of algebraic
  !    precision (Patterson, 1968).
  !
  !
  !  Parameters:
  !
  !    Input, external real(8) :: F, the name of the function routine, of the form
  !      function f ( x )
  !      real(8) :: f
  !      real(8) :: x
  !    which evaluates the integrand function.
  !
  !    Input, real(8) :: A, B, the limits of integration.
  !
  !    Input, real(8) :: EPSABS, EPSREL, the absolute and relative accuracy requested.
  !
  !    Output, real(8) :: RESULT, the estimated value of the integral.
  !    RESULT is obtained by applying the 21-point Gauss-Kronrod rule (RES21)
  !    obtained  by optimal addition of abscissae to the 10-point Gauss rule
  !    (RES10), or by applying the 43-point rule (RES43) obtained by optimal
  !    addition of abscissae to the 21-point Gauss-Kronrod rule, or by 
  !    applying the 87-point rule (RES87) obtained by optimal addition of

     end if

! Selected SciFortran integration modules: no MPI or external datasets.
module scifortran_demo_functions
   implicit none
contains
   real(8) function integrand(t)
      real(8) :: t
      integrand = exp(t)
   end function integrand
   real(8) function decay(t)
      real(8) :: t
      decay = exp(-t)
   end function decay
end module scifortran_demo_functions

program main
   use scifortran_demo_functions, only: integrand, decay
   use SF_INTEGRATE, only: simps, trapz, quad
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 101
   integer :: i, key
   real(8) :: x(n), values(n), simpson, trapezoid, adaptive, infinite, rules(6)
   do i = 1, n
      x(i) = real(i-1,8)/real(n-1,8)
   end do
   values = x**3
   simpson = simps(values, 0.0d0, 1.0d0)
   trapezoid = trapz(values, 0.0d0, 1.0d0)
   call quad(integrand, 0.0d0, 1.0d0, epsabs=1.0d-11, epsrel=1.0d-11, result=adaptive)
   call quad(decay, 0.0d0, inf=1, epsabs=1.0d-11, epsrel=1.0d-11, result=infinite)
   do key = 1, 6
      call quad(integrand, 0.0d0, 1.0d0, key=key, epsabs=1.0d-11, epsrel=1.0d-11, result=rules(key))
   end do
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite([simpson,trapezoid,adaptive,infinite]))) error stop 'Nonfinite integral'
   if (abs(simpson-0.25d0) > 1.0d-12) error stop 'Simpson cubic integral failed'
   if (abs(trapezoid-0.25d0) > 3.0d-5) error stop 'Trapezoidal integral failed'
   if (abs(adaptive-(exp(1.0d0)-1.0d0)) > 1.0d-10) error stop 'Finite adaptive integral failed'
   if (abs(infinite-1.0d0) > 1.0d-10) error stop 'Infinite adaptive integral failed'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(rules))) error stop 'Nonfinite Gauss-Kronrod result'
   if (any(abs(rules-(exp(1.0d0)-1.0d0)) > 1.0d-10)) error stop 'Gauss-Kronrod rule failed'
   print '(a,f16.12)', 'Simpson integral of x**3 on [0,1]: ', simpson
   print '(a,f16.12)', 'Trapezoid integral:                ', trapezoid
   print '(a,f16.12)', 'Integral of exp(x) on [0,1]:        ', adaptive
   print '(a,f16.12)', 'Integral of exp(-x) on [0,infinity):', infinite
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum error for six Gauss-Kronrod rules: ', maxval(abs(rules-(exp(1.0d0)-1.0d0)))
   print '(a)', 'PASS scifortran'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: Selected integration subset, explicitly labeled in the menu: SF_INTEGRATE, GAUSS_QUADRATURE and standalone bundled QUADPACK procedures. Original include files remain in their source directories and the operator FPM wrapper compiles only the listed library files. Checksum-guarded edits promote 478 long coefficient literals from E to D exponents in DATA statements and REAL(8) PARAMETER array initializers in two bundled QUADPACK files. Each target array is checked to be REAL(8), and all decimal digits are retained. This avoids evaluating the supplied coefficients at default-real precision before assignment to double precision; formulas and the default-real compiler mode are unchanged. The linked quadrature-fortran BSD-3-Clause notice is restored as comments in GAUSS_QUADRATURE so source exports retain it. The consumer checks the Simpson and trapezoidal integrals of a sampled cubic against 1/4, adaptive integration of exp(x) over [0,1] against e-1 and exp(-x) over [0,infinity) against 1, and rejects nonfinite results. All six finite-interval Gauss-Kronrod rule choices are also checked against e-1. The example uses module callbacks: an initial consumer with internal callbacks segfaulted in the sandbox. Other SciFortran modules, MPI, linear algebra, the SCIFOR umbrella module, multidimensional/vector quadrature and all integration options are outside this selected build and verification scope.

! Python and NumPy are installed in the playground sandbox.
! Locally, link with the flags from: python3-config --embed --ldflags
program main
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use forpy_mod
   implicit none
   type(module_py) :: numpy, linalg
   type(ndarray) :: array
   type(tuple) :: arguments
   type(object) :: result
   real(real64) :: values(2,3), total, norm
   values = reshape([1.0_real64,2.0_real64,3.0_real64,4.0_real64,5.0_real64,6.0_real64], [2,3])
   call check(forpy_initialize())
   call check(import_py(numpy, 'numpy'))
   call check(import_py(linalg, 'numpy.linalg'))
   call check(ndarray_create(array, values))
   call check(tuple_create(arguments, 1))
   call check(arguments%setitem(0, array))
   call check(call_py(result, numpy, 'sum', arguments))
   call check(cast(total, result))
   call result%destroy()
   call check(call_py(result, linalg, 'norm', arguments))
   call check(cast(norm, result))
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(total) .or. .not. ieee_is_finite(norm)) error stop 'Nonfinite NumPy result'
   if (abs(total-sum(values)) > 1.0e-12_real64) error stop 'NumPy sum mismatch'
   if (abs(norm-sqrt(sum(values**2))) > 1.0e-12_real64) error stop 'NumPy norm mismatch'
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'NumPy sum:  ', total
   print '(a,f12.8)', 'NumPy norm: ', norm
   call result%destroy()
   call arguments%destroy()
   call array%destroy()
   call linalg%destroy()
   call numpy%destroy()
   call forpy_finalize()
   print '(a)', 'PASS forpy'
contains
   subroutine check(code)
      integer, intent(in) :: code
      if (code /= 0) then
         call err_print()
         print '(a,i0)', 'Forpy error: ', code
         error stop 'Python operation failed'
      end if
   end subroutine check
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: The existing generated upstream forpy_mod.F90 source is wrapped for FPM without running Fypp or changing the library. It embeds the sandbox Python 3.12 runtime using the linker flags advertised by python3-config --embed --ldflags, with an explicit runtime library search path. The consumer copies a 2-by-3 Fortran real64 array to NumPy, calls numpy.sum and numpy.linalg.norm, verifies both returned scalars independently in Fortran and checks finite values and every API status. Python references are destroyed before finalization. Other Python versions, no-copy array lifetimes, callbacks, Python extension modules and plotting are not validated. Exported projects need Python and NumPy and linker flags appropriate to the local Python installation.

! Deterministic inference from a tiny Keras-style text model; no Python needed.
program main
   use mod_kinds, only: rk
   use mod_network, only: network_type
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(network_type) :: network, restored
   real(rk) :: inputs(2,4), weights(2,3), bias(3), hidden(3), expected
   real(rk), allocatable :: prediction(:), again(:)
   integer :: unit, i, status
   weights = reshape([1.0_rk,2.0_rk, -1.0_rk,0.5_rk, 0.25_rk,-2.0_rk], [2,3])
   bias = [1.0_rk,-1.0_rk,0.5_rk]
   inputs = reshape([1.0_rk,2.0_rk, -2.0_rk,0.5_rk, 0.0_rk,0.0_rk, 3.0_rk,-1.0_rk], [2,4])
   open(newunit=unit, file='tiny-network.txt', status='replace', action='write', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'Model file open failed'
   write(unit, '(a)') '5', 'input 2', 'dense 3', 'relu 0', 'dense 1', 'linear 0', '0.01'
   write(unit, *) bias
   write(unit, *) 0.25_rk
   write(unit, *) weights
   write(unit, *) [2.0_rk,-3.0_rk,0.5_rk]
   close(unit)
   call network%load('tiny-network.txt')
   if (network%input_size /= 2 .or. network%output_size /= 1) error stop 'Network dimensions failed'
   call network%save('saved-network.txt')
   call restored%load('saved-network.txt')
   do i = 1, size(inputs,2)
      hidden = max(0.0_rk, matmul(transpose(weights), inputs(:,i)) + bias)
      expected = dot_product([2.0_rk,-3.0_rk,0.5_rk], hidden) + 0.25_rk
      prediction = network%output(inputs(:,i))
      again = restored%output(inputs(:,i))
      if (size(prediction) /= 1 .or. size(again) /= 1) error stop 'Prediction shape failed'
      if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(prediction)) .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(again))) &
         error stop 'Nonfinite prediction'
      if (abs(prediction(1)-expected) > 1.0e-12_rk) error stop 'Inference mismatch'
      if (abs(again(1)-expected) > 1.0e-12_rk) error stop 'Model save/load mismatch'
      print '(a,2f7.2,a,f10.5)', 'Input: ', inputs(:,i), '  prediction: ', prediction(1)
   end do
   open(newunit=unit, file='tiny-network.txt', status='old')
   close(unit, status='delete')
   open(newunit=unit, file='saved-network.txt', status='old')
   close(unit, status='delete')
   print '(a)', 'PASS fkb'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: The upstream CMake neural library source set is wrapped for FPM in REAL64/INT32 mode with single-image coarrays and OpenMP. The deterministic consumer writes and loads a tiny two-dense-layer ReLU network, checks four predictions against independently calculated weights and biases, and verifies saving and reloading the model. K (Approximation) describes the tested neural-network inference. Training, Keras conversion tools, dropout and batch normalization are not verified; no optimization classification is inferred from their presence.

! One MPI process. A = [5 4; 4 5] has eigenvalues 1 and 9.
program main
   use mpi, only: MPI_Init_thread, MPI_THREAD_SERIALIZED, MPI_Finalize, MPI_Comm_size, MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_SUCCESS
   use DataTypesModule, only: NTREAL
   use ProcessGridModule, only: ConstructProcessGrid, DestructProcessGrid
   use PSMatrixModule, only: Matrix_ps, ConstructEmptyMatrix, FillMatrixFromTripletList, &
      GatherMatrixTripletList, DestructMatrix
   use TripletModule, only: Triplet_r
   use TripletListModule, only: TripletList_r, ConstructTripletList, AppendToTripletList, DestructTripletList
   use SolverParametersModule, only: SolverParameters_t, ConstructSolverParameters, DestructSolverParameters
   use SquareRootSolversModule, only: SquareRoot, InverseSquareRoot
   use InverseSolversModule, only: Invert
   use ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(Matrix_ps) :: matrix, root, inverse_root, inverse
   type(TripletList_r) :: entries
   type(Triplet_r) :: entry
   type(SolverParameters_t) :: parameters
   real(NTREAL) :: a(2,2), result(2,2), expected(2,2), identity(2,2), residual
   integer :: ierr, processes, provided, i, j
   call MPI_Init_thread(MPI_THREAD_SERIALIZED, provided, ierr)
   if (ierr /= MPI_SUCCESS) error stop 'MPI initialization failed'
   if (provided < MPI_THREAD_SERIALIZED) error stop 'MPI thread support is insufficient'
   call MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, processes, ierr)
   if (ierr /= MPI_SUCCESS .or. processes /= 1) error stop 'This example uses one MPI process'
   call ConstructProcessGrid(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1, 1, 1)
   a = reshape([5.0_NTREAL,4.0_NTREAL,4.0_NTREAL,5.0_NTREAL], [2,2])
   identity = reshape([1.0_NTREAL,0.0_NTREAL,0.0_NTREAL,1.0_NTREAL], [2,2])
   call ConstructTripletList(entries)
   do j = 1, 2
      do i = 1, 2
         entry%index_row = i
         entry%index_column = j
         entry%point_value = a(i,j)
         call AppendToTripletList(entries, entry)
      end do
   end do
   call ConstructEmptyMatrix(matrix, 2)
   call FillMatrixFromTripletList(matrix, entries)
   call DestructTripletList(entries)
   call ConstructSolverParameters(parameters, converge_diff_in=1.0e-12_NTREAL, &
      threshold_in=1.0e-14_NTREAL, max_iterations_in=200, be_verbose_in=.false.)
   call SquareRoot(matrix, root, parameters)
   call extract(root, result)
   expected = reshape([2.0_NTREAL,1.0_NTREAL,1.0_NTREAL,2.0_NTREAL], [2,2])
   residual = maxval(abs(matmul(result,result)-a))
   if (maxval(abs(result-expected)) > 1.0e-9_NTREAL .or. residual > 1.0e-9_NTREAL) &
      error stop 'Matrix square root failed'
   print '(a)', 'Matrix square root:'
   do i = 1, 2
      print '(2f14.9)', result(i,:)
   end do
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Square-root residual: ', residual
   call InverseSquareRoot(matrix, inverse_root, parameters)
   call extract(inverse_root, result)
   expected = reshape([2.0_NTREAL,-1.0_NTREAL,-1.0_NTREAL,2.0_NTREAL], [2,2])/3.0_NTREAL
   residual = maxval(abs(matmul(result,matmul(a,result))-identity))
   if (maxval(abs(result-expected)) > 1.0e-9_NTREAL .or. residual > 1.0e-9_NTREAL) &
      error stop 'Inverse square root failed'
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Inverse-square-root residual: ', residual
   call Invert(matrix, inverse, parameters)
   call extract(inverse, result)
   expected = reshape([5.0_NTREAL,-4.0_NTREAL,-4.0_NTREAL,5.0_NTREAL], [2,2])/9.0_NTREAL
   residual = maxval(abs(matmul(a,result)-identity))
   if (maxval(abs(result-expected)) > 1.0e-9_NTREAL .or. residual > 1.0e-9_NTREAL) &
      error stop 'Matrix inverse failed'
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Matrix-inverse residual: ', residual
   call DestructMatrix(inverse)
   call DestructMatrix(inverse_root)
   call DestructMatrix(root)
   call DestructMatrix(matrix)
   call DestructSolverParameters(parameters)
   call DestructProcessGrid()
   call MPI_Finalize(ierr)
   if (ierr /= MPI_SUCCESS) error stop 'MPI finalization failed'
   print '(a)', 'PASS ntpoly'
contains
   subroutine extract(source, dense)
      type(Matrix_ps), intent(in) :: source
      real(NTREAL), intent(out) :: dense(2,2)
      type(TripletList_r) :: list
      integer :: k, row, column
      call GatherMatrixTripletList(source, list)
      dense = 0.0_NTREAL
      do k = 1, list%CurrentSize
         row = list%data(k)%index_row
         column = list%data(k)%index_column
         if (min(row,column) < 1 .or. max(row,column) > 2) error stop 'Matrix index out of range'
         dense(row,column) = dense(row,column) + list%data(k)%point_value
      end do
      call DestructTripletList(list)
      if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(dense))) error stop 'Nonfinite matrix entries'
   end subroutine extract
end program main

! Single-process illustration of the typed MPI wrappers; no speedup is implied.
program main
   use libmpifx_module
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(mpifx_comm) :: comm
   real(real64) :: values(3), reduced(3), expected(3)
   integer :: total, status
   call mpifx_init(error=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'MPI initialization failed'
   call comm%init(error=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'Communicator initialization failed'
   if (comm%size /= 1) error stop 'This example uses exactly one MPI process'
   expected = [1.25_real64, -2.5_real64, 4.0_real64]
   values = expected
   call mpifx_bcast(comm, values, error=status)
   if (status /= 0 .or. any(values /= expected)) error stop 'Broadcast failed'
   call mpifx_allreduce(comm, values, reduced, MPI_SUM, error=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'Array reduction failed'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(reduced))) error stop 'Nonfinite reduction'
   if (maxval(abs(reduced-expected)) > 1.0e-12_real64) error stop 'Array sum mismatch'
   call mpifx_allreduce(comm, 7, total, MPI_SUM, error=status)
   if (status /= 0 .or. total /= 7) error stop 'Integer reduction failed'
   call mpifx_allreduceip(comm, values, MPI_MAX, error=status)
   if (status /= 0 .or. any(values /= expected)) error stop 'In-place maximum failed'
   print '(a,i0)', 'MPI processes: ', comm%size
   print '(a,3f10.4)', 'Broadcast and reduced vector: ', reduced
   print '(a,i0)', 'Reduced integer: ', total
   call mpifx_finalize(error=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'MPI finalization failed'
   print '(a)', 'PASS mpifx'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: The upstream CMake library source list is generated with Fypp 3.2, with every generated file checksum locked in the recipe. The example exercises communicator initialization, real-vector broadcast, real and integer all-reduce and in-place maximum reduction on exactly one MPI process, checking API statuses and returned data. MPICH is pinned and UCX transports are limited to self/shared memory. This illustrates typed communication APIs, not parallel execution or speedup; point-to-point messaging, multiple processes and other wrappers are outside verification scope. Classification R covers the tested service routines.

! A one-process BLACS grid illustrates the API, not distributed performance.
program main
   use libscalapackfx_module
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: dp => real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(blacsgrid) :: grid
   real(dp), allocatable :: a(:,:), vectors(:,:)
   real(dp) :: original(3,3), eigenvalues(3), expected(3), identity(3,3), residual, orthogonality
   integer :: desca(DLEN_), descz(DLEN_), rank, processes, info, i
   call blacsfx_pinfo(rank, processes)
   if (processes /= 1) error stop 'This example uses exactly one MPI process'
   call grid%initgrid(1, 1)
   call scalafx_creatematrix(grid, 3, 3, 2, 2, a, desca, info=info)
   if (info /= 0) error stop 'Matrix descriptor failed'
   call scalafx_creatematrix(grid, 3, 3, 2, 2, vectors, descz, info=info)
   if (info /= 0) error stop 'Eigenvector descriptor failed'
   original = reshape([2.0_dp,1.0_dp,0.0_dp, 1.0_dp,2.0_dp,1.0_dp, 0.0_dp,1.0_dp,2.0_dp], [3,3])
   a = original
   call scalafx_psyev(a, desca, eigenvalues, vectors, descz, jobz='V', uplo='L', info=info)
   if (info /= 0) error stop 'ScaLAPACK eigensolver failed'
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(eigenvalues)) .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(vectors))) &
      error stop 'Nonfinite eigensystem'
   expected = [2.0_dp-sqrt(2.0_dp), 2.0_dp, 2.0_dp+sqrt(2.0_dp)]
   residual = 0.0_dp
   identity = 0.0_dp
   do i = 1, 3
      identity(i,i) = 1.0_dp
      residual = max(residual, maxval(abs(matmul(original,vectors(:,i))-eigenvalues(i)*vectors(:,i))))
   end do
   orthogonality = maxval(abs(matmul(transpose(vectors),vectors)-identity))
   if (maxval(abs(eigenvalues-expected)) > 1.0e-10_dp .or. residual > 1.0e-10_dp .or. &
       orthogonality > 1.0e-10_dp) error stop 'Eigensystem checks failed'
   print '(a,3f14.9)', 'Eigenvalues: ', eigenvalues
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum eigenpair residual: ', residual
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Orthogonality residual: ', orthogonality
   call grid%destruct()
   call blacsfx_exit(keepmpi=.false.)
   print '(a)', 'PASS scalapackfx'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: The upstream CMake library source list is generated with Fypp 3.2 and exact generated-output checksums. The example uses a 1-by-1 BLACS grid and pinned MPICH, ScaLAPACK and OpenBLAS native libraries. It computes eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a symmetric 3-by-3 tridiagonal matrix using scalafx_psyev, checks eigenvalues against 2-sqrt(2), 2 and 2+sqrt(2), and independently checks eigenpair residuals and orthogonality. All entries must be finite. D4a1 (ordinary real symmetric eigenproblems) applies to the tested eigensolver. This is a one-process API example, not a distributed-performance demonstration; other solvers, generalized eigenproblems and multiple processes are not verified.

! Use a file driver so the playground can display the PNG without a GUI.
program main
   use easy_plplot_m
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n = 201
   real(wp) :: x(n), sine(n), cosine(n), pi
   logical :: exists
   integer :: bytes
   pi = acos(-1.0_wp)
   x = linspace(0.0_wp, 2.0_wp*pi, n)
   sine = sin(x)
   cosine = cos(x)
   call setup(device='pngcairo', fileName='trigonometry-%n.png', figSize=[800,500])
   call figure()
   call subplot(1, 1, 1)
   call xylim([0.0_wp,2.0_wp*pi], [-1.1_wp,1.1_wp])
   call plot(x, sine, lineColor='b', lineWidth=2.0_wp)
   call plot(x, cosine, lineColor='r', lineWidth=2.0_wp)
   call ticks()
   call labels('x', 'y', 'Sine (blue) and cosine (red)')
   call show()
   inquire(file='trigonometry-1.png', exist=exists, size=bytes)
   if (.not. exists) error stop 'Plot was not created'
   if (bytes < 1000) error stop 'Plot file is unexpectedly small'
   print '(a,i0,a)', 'Created trigonometry-1.png (', bytes, ' bytes)'
   print '(a)', 'PASS easy-plplot'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: The existing upstream FPM package is compiled against pinned PLplot native libraries and the Cairo file driver. The main plots sine and cosine over [0,2*pi] using the pngcairo device, checks that the output file exists and is nontrivial, and the restricted sandbox must return a valid PNG preview for browser display. GUI devices, animation, interactive windows and other plotting routines are outside verification scope. Q describes the tested graphics functionality.

! A small configuration is created locally; no external data file is needed.
program main
   use yafyaml
   implicit none
   type(Parser) :: reader
   class(YAML_Node), allocatable :: document
   integer, allocatable :: samples(:)
   integer :: unit, rc, iterations
   logical :: enabled
   character(:), allocatable :: title
   open(newunit=unit, file='settings.yaml', status='replace', action='write')
   write(unit,'(a)') 'title: Fortran playground', 'iterations: 12', 'enabled: true', &
      'samples: [2, 3, 5, 7]', 'solver:', '  tolerance: 0.001'
   close(unit)
   reader = Parser('core')
   document = reader%load('settings.yaml')
   call document%get(iterations, 'iterations', rc=rc)
   if (rc /= YAFYAML_SUCCESS .or. iterations /= 12) error stop 'Integer setting mismatch'
   call document%get(enabled, 'enabled', rc=rc)
   if (rc /= YAFYAML_SUCCESS .or. .not. enabled) error stop 'Boolean setting mismatch'
   call document%get(title, 'title', rc=rc)
   if (rc /= YAFYAML_SUCCESS) error stop 'String setting failed'
   if (title /= 'Fortran playground') error stop 'String setting mismatch'
   call document%get(samples, 'samples', rc=rc)
   if (rc /= YAFYAML_SUCCESS) error stop 'Sequence setting failed'
   if (size(samples) /= 4) error stop 'Sequence size mismatch'
   if (any(samples /= [2,3,5,7])) error stop 'Sequence values mismatch'
   if (document%has('missing')) error stop 'Unexpected missing key'
   print '(a)', 'Title: '//title
   print '(a,i0)', 'Iterations: ', iterations
   print '(a,l1)', 'Enabled: ', enabled
   print '(a,4i4)', 'Samples: ', samples
   open(newunit=unit, file='settings.yaml', status='old')
   close(unit, status='delete')
   print '(a)', 'PASS yafyaml'
end program main

! A serial logging configuration; only WARNING and ERROR should reach the file.
program main
   use pflogger
   implicit none
   class(Logger), pointer :: log
   integer :: unit, status, count
   character(512) :: line
   open(newunit=unit, file='logging.yaml', status='replace', action='write')
   write(unit,'(a)') 'schema_version: 1', 'formatters:', '  basic:', '    class: Formatter', &
      "    format: '%(name)a~: %(levelName)a~: %(message)a'", &
      'handlers:', '  checked_file:', '    class: FileHandler', '    filename: checked.log', &
      '    formatter: basic', '    level: WARNING', 'loggers:', '  main:', &
      '    handlers: [checked_file]', '    level: DEBUG'
   close(unit)
   call initialize()
   call logging%load_file('logging.yaml', rc=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'Logging configuration failed'
   log => logging%get_logger('main')
   call log%debug('hidden-debug')
   call log%info('hidden-info')
   call log%warning('accepted-warning')
   call log%error('accepted-error')
   call logging%free()
   call finalize()
   open(newunit=unit, file='checked.log', status='old', action='read', iostat=status)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'Log file was not created'
   count = 0
   do
      read(unit,'(a)',iostat=status) line
      if (status < 0) exit
      if (status > 0) error stop 'Log file read failed'
      count = count + 1
      if (index(line,'hidden-') /= 0) error stop 'Severity filtering failed'
      if (count == 1 .and. trim(line) /= 'main: WARNING: accepted-warning') error stop 'Warning record mismatch'

      print '(a)', trim(line)

   close(unit, status='delete')

   open(newunit=unit, file='logging.yaml', status='old')
   close(unit, status='delete')
   print '(a)', 'PASS pflogger'
end program main

program main
   use flook
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(luaState), target :: state
   type(luaTbl) :: table
   integer :: status, total
   real(real64) :: answer
   character(256) :: message
   call lua_init(state)
   ! Load a Lua chunk before accessing its global tables, as in the author examples.
   call lua_run(state, code='parameters = {}', error=status, message=message)
   if (status /= 0) error stop 'Lua initialization failed'
   table = lua_table(state, 'parameters')
   call lua_set(table, 'alpha', 2.5_real64)
   call lua_set(table, 'beta', -1.0_real64)
   call lua_set(table, 'n', 6)
   call lua_close(table)
   call lua_run(state, code='results = {answer=parameters.alpha*parameters.n+parameters.beta,total=0}; '// &
      'for i=1,parameters.n do results.total=results.total+i end', error=status, message=message)
   if (status /= 0) then
      print '(a)', trim(message)
      error stop 'Lua script failed'
   end if
   table = lua_table(state, 'results')
   answer = -huge(answer)
   total = -1
   call lua_get(table, 'answer', answer)
   call lua_get(table, 'total', total)
   call lua_close(table)
   call lua_close(state)
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(answer)) error stop 'Nonfinite Lua result'
   if (abs(answer-14.0_real64) > 1.0e-12_real64 .or. total /= 21) error stop 'Lua result mismatch'
   print '(a,f8.3)', 'Lua computed alpha*n + beta: ', answer

end program main

! Headless Gnuplot contours; the PNG is returned to the playground browser.
program main
   use ogpf
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: n=61
   real(wp) :: axis(n), x(n,n), y(n,n), z(n,n)
   type(gpf) :: plot
   logical :: exists
   integer :: i, j, bytes
   axis = linspace(-3.0_wp, 3.0_wp, n)
   do j = 1, n
      do i = 1, n
         x(i,j) = axis(i)
         y(i,j) = axis(j)
      end do
   end do
   z = exp(-(x*x+y*y))
   call plot%options('set terminal pngcairo size 800,600 font "DejaVu Sans,11"')
   call plot%options('set output "gaussian.png"')
   call plot%title('Contours of exp(-(x**2 + y**2))')
   call plot%xlabel('x')
   call plot%ylabel('y')
   call plot%contour(x, y, z, lspec='with lines linewidth 2 linecolor rgb "#1565c0"')
   inquire(file='gaussian.png', exist=exists, size=bytes)
   if (.not. exists) error stop 'Contour PNG was not created'
   if (bytes < 1000) error stop 'Contour PNG is unexpectedly small'
   print '(a,i0,a)', 'Created gaussian.png (', bytes, ' bytes)'
   print '(a)', 'PASS ogpf'
end program main

! Based on the author's doc/examples/integration.f90, with independent checks.
module playground_fgsl_integrand
   use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding, only: c_double, c_ptr, c_f_pointer
   implicit none
contains
   function integrand(x, parameters) bind(c) result(y)
      real(c_double), value :: x
      type(c_ptr), value :: parameters
      real(c_double) :: y
      real(c_double), pointer :: alpha
      call c_f_pointer(parameters, alpha)
      y = log(alpha*x)/sqrt(x)
   end function integrand
end module playground_fgsl_integrand

program main
   use fgsl
   use playground_fgsl_integrand
   use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding, only: c_loc
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer(fgsl_size_t), parameter :: limit=1000
   real(fgsl_double), target :: alpha
   real(fgsl_double) :: value, estimate
   integer(fgsl_int) :: status
   type(fgsl_function) :: function
   type(fgsl_integration_workspace) :: workspace
   alpha = 1.0_fgsl_double
   function = fgsl_function_init(integrand, c_loc(alpha))
   workspace = fgsl_integration_workspace_alloc(limit)
   if (.not. fgsl_well_defined(workspace)) error stop 'Workspace allocation failed'
   status = fgsl_integration_qags(function, 0.0_fgsl_double, 1.0_fgsl_double, &
      0.0_fgsl_double, 1.0e-8_fgsl_double, limit, workspace, value, estimate)
   call fgsl_function_free(function)
   call fgsl_integration_workspace_free(workspace)
   if (status /= fgsl_success) error stop 'Adaptive integration failed'
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(value) .or. .not. ieee_is_finite(estimate)) error stop 'Nonfinite result'
   if (abs(value+4.0_fgsl_double) > 1.0e-7_fgsl_double) error stop 'Integral differs from exact -4'
   if (estimate < 0.0_fgsl_double .or. estimate > 1.0e-7_fgsl_double) error stop 'Error estimate too large'
   print '(a,f18.12)', 'Integral of log(x)/sqrt(x) on [0,1]: ', value
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Estimated absolute error: ', estimate
   print '(a)', 'Exact integral: -4; PASS fgsl'
end program main

! Argon dimer energy and forces, adapted from the author's mbd_api_tests.F90.
program main
   use mbd, only: mbd_input_t, mbd_calc_t
   use mbd_constants, only: dp, ang, MBD_LOG_LVL_ERROR
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(mbd_input_t) :: input
   type(mbd_calc_t) :: calculation
   real(dp) :: energy, gradients(3,2)
   integer :: code
   character(200) :: origin, message
   input%atom_types = ['Ar', 'Ar']
   input%coords = reshape([0.0_dp, 0.0_dp, 0.0_dp, 0.0_dp, 0.0_dp, 4.0_dp*ang], [3,2])
   input%xc = 'pbe'
   input%log_level = MBD_LOG_LVL_ERROR
   call calculation%init(input)
   call check_exception()
   call calculation%update_vdw_params_custom([11.0_dp,11.0_dp], [63.525_dp,63.525_dp], [3.55_dp,3.55_dp])
   call check_exception()
   call calculation%evaluate_vdw_method(energy)
   call check_exception()
   call calculation%get_gradients(gradients)
   call check_exception()
   call calculation%destroy()
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(energy) .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(gradients))) error stop 'Nonfinite result'
   if (abs(energy-(-2.4329456747018696e-4_dp)) > 1.0e-13_dp) error stop 'Energy differs from reference'
   if (abs(sum(abs(gradients))-2.3279742219399908e-4_dp) > 1.0e-13_dp) error stop 'Wrong gradients'
   if (maxval(abs(sum(gradients,dim=2))) > 1.0e-13_dp) error stop 'Forces are not equal and opposite'
   print '(a,es20.12)', 'Argon dimer dispersion energy (hartree): ', energy
   print '(a,es20.12)', 'Sum of absolute gradients: ', sum(abs(gradients))
   print '(a)', 'PASS libmbd'
contains
   subroutine check_exception()
      call calculation%get_exception(code, origin, message)
      if (code /= 0) then
         print '(a)', trim(origin)//': '//trim(message)
         error stop 'libMBD reported an exception'
      end if
   end subroutine check_exception
end program main

! Single-process CPU/FFTW example based on the author's 2-D complex FFT test.
program main
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64, int32, int64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   use mpi_f08
   use dtfft
   implicit none
   integer(int32), parameter :: nx=8, ny=8
   type(dtfft_plan_c2c_t) :: plan
   complex(real64), pointer :: input(:,:), output(:,:)
   complex(real64) :: expected(nx,ny)
   integer(int32) :: in_counts(2), out_counts(2), code, processes
   integer(int64) :: allocation_size
   real(real64) :: forward_error, backward_error
   call MPI_Init(code)
   call check()
   call MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, processes, code)
   call check()
   if (processes /= 1) error stop 'This example expects one MPI process'
   call plan%create([nx,ny], effort=DTFFT_ESTIMATE, executor=DTFFT_EXECUTOR_FFTW3, error_code=code)
   call check()
   call plan%get_local_sizes(in_counts=in_counts, out_counts=out_counts, &
      alloc_size=allocation_size, error_code=code)
   call check()
   if (any(in_counts /= [nx,ny])) error stop 'Unexpected local input shape'
   call plan%mem_alloc(allocation_size, input, in_counts, error_code=code)
   call check()
   call plan%mem_alloc(allocation_size, output, out_counts, error_code=code)
   call check()
   expected = cmplx(0.0_real64,0.0_real64,kind=real64)
   expected(1,1) = cmplx(1.0_real64,0.0_real64,kind=real64)
   input = expected
   call plan%execute(input, output, DTFFT_EXECUTE_FORWARD, error_code=code)
   call check()
   forward_error = maxval(abs(output-1.0_real64))
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(forward_error) .or. forward_error > 1.0e-12_real64) &
      error stop 'Impulse transform should have all coefficients equal to one'
   output = output/real(nx*ny,real64)
   call plan%execute(output, input, DTFFT_EXECUTE_BACKWARD, error_code=code)
   call check()
   backward_error = maxval(abs(input-expected))
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(backward_error) .or. backward_error > 1.0e-12_real64) &
      error stop 'Inverse transform did not recover the impulse'
   call plan%mem_free(input, code)
   call check()
   call plan%mem_free(output, code)
   call check()
   call plan%destroy(error_code=code)
   call check()
   call MPI_Finalize(code)
   call check()
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Forward FFT maximum error: ', forward_error
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Inverse FFT maximum error: ', backward_error
   print '(a)', 'PASS dtfft'
contains
   subroutine check()
      if (code /= 0) then
         print '(a,i0)', 'MPI/dtFFT error: ', code
         error stop 'Operation failed'
      end if
   end subroutine check
end program main

! Serial block-sparse multiplication, following the author's matrix examples.
program main
   use dbcsr_api
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: real64
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   type(dbcsr_type) :: a, b, c
   type(dbcsr_distribution_type) :: distribution
   integer, pointer :: row_sizes(:), col_sizes(:), rows(:), columns(:)
   real(real64), pointer :: block(:,:)
   real(real64) :: dense_a(4,4), dense_b(4,4), result(4,4), expected(4,4), residual
   integer :: i, j, r, s
   logical :: transposed, found
   allocate(row_sizes(2), col_sizes(2), rows(2), columns(2))
   row_sizes = 2
   col_sizes = 2
   rows = 0
   columns = 0
   call dbcsr_init_lib(0)
   call dbcsr_distribution_new(distribution, group=0, row_dist=rows, col_dist=columns)
   call dbcsr_create(a, 'A', distribution, dbcsr_type_no_symmetry, row_sizes, col_sizes, &
      data_type=dbcsr_type_real_8)
   call dbcsr_create(b, 'B', distribution, dbcsr_type_no_symmetry, row_sizes, col_sizes, &
      data_type=dbcsr_type_real_8)
   call dbcsr_create(c, 'C', distribution, dbcsr_type_no_symmetry, row_sizes, col_sizes, &
      data_type=dbcsr_type_real_8)
   dense_a = 0.0_real64
   dense_a(1:2,1:2) = reshape([2.0_real64,0.0_real64,1.0_real64,3.0_real64],[2,2])
   dense_a(3:4,3:4) = reshape([4.0_real64,1.0_real64,0.0_real64,5.0_real64],[2,2])
   dense_b = 0.0_real64
   dense_b(1:2,1:2) = reshape([1.0_real64,0.0_real64,0.0_real64,2.0_real64],[2,2])
   dense_b(1:2,3:4) = reshape([1.0_real64,2.0_real64,0.0_real64,1.0_real64],[2,2])
   dense_b(3:4,3:4) = reshape([3.0_real64,0.0_real64,0.0_real64,4.0_real64],[2,2])
   do j=1,2
      do i=1,2
         r=2*i-1
         s=2*j-1
         if (any(dense_a(r:r+1,s:s+1) /= 0.0_real64)) &
            call dbcsr_put_block(a, i, j, dense_a(r:r+1,s:s+1))
         if (any(dense_b(r:r+1,s:s+1) /= 0.0_real64)) &
            call dbcsr_put_block(b, i, j, dense_b(r:r+1,s:s+1))
      end do
   end do
   call dbcsr_finalize(a)
   call dbcsr_finalize(b)
   call dbcsr_finalize(c)
   call dbcsr_multiply('N', 'N', 1.0_real64, a, b, 0.0_real64, c)
   result = 0.0_real64
   do j=1,2
      do i=1,2
         call dbcsr_get_block_p(c, i, j, block, transposed, found)
         if (.not. found) cycle
         r=2*i-1
         s=2*j-1
         if (transposed) then
            result(r:r+1,s:s+1) = transpose(block)
         else
            result(r:r+1,s:s+1) = block
         end if
      end do
   end do
   expected = matmul(dense_a,dense_b)
   residual = maxval(abs(result-expected))
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(result)) .or. residual > 1.0e-12_real64) &
      error stop 'Block-sparse product differs from MATMUL'
   call dbcsr_release(a)
   call dbcsr_release(b)
   call dbcsr_release(c)
   call dbcsr_distribution_release(distribution)
   call dbcsr_finalize_lib()
   deallocate(row_sizes, col_sizes, rows, columns)
   print '(a)', 'Block-sparse matrix product:'
   do i=1,4
      print '(4f9.2)', result(i,:)
   end do
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Maximum difference from MATMUL: ', residual
   print '(a)', 'PASS dbcsr'
end program main

gams_procedures.notes: The upstream CMake-selected serial CPU library is rendered with Fypp 3.2, with exact generated-output hashes. Simple USE lists emitted from Python sets are sorted for reproducibility across Python versions and platforms; numerical algorithms are unchanged. MPI, OpenMP, GPU, LIBXS and LIBXSMM are disabled, and the library links pinned OpenBLAS. The diagnostic filename macro uses __FILE__. The checked main creates two 4-by-4 block-sparse matrices, multiplies them through dbcsr_multiply, reconstructs the result and independently compares it with MATMUL, requiring finite entries and a small maximum error. D1 covers matrix operations. Parallel scaling, accelerators and tensor operations are outside this verification scope. GPL-2.0-or-later notices are retained. The wrapper repeats the base-hooks USE list so FPM can order dependencies hidden in the original include. Its manifest permits legacy implicit external BLAS/LAPACK calls; runtime and bounds checks remain enabled.

! Small complex 3-D FFT using the library's built-in CPU backend.
program main
   use mpi
   use decomp_2d, only: decomp_2d_init, decomp_2d_finalize, decomp_log, decomp_info, alloc_x, alloc_z
   use decomp_2d_fft
   use decomp_2d_constants, only: mytype, D2D_LOG_QUIET, &
      DECOMP_2D_FFT_FORWARD, DECOMP_2D_FFT_BACKWARD, PHYSICAL_IN_X
   use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: nx=8, ny=6, nz=4
   integer :: code, processes, p_row, p_col
   type(decomp_info), pointer :: physical
   complex(mytype), allocatable :: input(:,:,:), output(:,:,:), expected(:,:,:)
   real(mytype) :: forward_error, backward_error
   call MPI_Init(code)
   if (code /= MPI_SUCCESS) error stop 'MPI initialization failed'
   call MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, processes, code)
   if (code /= MPI_SUCCESS .or. processes /= 1) error stop 'This example expects one process'
   decomp_log = D2D_LOG_QUIET
   p_row = 1
   p_col = 1
   call decomp_2d_init(nx, ny, nz, p_row, p_col, complex_pool=.true.)
   call decomp_2d_fft_init(PHYSICAL_IN_X)
   physical => decomp_2d_fft_get_ph()
   call alloc_x(input, physical, .true.)
   call alloc_z(output, physical, .true.)
   allocate(expected, mold=input)
   expected = cmplx(0.0_mytype,0.0_mytype,kind=mytype)
   expected(1,1,1) = cmplx(1.0_mytype,0.0_mytype,kind=mytype)
   input = expected
   call decomp_2d_fft_3d(input, output, DECOMP_2D_FFT_FORWARD)
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(real(output))) .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(output)))) &
      error stop 'Nonfinite forward transform'
   forward_error = maxval(abs(output-1.0_mytype))
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(forward_error) .or. forward_error > 1.0e-12_mytype) &
      error stop 'Impulse transform has incorrect Fourier coefficients'
   call decomp_2d_fft_3d(output, input, DECOMP_2D_FFT_BACKWARD)
   input = input/real(nx*ny*nz,mytype)
   if (.not. all(ieee_is_finite(real(input))) .or. .not. all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(input)))) &
      error stop 'Nonfinite inverse transform'
   backward_error = maxval(abs(input-expected))
   if (.not. ieee_is_finite(backward_error) .or. backward_error > 1.0e-12_mytype) &
      error stop 'Inverse transform did not reconstruct the input'
   deallocate(input, output, expected)
   nullify(physical)
   call decomp_2d_fft_finalize()
   call decomp_2d_finalize()
   call MPI_Finalize(code)
   if (code /= MPI_SUCCESS) error stop 'MPI finalization failed'
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Forward 3-D FFT maximum error: ', forward_error
   print '(a,es12.4)', 'Inverse 3-D FFT maximum error: ', backward_error
   print '(a)', 'PASS 2decomp-fft'
end program main

   ! y = 2*max(x1+2*x2+.5,0) - 3*max(-x1+.5*x2-.25,0) + 1
   expected = [12., -4.75, 2., 1.]
   do i = 1, 4

   end do
   print '(a)', 'PASS ennuf'

program main
use ddcosmo
! 
!      888      888  .d8888b.   .d88888b.   .d8888b.  888b     d888  .d88888b.  
!      888      888 d88P  Y88b d88P" "Y88b d88P  Y88b 8888b   d8888 d88P" "Y88b 
!      888      888 888    888 888     888 Y88b.      88888b.d88888 888     888 
!  .d88888  .d88888 888        888     888  "Y888b.   888Y88888P888 888     888 
! d88" 888 d88" 888 888        888     888     "Y88b. 888 Y888P 888 888     888 
! 888  888 888  888 888    888 888     888       "888 888  Y8P  888 888     888 
! Y88b 888 Y88b 888 Y88b  d88P Y88b. .d88P Y88b  d88P 888   "   888 Y88b. .d88P 
!  "Y88888  "Y88888  "Y8888P"   "Y88888P"   "Y8888P"  888       888  "Y88888P"  
!                                                                              
!
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
!  COPYRIGHT (C) 2015 by Filippo Lipparini, Benjamin Stamm, Paolo Gatto        !
!  Eric Cancès, Yvon Maday, Jean-Philip Piquemal, Louis Lagardère and          !
!  Benedetta Mennucci.                                                         !
!                             ALL RIGHT RESERVED.                              !
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
!
!
! A modular implementation of COSMO using a domain decomposition linear scaling
! strategy.
!
! This code is governed by the LGPL license and abiding by the rules of 
! distribution of free software.
! This program is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but  
! WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of MERCHANTABILITY 
! or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
! See the GNU Lesser General Public License for more details.
!
! Users of this code are asked to include the following references in their
! publications:
!
! [1] E. Cancès, Y. Maday, B. Stamm
!     "Domain decomposition for implicit solvation models"
!     J. Chem. Phys. 139, 054111 (2013)
!
! [2] F. Lipparini, B. Stamm, E. Cancès, Y. Maday, B. Mennucci
!     "Fast Domain Decomposition Algorithm for Continuum Solvation Models: 
!      Energy and First Derivatives"
!     J. Chem. Theory Comput. 9, 3637–3648 (2013)
!
! Also, include one of the three following reference depending on whether you
! use this code in conjunction with a QM [3], Semiempirical [4] or Classical [5]
! description of the solute:
!
! [3] F. Lipparini, G. Scalmani, L. Lagardère, B. Stamm, E. Cancès, Y. Maday,
!     J.-P. Piquemal, M. J. Frisch, B. Mennucci
!     "Quantum, classical, and hybrid QM/MM calculations in solution: General 
!      implementation of the ddCOSMO linear scaling strategy"
!     J. Chem. Phys. 141, 184108 (2014)
!     (for quantum mechanical models)
!
! [4] F. Lipparini, L. Lagardère, G. Scalmani, B. Stamm, E. Cancès, Y. Maday,
!     J.-P. Piquemal, M. J. Frisch, B. Mennucci
!     "Quantum Calculations in Solution for Large to Very Large Molecules: 
!      A New Linear Scaling QM/Continuum Approach"
!     J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 5, 953-958 (2014)
!     (for semiempirical models)
!
! [5] F. Lipparini, L. Lagardère, C. Raynaud, B. Stamm, E. Cancès, B. Mennucci
!     M. Schnieders, P. Ren, Y. Maday, J.-P. Piquemal
!     "Polarizable Molecular Dynamics in a Polarizable Continuum Solvent"
!     J. Chem. Theory Comput. 11, 623-634 (2015)
!     (for classical models, including polarizable force fields
!     
! The users of this code should also include the appropriate reference to the
! COSMO model. This distribution includes the routines to generate lebedev
! grids by D. Laikov and C. van Wuellen, as publicly available on CCL. If the routines
! are used, the following reference should also be included:
!
! [6] V.I. Lebedev, and D.N. Laikov
!     "A quadrature formula for the sphere of the 131st
!      algebraic order of accuracy"
!     Doklady Mathematics, Vol. 59, No. 3, 1999, pp. 477-481.
!
! Written by Filippo Lipparini, October 2015
!            Paolo Gatto,       December 2017
!            Filippo Lipparini, March 2018
!
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
!                                                                              !
! Sample interface with the ddcosmo module.                                    !
! This program reads the various ddcosmo parameters and the geometrical        !
! information of the molecule from a text file. The solute is described        !
! by point charges, which are also read from a file.                           !
! Finally, the van der Waals radii are also read in.                           !
!                                                                              !
! This program shows how to call the ddcosmo routines and how to initialize    !
! the various ddcosmo quantities; also, shows where the user should place      !
! his/her routines to compute the molecular electrostatic quantities.          !
!                                                                              !
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
implicit none
!
integer :: i, ii, isph, ig, n
real*8  :: tobohr, esolv
real*8, allocatable :: dummy_phi(:), dummy_glm(:,:)
real*8, parameter :: toang=0.52917721092d0, tokcal=627.509469d0
!
! quantities to be allocated by the user.
! - solute's parameters, such as coordinates, vdw radii and
!   point charges used to model the solute (or multipoles, or
!   qm density...)
!
real*8, allocatable :: x(:), y(:), z(:), rvdw(:), charge(:)
!
! - electrostatic potential phi(ncav) and psi vector psi(nylm,n)
!
real*8, allocatable :: phi(:), psi(:,:)
!
! - ddcosmo solution sigma (nylm,n) and adjoint solution s(nylm,n)
!
real*8, allocatable :: sigma(:,:), s(:,:)
!
! - forces:
!
real*8, allocatable :: fx(:,:), zeta(:), ef(:,:)
!
! - for qm solutes, fock matrix contribution.
!
! here, we read all the ddcosmo parameters from a file named Input.txt
!
interface
  subroutine mkrhs(n,charge,x,y,z,ncav,ccav,phi,nylm,psi)
    integer, intent(in) :: n,ncav,nylm
    real(8), intent(in) :: charge(n),x(n),y(n),z(n),ccav(3,ncav)
    real(8), intent(out) :: phi(ncav),psi(nylm,n)
  end subroutine
  subroutine cosmo(star,cart,phi,glm,psi,sigma,esolv)
    use ddcosmo, only: ncav,nylm,nsph
    logical, intent(in) :: star,cart
    real(8), intent(in) :: phi(ncav),glm(nylm,nsph),psi(nylm,nsph)
    real(8), intent(inout) :: sigma(nylm,nsph),esolv
  end subroutine
  subroutine forces_dd(n,phi,sigma,s,fx)
    use ddcosmo, only: ncav,nylm
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(8), intent(in) :: phi(ncav),sigma(nylm,n),s(nylm,n)
    real(8), intent(out) :: fx(3,n)
  end subroutine
  subroutine efld(nsrc,src,csrc,ntrg,ctrg,ef)
    integer, intent(in) :: nsrc,ntrg
    real(8), intent(in) :: src(nsrc),csrc(3,nsrc),ctrg(3,ntrg)
    real(8), intent(out) :: ef(3,ntrg)
  end subroutine
end interface

iprint=0; nproc=1; lmax=6; ngrid=110; iconv=7; igrad=1
eps=78.3553d0; eta=0.2d0
n=4
allocate(x(n),y(n),z(n),rvdw(n),charge(n))
charge=[0.08130d0,-0.20542d0,0.06206d0,0.06206d0]
x=0.d0; y=[0.d0,0.d0,1.76689d0,-1.76689d0]
z=[-1.16691d0,1.42202d0,-2.18736d0,-2.18736d0]
rvdw=[4.00253d0,3.63772d0,2.99956d0,2.99956d0]
tobohr = 1.0d0/toang
x    = x*tobohr
y    = y*tobohr
z    = z*tobohr
rvdw = rvdw*tobohr
!

!
! call the initialization routine. this routine allocates memory, computes some
! quantities for internal use and creates and fills an array ccav(3,ncav) with
! the coordinates of the grid points at which the user needs to compute the potential.
! ncav is the number of external grid points and nylm the number of spherical
! harmonics functions used for the expansion of the various ddcosmo quantities;
! both are computed by ddinit and defined as common variables in ddcosmo.mod.
!
call ddinit(n,x,y,z,rvdw)
!
allocate (phi(ncav),psi(nylm,n),dummy_phi(ncav),dummy_glm(nylm,n))
dummy_phi=0.d0; dummy_glm=0.d0
!
! --------------------------   modify here  --------------------------  
!
! place here your favorite routine to assemble the solute's electrostatic potential
! and the "psi" vector. Such a routine should replace "mkrhs".
! for classical solutes, assembling the psi vector is straightforward; for qm solutes
! it requires a numerical integration (similar to the one used to compute the xc 
! contributions in dft), as detaild in J. Chem. Phys. 141, 184108
! here, we compute the potential and the psi vector using the supplied routine mkrhs,
! which needs to be replaced by your routine.
!
call mkrhs(n,charge,x,y,z,ncav,ccav,phi,nylm,psi)
!
! --------------------------   end modify   --------------------------  
!
! now, call the ddcosmo solver
!
allocate (sigma(nylm,n))
!
call cosmo(.false., .true., phi, dummy_glm, psi, sigma, esolv)
!
if (iprint.ge.3) call prtsph('solution to the ddCOSMO equation',nsph,0,sigma)
!
write (6,'(1x,a,f14.6)') 'ddcosmo electrostatic solvation energy (kcal/mol):', esolv*tokcal
!
! this is all for the energy. if the forces are also required, call the solver for
! the adjoint problem. 
! the solution to the adjoint system is required also to compute the Fock matrix 
! contributions.
!
if (igrad.eq.1) then
  write(6,*)
  allocate (s(nylm,n))
  allocate (fx(3,n))
  call cosmo(.true., .false., dummy_phi, dummy_glm, psi, s, esolv)
!
  if (iprint.ge.3) call prtsph('solution to the ddCOSMO adjoint equation',nsph,0,s)
!
! now call the routine that computes the ddcosmo specific contributions to the forces.
!
  call forces_dd(n,phi,sigma,s,fx)
!
! form the "zeta" intermediate
!
  allocate (zeta(ncav))
  call ddmkzeta(s,zeta)
!
  if (iprint.ge.4) call ptcart('zeta',nsph,0,zeta)
!
! --------------------------   modify here  --------------------------  
!
! finally, add the contributions that depend on the derivatives of the potential
! on the derivatives of the potential, i.e., the electric field
! produced by the solute at the cavity points times the ddcosmo intermediate zeta 
! and the solute's potential derivatives at the cavity points times zeta. 
! the two terms are described in JCP, 141, 184108, eqs. 47, 48.
!
! for a solute represented by point charges, the two terms can be rearranged as zeta 
! contracted with the electric field of the solute plus the electric field produced
! by zeta, which have the physical dimension of a charge, at the nuclei times the 
! charges. This rearrangement allows one to use fast summations methods, such as the
! fast multipole method, for this task.
!
! a routine for point charges that follows the aformentioned strategy is provided as
! an example (efld). note that the coordinates should be packed into an array of
! dimension (3,n). we use csph, as it contains exactly this.
! the user will need to replace efld with his/her favorite routine.
!
  allocate(ef(3,max(n,ncav)))
!
! 1. solute's electric field at the cav points times zeta:
!
!   compute the electric field
!
  call efld(n,charge,csph,ncav,ccav,ef)
!
!   contract it with the zeta intermediate
!
  ii = 0
  do isph = 1, nsph
    do ig = 1, ngrid
      if (ui(ig,isph).gt.zero) then 
        ii = ii + 1
        fx(:,isph) = fx(:,isph) - zeta(ii)*ef(:,ii)
      end if
    end do
  end do
!
! 2. "zeta's" electric field at the nuclei times the charges. 
!
!   compute the "electric field"
!
  call efld(ncav,zeta,ccav,n,csph,ef)
!
!   contract it with the solute's charges.
!
  do isph = 1, nsph
    fx(:,isph) = fx(:,isph) - ef(:,isph)*charge(isph)
  end do
!
! for point charges, there is no contribution from the derivatives of the psi vector.
! for quantum mechanical solutes, such a contribution needs to be handled via a numerical
! integration.
!
! --------------------------   end modify   --------------------------  
! 
  deallocate (zeta, ef)
!
  if (iprint.ge.1) then
    write(iout,2000)
2000 format(1x,'ddCOSMO forces (atomic units):',/, &
              1x,' atom',15x,'x',15x,'y',15x,'z')
    do isph = 1, nsph
      write(6,'(1x,i5,3f16.8)') isph, fx(:,isph)
    end do
  end if
end if
!
! clean up:
!
if (.not.ieee_is_finite(esolv)) error stop 'Nonfinite energy'
if (abs(esolv*tokcal-(-0.648257d0)) > 2.d-6) error stop 'Energy differs from author reference'
if (.not.all(ieee_is_finite(fx))) error stop 'Nonfinite forces'
if (maxval(abs(fx-reshape([0.d0,0.d0,-0.00009734d0, &
    0.d0,0.d0,0.00023388d0, 0.d0,-0.00001589d0,-0.00006827d0, &
    0.d0,0.00001589d0,-0.00006827d0],[3,4]))) > 2.d-7) error stop 'Forces differ from author reference'
print '(a,es12.4)', 'Net force maximum: ',maxval(abs(sum(fx,dim=2)))
if (maxval(abs(sum(fx,dim=2))) > 1.d-7) error stop 'Forces do not sum to zero'
print '(a)', 'Energy and forces agree with author formaldehyde reference'
print '(a)', 'PASS ddpcm'

deallocate (x,y,z,rvdw,charge,phi,psi,sigma,dummy_phi,dummy_glm)
!
if (igrad.eq.1) deallocate (s,fx)
call memfree
!
end program main
